Ingredient Names: beef mince, potato, green peas, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cube the potatoes and shell the peas. Step 3: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and chopped onion and fry for 6-7 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the beef mince and ginger garlic paste and fry for 10 minutes, breaking up lumps, until all the water dries. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 6 minutes until oil appears. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add the potato and green peas and half a cup of water, cover and cook on low heat for 25 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Uncover, add green chili and garam masala and cook 3 minutes until dry. Step 8: Garnish with coriander and serve with chapati. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days; reheat on low heat with a little water.

Ingredient Names: oil, onion, minced garlic, chili flakes, turmeric, cumin seeds, coriander powder, mango powder, salt, green chilies, tomato puree, potatoes, green beans, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Preheat a pan over a high heat and add the oil. Allow to oil to warm up. Step 2: Add the finely diced onion. Sauté this over a high heat, stirring often, until the onions become translucent and limp - about 5 minutes. Step 3: Add in the minced garlic, all the spices (chilli flakes, turmeric, cumin seeds, coriander powder, mango powder, salt) and the green chillies. Mix through, then add the tomato purée. Continue to sauté this for 5 minutes. We don't want to onions to darken much - this recipe works better when the onions are lighter and are caramelised. You may need to turn the heat down to a medium flame if you find the onions are browning too much. Step 4: Add the diced potatoes. Sauté for 3-5 minutes. Step 5: Add the green beans. Sauté for 2-3 minutes. Step 6: Turn the heat down to low, cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender. Step 7: Stir in the chopped coriander and serve.

Instructions: Step 1: Combine the onion, green chili pepper, cilantro, and mint (if using) in a food processor. Use the pulse function to chop so that the onions are finely chopped but not blended. Instructions: Step 1: First, sprinkle a couple of teaspoons of salt into a bowl with the bitter melon, mix and set aside. This helps take out some of the bitter flavors. Ingredient Names: neutral oil, okra, yellow onion, garlic cloves, crushed ginger, tomatoes, sea salt or table salt, cumin seeds, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, green chili peppers, chopped cilantro, freshly squeezed lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and dry the okra. Chop the okra into 1/2-3/4 inch pieces, discarding the stems. The easiest way to do this is to line a few of them up and cut them at the same time. Sprinkle 1/4 tsp salt on the okra and mix. Set aside. Step 2: Heat a wide-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat and add the oil. Once hot, add half of the chopped okra. Stir-fry the okra, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 minutes or until the slime disappears and the okra starts to crisp and brown. I like to sprinkle a bit more salt on the okra here. Use a slotted spoon to remove the okra from the pan and set it aside. Repeat with the remaining batch. Remove the pan from heat, and wipe clean to remove any excess seeds, if needed. Step 3: Heat another 2 tbsp of oil over high heat and add the onions. Sauté until the onions turn golden, about 10 minutes. If the onions start sticking to the bottom of the pan, deglaze with a tablespoon or 2 of water. And add the garlic and ginger, if using, and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the cubed tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes soften, about 3 minutes. Stir in the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, cumin seeds and spice powders (coriander, cumin, turmeric and red chili). The oil should start separating from the masala or base of the curry. Add the fried okra and green chili pepper. Sauté for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Step 4: Reduce the heat and allow the okra to simmer for a few minutes, stirring occasionally. Garnish with cilantro and a squeeze of lemon, if desired. This dry curry is typically served with roti, naan, or other bread but can also be eaten as a side with rice.

Ingredient Names: mint leaves, loosely packed, frozen limeade concentrate, sugar, lemon juice, lime juice, ice cubes or, cold water, to
Instructions: Step 1: Add the mint leaves, frozen concentrate, sugar, lemon juice, and lime juice to a large blender. Blend until completely smooth, about 1 minute. You want to get rid of any small bits of mint as much as possible. Step 2: Add the ice and water (if making a single batch) or just ice. Taste and adjust, adding up to 1 tbsp sugar for sweetness and more lime/lemon for tang.

Ingredient Names: fennel seeds, cucumber seeds, melon seeds, sugar, water, lemon juice, ice
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the seeds overnight and grind. Step 3: Cook into a syrup with sugar and strain (bazoori syrup). The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Mix with chilled water, lemon and ice. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Serve straight away, while it is fresh.

Ingredient Names: custard apple, chilled milk, sugar, ice
Instructions: Step 1: Peel and chop the custard apple (sharifa), removing seeds. Step 2: Blend the custard apple (sharifa) with chilled milk, sugar and ice for 1 minute until smooth and frothy. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 3: Serve immediately in tall glasses.

Ingredient Names: strawberries, chilled milk, sugar, ice
Instructions: Step 1: Peel and chop the strawberries, removing seeds. Step 2: Blend the strawberries with chilled milk, sugar and ice for 1 minute until smooth and frothy. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 3: Serve immediately in tall glasses.

Ingredient Names: tea leaves, water, lemon, mint leaves, sugar
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: pick and wash the mint leaves; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Step 2: Brew light black tea and add lemon and mint; no milk. Step 3: Serve steaming hot.

Ingredient Names: watermelon, water, sugar, black salt, ice
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the watermelon and remove seeds. Step 2: Juice or blend and strain; add a little sugar and black salt to taste. Step 3: Serve fresh with ice.

Ingredient Names: milk, almonds, cashews, pistachios, melon seeds, poppy seeds, fennel seeds, black pepper, cardamom, rose petals, sugar, ice
Instructions: Step 1: Soak nuts, seeds, fennel, pepper and rose petals for 2 hours. Step 2: Grind into a fine paste with a little milk. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 3: Mix the paste into chilled milk with sugar, strain and serve with ice; a Sindhi summer cooler. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells.

Ingredient Names: milk, almonds, fennel seeds, melon seeds, black pepper, cardamom, rose petals, sugar
Instructions: Step 1: Chill the glasses and keep all the liquids cold. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 2: Grind soaked nuts and spices into paste and mix into chilled sweet milk; strain. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 3: Serve chilled immediately.

Ingredient Names: millet flour, buttermilk, salt, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Cook bajra flour in water for 20 minutes into a thin porridge and cool. Step 2: Mix with buttermilk, salt and roasted cumin and leave 2 hours; drunk in the desert heat. Step 3: Serve straight away, while it is fresh.

Ingredient Names: basil seeds, lemon juice, sugar, cold water
Instructions: Step 1: Chill the glasses and keep all the liquids cold. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 2: Soak basil seeds 20 minutes and stir into sweet lemon water. Step 3: Serve chilled immediately.

Ingredient Names: tea leaves, milk, sugar, saffron, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Brew tea with cardamom and finish with saffron soaked in warm milk. Step 2: Serve steaming hot.

Ingredient Names: flour, yeast, sugar, nigella seeds, egg, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a soft yeasted dough and rise 2 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Shape large oval naans, brush with egg and press lines with the fingers; add nigella. Step 3: Bake at 250°C for 7 minutes. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: flour, yogurt, baking powder, potato, green chili, chaat masala, fresh coriander, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead flour with yogurt and baking powder and rest 1 hour. Step 3: Fill with spiced mashed potatoes, roll and bake in a tandoor or on a tawa. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Brush with butter and serve with cholay.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, yogurt, salt, potato, green chili, cumin seeds, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mash spiced boiled potatoes. Step 3: Stuff into dough balls and roll flat. Step 4: Bake 7 minutes and brush with butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: pearl millet flour, warm water, salt, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Knead millet flour with warm water and salt for 5 minutes. Step 2: Pat into thick rotis by hand. Step 3: Cook on a hot tawa for 2-3 minutes each side and brush with ghee. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Serve with saag or gur and butter in winter.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ghee, milk, sugar, salt, sesame seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with milk, sugar and salt and rest 30 minutes. Step 2: Roll out, spread ghee, fold several times to make layers and rest 15 minutes. Step 3: Roll into small rounds, sprinkle sesame and bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until crisp. Step 4: Serve with tea or nihari.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yogurt, semolina, baking soda, sugar, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Knead a soft dough with yogurt and rest 3 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Roll oval and fry in hot oil for 1 minute until puffed; serve with cholay.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, cheese, onion, fresh coriander, green chili, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make thin breads and spread with a filling of local cheese, herbs and chili. Step 3: Cover with another bread and cook on a tawa with butter for 4 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, salt, sugar, baking powder, oil, yogurt, warm water, unsalted butter, garlic powder, chopped cilantro or parsley
Instructions: Step 1: Mix all ingredients together and keep aside. Step 2: In a mixing bowl, add all the ingredients except water. Mix well with your hand or using a stand mixer. Step 3: Gradually add the warm water and knead until you get a soft but not a sticky dough. Step 4: Knead for 5 minutes. Cover and keep aside for two hours. Step 5: Form four equal size balls from the dough. Cover and let it rest for 20 minutes. Step 6: Dust the working surface with flour and roll the first ball into an oval shape. Step 7: Do not roll it thin, a little less than 1/4 inch in thickness. Step 8: Wet the surface of the rolled dough with water, place the wet side on a hot pan. Step 9: When the bubbles appear and the surface no longer looks raw, remove the naan and place it on a baking pan. Step 10: Place the pan under the broiler, when the naan has brown patches, it’s ready, so take it out and rub with butter garlic mixture. Cover to keep the naan soft.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, water, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead wheat flour with water and salt into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Roll thin rounds. Step 3: Cook on a hot tawa for 30-40 seconds each side, then puff directly on the flame for a few seconds. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: rice flour, boiling water, salt, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Pour boiling water on rice flour and salt, cover 5 minutes and knead. Step 2: Roll gently and cook on a tawa 1-2 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 3: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, yogurt, salt, mozzarella cheese, cheddar cheese, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Stuff grated cheese into dough balls and roll. Step 3: Bake in a tandoor or hot oven for 7 minutes until the cheese melts. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, beef mince, onion, tomato, green chili, fresh coriander, black pepper, salt, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead a stiff wheat dough and rest 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Mix raw mince with onion, tomato, chili, coriander, pepper and salt. Step 4: Spread filling between two thin dough sheets and seal the edges. Step 5: Cook on a tawa with butter on low heat for 8-10 minutes each side until cooked through. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, walnuts, cottage cheese, onion, coriander, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Step 2: Make two thin rotis. Step 3: Fill with crushed walnuts, cottage cheese, onion and coriander and cook on a tawa. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Brush with butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, butter, walnuts, salt, water
Instructions: Step 1: Make thin wheat rotis on a tawa, 1 minute each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 2: Spread with melted butter and crushed walnuts. Step 3: Fold and serve warm with tea.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, yogurt, sugar, salt, garlic, butter, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Knead and rise the naan dough 2 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Shape, press chopped garlic and coriander on top. Step 4: Bake 6 minutes and brush with garlic butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, jaggery, fennel seeds, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Knead wheat flour with melted gur and fennel. Step 2: Roll thick and cook on tawa with ghee. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 3: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, yak meat mince, onion, green chili, fresh coriander, black pepper, salt, apricot oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead a stiff dough and roll two thin sheets. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Spread raw spiced mince between them and seal. Step 4: Bake in a pan or on a tawa on low heat for 20 minutes, flipping, until the meat is cooked inside. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Brush with apricot oil. Step 6: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: sprouted wheat flour, butter, apricot oil, water
Instructions: Step 1: Make a dough from sprouted wheat flour and water and rest 20 minutes. Step 2: Roll thick bread and bake on a tawa for 6 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 3: Break into pieces, soak with melted butter and apricot oil and serve hot.

Ingredient Names: jowar flour, hot water, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead jowar flour with hot water and salt. Step 2: Pat into roti between the palms. Step 3: Cook on a hot tawa 2 minutes per side and puff on the flame. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, salt, water, yeast
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a stiff dough with flour, salt, yeast and water and rest 1 hour. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Wrap the dough around a heated round stone. Step 3: Bake the stone in the embers of a fire for 20-25 minutes until a hard crust forms. Step 4: Break open and eat with sajji or rosh. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, yogurt, sugar, salt, nigella seeds, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Knead flour with yeast, yogurt, sugar and salt and rise 2 hours. Step 3: Shape and sprinkle nigella seeds. Step 4: Bake 6 minutes and brush with butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: flour, yeast, sugar, milk, ghee, sesame seeds, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with yeast, sugar, milk and salt into a soft dough and rise 2 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Shape long oval naans and press deep lines with fingers; sprinkle sesame. Step 3: Bake in a very hot tandoor or oven at 250°C for 6 minutes. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ghee, sugar, poppy seeds, salt, milk
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with ghee, sugar, salt and milk into a crumbly dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Shape small thick discs and sprinkle poppy seeds. Step 3: Bake at 190°C for 18-20 minutes; eat with noon chai. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water, sesame seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with yeast, sugar and salt and leave 2 hours to rise. Step 2: Shape thick rounds, sprinkle sesame. Step 3: Bake in a tandoor for 3-4 minutes; eaten with paye and nihari. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, flour, ghee, sugar, sesame seeds, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flours with ghee, sugar and salt into a stiff dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Roll thick, prick and sprinkle sesame. Step 3: Bake in a tandoor 6 minutes until crisp. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, ghee, salt, egg, water
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a soft dough and rest 30 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Roll thin, spread ghee, fold into many layers and roll again. Step 3: Cook on a tawa with ghee for 3 minutes each side until flaky; serve with eggs. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks.

Ingredient Names: atta flour, ghee, salt, warm water to knead the dough, extra flour to roll out the dough, oil to spread on the dough and to cook with
Instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, mix the atta with ghee, salt, and water. Rub the mixture together well. Step 2: Gradually add the water and knead until you get a smooth dough. The dough shouldn't stick to your hand or the bowl. Step 3: Cover the dough, and let it rest for at least 20 minutes, or for the best result, an hour. Step 4: Divide the dough into 4 equal size balls. Step 5: Dip the ball in the flour, then roll out the dough into a thin circle. Step 6: Spread 1 teaspoon melted butter or oil on top of the rolled-out dough, then sprinkle 3 pinches of flour. Step 7: Now start folding the rolled-out dough like a paper fan (pleating). Step 8: When done, hold the ends of the folded dough and slowly tap on your working surface while pulling it gently from both ends. This will make it longer. Step 9: Roll it up like a Swiss roll. Step 10: Coat it with flour and roll it out gently to a 6-inch round shape. Do not apply pressure, or you will lose the layers. Keep a gentle pressure when rolling out. Step 11: Heat the griddle over medium flame. Place the lachha paratha. When you see bubbles on the surface, flip it. Step 12: Spread 1 teaspoon oil over each side, and cook until both sides get golden brown spots and you see the flaky layers separating.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yogurt, baking powder, sugar, salt, milk, ghee, nigella seeds, sesame seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Knead flour with yogurt, baking powder, sugar, salt and milk into a soft dough and rest 2 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Shape into oval kulchas and sprinkle nigella and sesame seeds. Step 4: Bake in a hot tandoor or oven at 250°C for 6-8 minutes. Step 5: Brush with ghee and serve with cholay.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, white butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Cook thin rotis on a tawa and puff on the flame. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 2: Spread fresh white makhan and serve with saag or lassi.

Ingredient Names: maize flour, warm water, salt, ghee, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Mix maize flour and salt and knead with warm water little by little for 5 minutes into a soft dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Divide into balls; wet your palms and pat each ball into a thick roti between your hands or on a plastic sheet. Step 3: Place on a hot tawa and cook on medium heat for 2 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Brush with ghee and cook 1 more minute until brown spots appear. Step 5: Serve hot with butter and sarson ka saag.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, gram flour, onion, green chili, ajwain, fresh coriander, red chili powder, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead both flours with onion, chili, ajwain, herbs and spices. Step 3: Roll thick and cook on a tawa with ghee for 3 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, sugar, ghee, cardamom, fennel seeds, poppy seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Dissolve sugar in warm water and cool. Step 2: Knead flour with ghee, cardamom, fennel and the sugar water into a stiff dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Roll thick, prick and cook on a tawa on low heat for 5 minutes each side with ghee. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Serve with tea on Thadri festival.

Ingredient Names: wheat bread, dried cheese, onion, fresh coriander, mint leaves, apricot oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash and chop the fresh coriander; and pick and wash the mint leaves. Step 2: Crumble bread into a bowl. Step 3: Mix with soaked crumbled dried cheese, onion, herbs and apricot oil. Step 4: Serve as a cold-weather meal.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, water, salt, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a soft dough and roll a large thin bread. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Cook on a convex iron saj over fire for 1-2 minutes per side. Step 3: Brush with ghee. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: warm milk, yeast, oil, sugar, egg, full-fat yogurt, desiccated coconut, white sugar, nuts, dried fruit, unsalted butter, melted, cinnamon powder, cardamom powder
Instructions: Step 1: In a large mixing bowl, add the warm milk and proceed to add the yeast. Allow to set for a few minutes. Step 2: Add the oil, stir in, followed by the sugar, egg and then yogurt. Whisking in with each addition. Step 3: Gradually add in the flour 1/4 at a time, mixing with a wooden spoon. Eventually you will need to knead the flour with your hands. Add in just enough flour to get a firm dough that isn't wet to touch. Step 4: Brush with oil, cover with cling film and set aside for 2 hour to allow the dough to rise,. Step 5: As you wait for the naan dough to rise, mix together all the ingredients for the stuffing. Taste test and adjust to your liking. Step 6: Once risen, divide your dough into 8 equal balls. Work one naan at a time, flouring the surface as needed to ensure the dough doesn't stick. Step 7: Roll out one dough ball until it is about the side of your hand. Step 8: Add about 3-4 tbsp of the filling into the centre of the naan. Step 9: Bring up the sides of the naan into the centre, then flatten with your palm. The stuffing should be encased fully within the dough now. See the blog post for full pictures on how to do this. Step 10: Roll this out, careful to ensure the naan doesn't stick to the surface and that the naan doesn't tear,. Step 11: STOVE METHOD: Transfer this onto a pre-heated pan or tava on a medium high heat. Allow one side to cook for a few minutes, then flip the naan using a spatula and cook the other side. Cook as needed until both sides are spotted golden as shown in the images,OVEN METHOD: Transfer into an oven preheated at 200c for 7-8 minutes, or until gold spots appear on the Naan. Step 12: Brush with some unsalted butter or ghee and set in a warm place covered as you prepare the rest of the naan.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, salt, sugar, oil, warm water
Instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, add the flour, salt, sugar, and oil, rub the ingredients together for at least a minute. Step 2: Add water gradually and knead until you get a smooth not sticky dough. Knead for 5 minutes more. Step 3: Place the dough in a bowl and cover. Leave it at room temperature for at least 20 minutes. Step 4: Knead the dough for few seconds, you will notice that the dough is much softer in texture now. Step 5: Make 6 equal balls from the dough. If you are new to kneading and rolling out, and these happened to be your first Pulkas, then it’s better to keep the balls small in size and instead of 6 make around 8 equal balls to have more control when rolling the dough out. Step 6: Take one ball and dip it in flour, make sure the flour covers all sides of the ball. Step 7: Place the ball on working surface and flatten gently with your hand. Step 8: Roll the ball using a rolling pin starting from the middle to the edges. Try to maintain the round shape, dust with flour whenever needed. Step 9: Heat the skillet on medium-high heat which is number 4 in some stoves. Place the rolled dough on the skillet, wait for 10 seconds then flip the dough. Step 10: Cook the dough until the bottom side gets light brown patches. Remove the bread from the skillet and place the half cooked side of the bread on the high open flame. Use tongs for this step and the next. Step 11: The bread will puff up. Remove from flame and place in airtight container or on a plate but cover with a cloth to keep it moist. Step 12: Please be careful when using an open flame.

Ingredient Names: onion, thinly, crushed garlic, grated ginger, yellow fleshed potatoes roughly, achar oil or achar, salt, chili flakes, chili powder, turmeric / haldi, dhania powder / coriander powder, mustard seeds, kalonji/ nigella seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Saute the onion in a little oil on medium heat until the edges are lightly golden. Step 2: Stir in the garlic and ginger and saute for 30 seconds. Step 3: Now stir in the spices, saute for another 30 seconds. Step 4: Add the potatoes into the pot along with 3 cups of water and stir well. Step 5: Bring the potatoes to a boil and simmer on low heat until tender. Step 6: Mix well pressing gently to break up the potatoes a little, then stir in the achar/oil and adjust seasoning.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, semolina, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a stiff dough with a spoon of semolina and oil; rest 15 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Roll small rounds. Step 3: Fry in hot oil for 30-40 seconds each side until puffed. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, yogurt, salt, beef mince, onion, green chili, garam masala, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook mince with spices 15 minutes until dry. Step 3: Stuff into risen dough balls and roll flat. Step 4: Bake in a tandoor 7-8 minutes and brush with butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yeast, milk, egg, sugar, salt, ghee, sesame seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with yeast, milk, egg, sugar, salt and ghee; rise 2 hours. Step 2: Shape, brush with egg-milk and sprinkle sesame. Step 3: Bake in a tandoor or at 250°C for 6-8 minutes. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: flour, wheat flour, milk, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a very soft dough of both flours with milk and rest 1 hour. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Roll paper thin and stretch over the back of the hands. Step 3: Cook on an upturned karahi 30 seconds per side and fold like a handkerchief. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, milk, ghee, sugar, saffron, cardamom, yeast, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with warm milk, ghee, sugar, yeast and cardamom; rise 2 hours. Step 2: Shape rounds, prick, and brush with saffron milk. Step 3: Bake at 220°C for 10-12 minutes, brushing again; serve with qorma.

Ingredient Names: maize flour, wheat flour, onion, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead maize and wheat flour with chopped onion, chili, coriander, cumin and salt. Step 3: Pat into thick rotis and cook on a tawa with ghee 3 minutes per side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Serve with saag.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, milk, yogurt, egg, sugar, ghee, yeast, saffron, poppy seeds, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Knead a soft rich dough and rise 2 hours. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Shape, brush with saffron and sprinkle poppy seeds. Step 4: Bake 8-10 minutes. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, water, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead a slightly stiff wheat dough and rest 30 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Pat into thick rounds by hand. Step 3: Slap onto the tandoor wall and bake 2-3 minutes until spotted. Step 4: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: flour, yeast, yogurt, sesame seeds, nigella seeds, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Make a soft yeasted naan dough and rest 2 hours. Step 3: Shape and press sesame and nigella seeds on top. Step 4: Bake 4 minutes in a hot tandoor; brush with butter. Step 5: Keep the cooked breads wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft, and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, salt, water, ajwain, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Knead wheat flour with salt and water into a soft dough and rest for 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Knead ajwain into the dough and fold with ghee for layers. Step 3: Roll out the paratha as described. Step 4: Cook on a hot tawa for 1-2 minutes on each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 5: Spread ghee and shallow fry on medium heat for 1-2 minutes each side until golden and crisp. Step 6: Serve hot with yogurt, white butter, achaar or chai.

Ingredient Names: oil, cumin seeds, onion, to medium tomato, to medium russet potatoes, cumin powder, coriander powder, mild red chili powder, turmeric powder, salt, eggs, cilantro leaves, green chili peppers
Instructions: Step 1: Heat a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil, cumin seeds, and onions and sauté until golden, about 8 minutes. Add the tomato, potatoes, spice powders, and 3/4 tsp salt and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Step 2: Lower the heat to a little higher than the lowest setting and cover the pan with the lid. Allow the potatoes to cook for about 20 minutes, stirring a few times in between, until completely tender and well-cooked. If you feel the potatoes may stick to the bottom, add a splash of water. Step 3: Meanwhile, in a small bowl, whisk together the eggs, cilantro, green chili peppers, and ½ tsp salt. Step 4: Raise the heat to high and add the whisked eggs. Sometimes I like to drizzle in a bit of oil here, but this is optional. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2-3 minutes, or until the eggs are just cooked through.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, salt, water, potato, onion, green chili, anardana, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead wheat flour with salt and water into a soft dough and rest for 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Mash boiled potatoes with chopped onion, chili and anardana. Step 4: Take a ball of dough, open it into a cup, fill with the stuffing, seal and roll gently into a round paratha. Step 5: Cook on a hot tawa for 1-2 minutes on each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 6: Spread ghee and shallow fry on medium heat for 1-2 minutes each side until golden and crisp. Step 7: Serve hot with yogurt, white butter, achaar or chai.

Ingredient Names: mashed potato powder, salt, red chili powder, cumin, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, chopped onion, water, milk, chopped coriander, chopped mint, kneaded atta, oil/butter/ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Fill a bowl with the powdered mashed potatoes, chopped onion and all the spices. Step 2: Pour on freshly boiled water onto your powder mixture slowly, one gulp at a time, mixing with a spoon as you go along. Stop once you see the mixture is coming together somewhat but still looks slightly powdery. Step 3: Pour on warm milk, again one gulp at a time, until the mixture is soft and looks like regular mashed potatoes. You may need to get your hands involved to ensure the spices are evenly distributed. Step 4: Add the chopped coriander and optional mint. Put aside. Step 5: Using your kneaded atta, take our two equal sized small rounds of atta. Step 6: Roll them both out into equal sized circles. Step 7: Load up the aloo stuffing onto one of the rounds. You want to fill it up equally but you also need to ensure you don't overfill, otherwise it may rip during the next steps. You also want to leave some room around the edges. Step 8: Once you have placed your stuffing layer, take the other round and put it on top of the stuffing. Line up the rounds and then pinch together the sides. Step 9: Roll out until your desired size. Step 10: Place onto a pan which has been pre-heated on about a medium heat. Immediately spread a spoonful or two of oil/ghee/butter around the rim of the paratha. Flip the paratha once the colour has changed and allow the other side to change colour. Then flip again once one side has crisped up. Allow the other side to crisp up.

Ingredient Names: onion, garlic, ginger, tomatoes, hard, salt, red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder
Instructions: Step 1: In a pan, heat your oil and add the onions, garlic and ginger. Saute till golden, but ensure that the onions do not burn. Step 2: Add the tomatoes, all the spices and a splash of water. Cook on high. Step 3: Continue to cook on high, stirring continuously until the masala dries out and begins to gather in the centre. Step 4: At this point, add the hardboiled eggs and stir in. You can cut 4 shallow slits into the egg using a sharp knife to allow some of the flavour and masala to seep in. Step 5: Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, eggs, ghee, onion, green chili, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roll a paratha, cook one side and crack an egg with onion and chili on the other side. Step 3: Fold and fry in ghee until golden. Step 4: Serve hot straight from the pan with chai, yogurt or achaar.

Ingredient Names: bread, eggs, milk, sugar, cardamom powder, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk eggs with milk, sugar and cardamom. Step 2: Dip bread slices and fry in butter 2 minutes per side until golden. Step 3: Serve with chai.

Ingredient Names: vegetable oil, pinch of methi/fenugreek seeds, two small-medium sized onions, ginger paste, garlic paste, salt, red chili powder, turmeric powder, tomato, potatoes, sprig curry leaves, green chilies, cilantro, juice of, boiled eggs, additional oil
Instructions: Step 1: Take a medium sized stock pot and put it on the stove at medium-high heat. Pour in your oil; it should coat the base of the pot. If it does not then add more, remember we can get rid of it later. Step 2: When the oil is hot toss in your fenugreek seeds, let them sizzle for a minute and then add your finely chopped onions. Step 3: When the onions become lightly golden at the edges then add your garlic and ginger pastes and let it cook for another 30 seconds. Step 4: Add the dry spices and cook for another 30 seconds. Step 5: Now it is tomato time, add it in, and cook until it becomes part of the onion paste until – you guessed it – the oil rises to the top. Step 6: If you want a curry with a smooth consistency then blitz the mix in a blender now along with a little water. Or use an immersion blender, traditional method in notes. Step 7: Add your potatoes, give it a quick stir and then add two cups of hot water, the curry leaves, and the green chillies. Step 8: Bring it to a boil, then drop the heat and leave it to simmer for 15-20 minutes depending on how quickly your potatoes cook. Step 9: Now put about an inch of oil in a frying pan – preferably one for which you can locate a similarly sized lid. Heat the oil and when it is nice and hot then gingerly and from a distance put in your eggs. Spluttering will ensue. Step 10: Cover it up and let it do its thing for two minutes, then lift the lid, use tongs to rotate the eggs, cover it up and cook for another two minutes. Keep doing this until most of the surface area of the egg is golden brown. Then remove from the pan and keep aside. Step 11: Check potatoes for doneness. If you want to really intensify the flavours then turn the heat up and cook till the infamous oil rises again, add the cilantro, lemon juice, and any additional water to thin the curry out. Step 12: Add the eggs, adjust seasoning.

Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 3: Temper cumin in oil, add the dal and spices and cook 5 minutes. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 6: Serve pakwan with dal topped with onion, imli and green chutney.

Instructions: Step 1: Knead wheat flour with salt and water into a soft dough and rest for 20 minutes. Ingredient Names: wheat flour, sugar, ghee, cardamom, poppy seeds, milk
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with sugar, cardamom, poppy seeds and ghee using milk. Step 2: Roll thick and cook on a tawa slowly with ghee 4 minutes per side. Ingredient Names: leftover chapati, onion, tomato, garlic, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, fresh coriander, oil, salt

Step 4: Serve hot straight from the pan with chai, yogurt or achaar.

Ingredient Names: chicken, onion, yogurt, dried plums, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, cardamom, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes. Step 6: Add soaked aloo bukhara in the last 10 minutes for a sweet-sour taste. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: chicken, potato, cauliflower, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Step 4: Add the chicken with ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the cabbage, cover and cook for 12 minutes until soft. Step 8: Finish with garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and serve with roti. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: quail, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean and halve the quails. Step 3: Fry with ginger garlic paste for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add tomatoes and salt and cook 15 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 5: Finish with black pepper and green chili. Step 6: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, okra, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, amchoor
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and fully dry the okra, then cut into pieces and fry in a little oil for 8 minutes so it is not slimy. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the okra, cover and cook for 15 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, coconut milk, gram flour, roasted peanuts, roasted chana, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, red chili, garlic, curry leaves, basmati rice, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Grind coconut, peanuts, roasted chana and spices into a smooth paste. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 3: Cook chicken in oil with garlic for 10 minutes. Step 4: Add the paste, gram flour and water and simmer 25 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Temper with curry leaves and serve with rice and fried onion. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, black pepper, salt, ghee, ginger julienne, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat a generous amount of desi ghee in a karahi. Step 3: Add chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add halved tomatoes, cover for 5 minutes, then remove the skins. Step 5: Bhuno on high heat for 10 minutes until the tomatoes melt and ghee floats. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add crushed black pepper, green chili and salt; garnish with ginger and coriander. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken tenderloin, plain yogurt, tandoori masala powder, lemon juice, salt, ghee or butter, neutral oil, to medium yellow onion, garlic cloves, ginger, ripe tomatoes, tomato paste, serrano pepper, kashmiri chili powder or paprika, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, red chili powder or cayenne, black pepper powder, sugar, water, butter, roughly, heavy whipping cream, dried fenugreek leaves, garam masala, cilantro
Instructions: Step 1: Combine the chicken with the ingredients to marinate. Mix well and set aside. Step 2: Place the onion, garlic, and ginger in a food processor and chop very finely. Make sure the garlic and ginger is properly minced. If you'd like, you can chop the onion first and then the garlic and ginger together. Step 3: Turn Instant Pot on sauté mode. Once hot, add ghee, oil and chopped onion mixture. Step 4: Sauté for about 8-10 minutes, until the onions are golden. Meanwhile, blend the tomatoes in the food processor. If needed, deglaze the pot with 1-2 tablespoons of water to help brown the onions evenly. Step 5: Add the blended tomatoes, tomato paste (if using), Serrano pepper, spices, salt, and sugar and sauté for 6-7 minutes. Once the tomatoes have broken down well and most of the moisture has evaporated, add the water and marinated chicken. Mix well to coat the chicken and close the pressure cooker. Step 6: Cancel sauté and pressure-cook on high for 8 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 5-7 minutes. Then, manually release any remaining pressure. Step 7: Open the lid and select Sauté - More/High. Once the butter chicken is to desired consistency, cancel Sauté and add in the butter, heavy whipping cream, and dried fenugreek (if using). Taste and adjust salt and sugar. Garnish with garam masala and cilantro. Serve with naan or rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, white chickpeas, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak chickpeas overnight and boil 40 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt and all the powdered spices and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add water, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the chicken is nearly tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the white chickpeas with enough water and simmer for 20-25 minutes until it is soft and the gravy is thick. Step 8: Temper with cumin fried in a little oil, add garam masala, green chili and coriander and serve hot. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, salt, black pepper, lemon, mutton fat
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the chicken into large pieces and season with salt only. Step 2: Thread on skewers alternating with small pieces of fat. Step 3: Grill over coals for 15 minutes, turning. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 4: Sprinkle black pepper and squeeze lemon. Step 5: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken wings, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, chaat masala, lemon juice, cornflour, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, lemon juice and salt and marinate the wings for 2 hours. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Coat the wings in cornflour. Step 4: Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 10 minutes until crisp and cooked through. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Toss with chaat masala and lemon while hot and serve with ketchup or chutney. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, yogurt, tomato, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, lemon juice, mustard oil, onion, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the boneless chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add a little water, cover and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add tomatoes, yogurt and crushed achaar spices and cook 10 minutes. Step 6: Cook uncovered for 3 minutes until thick, sprinkle garam masala and coriander. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 7: Serve in the handi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, tomato, ginger garlic paste, yogurt, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, lemon juice, green chili, mustard oil, oil, salt, fresh coriander

Ingredient Names: oil for cooking, onion, yogurt, salt, cumin seed powder, red chili powder, ginger garlic paste, crushed black pepper, garam masala powder, raw papaya paste, roasted poppy seeds, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and pat your chicken dry. Add cuts along the lengths of your chicken pieces. Step 2: Add all the ingredients of the marinade to a blender. Make a smooth paste. Step 5: On a BBQ grill - This is pretty straightforward. You fire up your grill and grill on both sides till it's nice and charred. Step 6: Pan frying. Pan fry the pieces on a grill pan at high heat on both sides for about 4 mins each. Then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pan and let it cook for another 10 minutes. You can smoke coal at this point if you like. Step 7: Baking and air frying- Preheat oven to 180 ℃ or 375 ℉. Grease a pan with oil or butter and place your chicken pieces on it. Coat the chicken with oil as well. Bake for 20 mins, 10 mins on each side. You can glaze the pieces with oil or leftover marinade when you flip them over. Broil for 1 minute towards the end for a nice charred finish. You can smoke it with coal at this point if you like. Step 8: Serve with some extra lemon slices to squeeze on top, onion slices and mint chutney.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, black pepper, onion, capsicum, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornflour, egg, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add soy and oyster sauce, a full tablespoon of crushed black pepper and water; thicken with cornflour. Step 5: Toss in the chicken and serve. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, cashews, capsicum, onion, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce, dried red chilies, cornflour, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes; and slice the nuts for garnish. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 5: Add chicken and cashews and toss. Ingredient Names: chicken mince, onion, tomato, maize flour, egg, anardana, crushed coriander seeds, red chili flakes, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix the chicken mince with chopped onion, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, chili flakes, egg, maize flour and salt. Step 3: Rest the mixture 30 minutes. Step 4: Shape into large thin round patties and press a tomato slice into each. Step 5: Shallow fry in hot fat for 4-5 minutes each side until the edges are crisp. Step 6: Serve with naan and yogurt chutney. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, distilled white vinegar, kosher salt, quarts water, plain, whole-milk greek yogurt, lemon juice, crushed garlic, crushed ginger, coriander powder, cumin powder, kashmiri chili powder, red chili flakes, garam masala, red chili powder or cayenne, carom seeds, russet potatoes, red onion, salted butter, chaat masala, lemon wedges, vegetable raita or mint raita, thinly
Instructions: Step 1: Prepare chicken: Rinse chicken inside out thoroughly. If you're not brining, drain and pat dry. Make 3-5 slanted cuts (about 1” deep) into the breasts, and 2-3 cuts into the legs, trying not to get to the bone. Then turn over and make a few slits on the less meaty side. (Bonus points if you can get your butcher to do this.). Step 2: Optional - Brine: In a large bowl, dissolve the salt and vinegar in 3 quarts (12 cups) water. (Keep stirring until salt is completely dissolved.) Submerge the chicken in the water. Cover and allow to sit on the counter for at least 30 minutes, up to 2 hours. If brining longer (up to overnight), place in the fridge. Remove the chicken from the brine and drain the water. Pat the chicken dry to prevent diluting the marinade. Step 3: Marinate: Combine all the ingredients listed under 'Marinade' in a medium bowl. Coat the chicken with the marinade, making sure to get in the cuts and crevices (I use kitchen gloves to do this). Stuff any leftover marinade into the cavity and place it breast side-down (this helps keep the chicken legs intact.) Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, up to 48 hours (the longer the better!). Step 4: Preheat oven: When ready to prepare the chicken, take it out of the fridge and allow it to come closer to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 325°F/165°C. Step 5: Roast/Steam: Place the potatoes and onion wedges in a deep, oven-safe roasting pan. Place the chicken breast side up and brush the remaining thick marinade over it (discard any liquidy marinade). Tie the legs using twine or an oven-safe silicone band. Drizzle 2 tbsp of oil on top of the chicken and vegetables. Cover the pot with a lid or seal with aluminum foil to create steam (dum). Roast for 60-70 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender (165+°F Internal temperature). Remove from the oven and allow to rest for 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle. Step 6: Pan-Fry Chicken: Heat the remaining 1/4 cup oil and butter (if using) in a large nonstick pan over med-high heat. Using your hands or tongs and wooden spoon, gently lift the whole chicken and place it in the oil. Cook the chicken for 3 minutes, breast side up. Tilt the pan and use a ladle to scoop the oil and pour it on the top and sides of the chicken. Carefully turn over the chicken and pan-fry the bottom, breast side down, until lightly golden and seared, 2-3 minutes. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of the chaat masala over the chicken. Using tongs to grab the sides, carefully lift the chicken and place it on a serving tray, breast side up. Sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 tsp of chaat masala. Step 7: Pan-fry Vegetables: Next, use a slotted spoon or tongs to transfer the potatoes and onions to the frying pan. Pan-fry for 2-3 minutes, until lightly charred. Discard the leftover roasting liquid/pan juices, or reduce it in the same pan to serve alongside. Serve with the potatoes and red onions (roasted and/or fresh), lemon wedges, and Vegetable Raita or Mint Raita.

Ingredient Names: chicken mince, of a bunch of a cilantro pack, mint leaves, indian red chilies, green chilies, onion, garlic, paprika, blackpepper powder, garam masala powder, salt, breadcrumbs, egg, shredded sharp cheddar cheese, cooking oil for coating and grilling
Instructions: Step 1: Making kebab mixture. Step 2: In a food processor, add cilantro, mint leaves, onion, garlic, red and green chilies. Process until they are finely chopped. Step 3: Wear a glove and squeeze all the liquid out of the chopped mix. You can also use a nutmilk bag or a cheese cloth to do this. Discard the liquid. Step 4: In a bowl, add the chopped mixture and all the remaining ingredients except oil and cheese. Mix or knead to make a uniform kebab mixture. Step 5: Add cheese at the end and mix until fully combined. Step 6: Shaping the Kebabs. Step 7: To divide the mixture into equal portions, use an icecream scooper or a tablespoon. Place each scoop of mixture on a plate. Step 8: Put the plate in the freezer for 15 mins and then take it out for shaping. Step 9: Pour 3 to 4 tablespoon oil in a cup and use some to grease the palm of your hands. Step 10: Take a portion of mixture and use the palm of your hands to roll it into a rough cigar shape. Step 11: Insert a thick skewer (or straw or wooden bbq stick) through one tip of the cigar and bring out on the other side. Step 12: Use the palm of your hands to perfect the shape of the cigars. Step 13: Carefully remove the kabab from the skewer by sliding the skewer out and placing the kabab back on the tray. Step 14: IF you want to cook the kababs with the skewers then leave the skewers intact. Step 15: Cooking the KababsOn the Stove (Gas or Electric). Step 16: For pan frying, place a large nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium heat on the stove. You can also use a grill pan. Step 17: Add oil to cover the base of the skillet. Step 18: When oil becomes hot (3 to 4 mins), add kababs to the pan without overcrowding it. Step 19: Use a straight spatula or tongs to turn the kababs frequently, allowing all sides to turn golden brown evenly. Step 20: Cook for a total of 5 mins. Step 21: Transfer kababs to your serving dish once they are done. Step 22: Line the airfryer tray with parchment paper. Step 23: Place kebabs in a single layer and use cooking spray grease them. Step 24: Air-fry at 200 C (400 F) for 3 mins. Step 25: Then flip the kebabs and cook for another 3 mins, oven-Baked. Step 26: Preheat the oven to 200 C (395 F). Step 27: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper, greased with butter or oil. Step 28: Place the kabab on the pan and place it in the middle rack of the oven. Turn on the top heat (broiler) on High (550°F/287°C). Step 29: Bake for a total of 8 mins, flipping the kababs at 5 min mark.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, cornflour, egg, green chili, capsicum, onion, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the chicken into cubes, coat with egg, cornflour and salt and fry 5 minutes until crisp. Step 3: Stir fry garlic, slit green chilies, capsicum and onion on high heat for 2 minutes. Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, green chili, capsicum, onion, garlic, soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, cornflour, egg, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the chicken into strips, coat with egg, cornflour and salt and fry 4 minutes. Step 3: Stir fry garlic, onion, capsicum and lots of slit green chilies on high heat for 2 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar and 1.5 cups water and boil. Step 5: Thicken lightly with cornflour slurry. Step 6: Add the chicken and simmer 2 minutes; serve with egg fried rice. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken breast or thighs, chow mein stir-fry noodles - see note, garlic cloves, fresh ginger, green onions, green cabbage, carrot, red onion, bell pepper, cored, halved widthwise and, sea salt, low-sodium vegetable stock, lime wedges, cornstarch, soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, chili garlic sauce, sugar, toasted sesame oil, black pepper, red chili flakes, ground white pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Place all ingredients listed under ‘Hakka Noodles Sauce’ in a medium bowl and whisk to combine. Step 2: Pour 2 tbsp of sauce over the chicken and toss to marinate. Set aside while you prepare the noodles. Step 3: Prepare noodles according to packet instructions. Use a tong to toss with 1 tsp of the oil to prevent them from sticking. Step 4: Heat remaining 2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick wok or fry pan over high heat. Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 10-15 seconds, until golden and starting to brown. Add the chicken and stir-fry until the color changes from pink to pale, 1-2 minutes. Stir in the veggies (green onions, cabbage, carrot, onion, and bell peppers). Sprinkle in ¼ tsp sea salt. Stir-fry for 5 minutes, until the cabbage is wilted and the vegetables are tender. Step 5: Add the noodles, sauce, and vegetable stock. Using tongs or two wooden spoons, toss everything together until combined and the sauce has dried up, 2-3 minutes. Garnish with green parts of onion and serve immediately. I like to serve with lime wedges, chili garlic, or ketchup.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, yogurt, tomato, red chili powder, cumin seeds, onion, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a clay handi or heavy pot and fry chopped onion for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the boneless chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add a little water, cover and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add a lot of whisked yogurt and cook on low heat for 10 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 6: Cook uncovered for 3 minutes until thick, sprinkle garam masala and coriander. Step 7: Serve in the handi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: oil, onions, garlic, minced ginger, cumin seeds, black cardamom pods, finger-sized piece whole cinnamon, red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, salt, tomato puree, chicken, skin-off and, fresh coriander, to garnish
Instructions: Step 1: Heat the oil in a pot. Once hot, add the finely sliced onions, garlic, ginger, black cardamom, cumin seeds and cinnamon stick. Fry this over a medium-high heat till the onions turn a light shade of golden. Step 2: Turn the heat to high and add the chicken pieces and tomato puree and the rest of the spices. Once the chicken is no longer pink and coated in the masala, add 1/2 cup (125ml) water. Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer. Step 3: After 15-20 minutes of simmering on low, the chicken should be nearly done. At this point, uncover and add the diced onion pieces. Cover again and cook for 7 -10 minutes. Step 4: Take the lid off and have a look at how the sauce in the curry is looking. If you'd like to thicken the sauce, cook it for a further few minutes over a medium to high heat, until the thickness is too your liking.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, cornflour, egg white, capsicum, spring onion, sugar, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Coat chicken strips in egg white, cornflour and salt and fry 4 minutes. Step 3: Fry lots of chopped garlic in oil for 1 minute. Step 4: Add soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, sugar and 1 cup water and bring to a boil; thicken with cornflour slurry. Step 5: Add chicken, capsicum and spring onion and cook 2 minutes; serve with egg fried rice. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, garlic, yogurt, red chili flakes, lemon juice, butter, salt, oil, onion, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless chicken into bite-size pieces. Step 3: Marinate in yogurt with a full head of crushed garlic, chili flakes and lemon for 3 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 4: Thread on skewers. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 15 minutes, turning and basting with butter or oil, until cooked and lightly charred; or cook on a hot tawa. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Give a smoke of hot coal for 2 minutes for the BBQ aroma. Step 7: Serve with onion rings, lemon, mint chutney and naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken mince, raw papaya paste, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, fried onion, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix the chicken mince with papaya paste, ginger garlic paste, crushed fried onion, red chili, garam masala and salt. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Rest for 1 hour. Step 4: With wet hands, wrap the mixture around skewers into long soft rolls. Step 5: Grill over coals for 10 minutes, turning and basting with butter. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Give a coal smoke and serve with paratha. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, wheat, barley, chana dal, masoor dal, moong dal, basmati rice, onion, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, ghee, fried onion, ginger julienne, lemon, mint leaves, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; pick and wash the mint leaves; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the grains overnight and the dals 2 hours; boil with turmeric for 2 hours until mushy and blend. Step 3: Cook chicken with onion and spices in ghee for 15 minutes, add water and cook 40 minutes; shred. Step 4: Mix chicken and grains and beat on low heat for 20 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Finish with tarka and garnish with fried onion, ginger, mint and lemon. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 6: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, onion, ginger paste, garlic paste, tomatoes, red chili powder, salt, soy sauce, diced green pepper, freshly cracked black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Heat 3-4 tbsp of oil in a wok or saucepan with a lid. Step 2: Add the onions and saute on medium heat until the edges start to change colour. Instructions: Step 1: Marinate chicken with vinegar, mustard, garlic, peppers and salt for 2 hours. Ingredient Names: ground chicken, kalonji/ nigella seeds, ground garlic, ground ginger, to matoes, salt, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala powder, green chilies, handful of, a squeeze of lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: - Heat oil in a wok and add the nigella seeds. Step 2: - When they start to splutter then add the minced/ground ginger and garlic.
