Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat butter and fry the chicken with salt on high heat for 10 minutes. Step 3: Add chopped tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until they melt. Step 4: Add whisked yogurt and cook 5 minutes until the gravy is creamy. Step 5: Add lots of crushed black pepper, ginger julienne and green chilies. Step 6: Serve with naan, Peshawar style. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken mince, onion, green chili, ginger garlic paste, fresh coriander, bread crumbs, garam masala, salt, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mince the chicken mince twice for a smooth texture. Step 3: Finely chop the onion and squeeze out all its water in a cloth. Step 4: Mix everything well and knead for 5 minutes, then chill for 1 hour so it holds on the skewer. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Wet your hands and press the mixture around flat skewers. Step 6: Grill over glowing coals for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes and brushing with butter or fat. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 7: Serve with paratha, onion rings, lemon and green chutney. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken thighs, boneless chicken breast, chana dal, ginger, garlic, diced onion, water, black cardamom, green cardamom pods, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, small cinnamon stick, salt, chili flakes, cilantro, mint, green chilies, onion
Instructions: Step 1: Grind all the Masalas in the Garam Masala section and set aside. Step 2: Run your ginger, garlic and onion from the first section through a food processor/ chopper or finely dice by hand. Step 3: Combine all the ingredients except the Hara Masala ones in the Instant Pot along with half a cup water and give it a mix. Step 4: Close the lid, set to seal and set to pressure for 25 Minutes then natural release (that means turn the machine off and walk away till the pressure releases, then open the valve.). Step 5: Now put the Instant pot on saute mode and saute until the excess moisture dries out and the meat mix begins to stick to the bottom. Step 6: Combine all the ingredients EXCEPT the green masala ones in a pot with 2 cups of water, bring to a boil and simmer on low for 45 minutes or until the daal is completely tender. You want it to essentially dissolve with a little pressure. Step 7: Crank up the heat, dry up excess water, your meat mixture should start to stick. Set aside to cool a little. Step 8: Now finely mince or use a food processor to chop the green masala ingredients. Step 9: Decision time: for a smooth kabab run the entire meat mix through a food processor (in batches or one go) OR run half of it through a food processor and mix it into the original kabab mix. This gives you a more fulsome kabab (my preference). Step 10: Stir in ALL the hara masala, feel free to sneak a taste! Step 11: Wet your palms and shape the kababs to your preferred size. Step 12: FRY A TEST KABAB! Adjust seasoning but do remember that fresh kababs are about 20% more assertive than their frozen counterparts. Step 13: Line a tray with parchment paper/plastic wrap and place your kababs on it as you shape them. Place the tray in the freezer and once the kababs are frozen then you can transfer them to a freezer safe container or bag. They will keep well for up to six months. Step 14: To fry: defrost on the counter or in the fridge or microwave and then shallow fry on medium high heat for about 1.5 minute per side.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, capsicum, onion, tomato, ketchup, chili sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, black pepper, oil, salt, egg fried rice
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Marinate chicken cubes with soy, vinegar, pepper and salt for 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Thread with onion, capsicum and tomato and pan fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Pour over a sauce of ketchup, chili sauce and soy cooked for 3 minutes. Step 5: Serve on egg fried rice. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, capsicum, onion, tomato, soy sauce, chili sauce, black pepper, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless chicken into pieces (or make deep cuts in larger pieces). Step 3: Mix all the marinade ingredients and rub well into the meat. Step 4: Marinate for 4 hours in the fridge. Step 6: Grill over hot coals for 15-20 minutes, turning and basting with oil, until charred at the edges. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 7: Give a coal smoke (dhuwan) for 2 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and serve with naan and raita. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, capsicum, onion, tomato, tomato ketchup, chili sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, rice, butter, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes; and wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Step 5: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken mince, chana dal, yogurt, onion, mint leaves, green chili, garam masala, eggs, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak chana dal 1 hour. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Boil the chicken mince and dal with spices until dry and grind smooth. Step 4: Mix hung yogurt with chopped onion, mint and green chili. Step 5: Stuff a little filling inside each kebab and seal. Step 6: Dip in egg and shallow fry 3 minutes per side. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, tomato, dumba fat, green chili, black pepper, ginger, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil and fat in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the chicken and fry for 8 minutes until sealed. Step 4: Cover and cook on medium heat for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Cook only with dumba fat, tomatoes and salt for 10 minutes, then add black pepper and green chili. Step 6: Keep cooking on high heat, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until the masala coats the meat and oil floats. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander, ginger julienne and green chili and serve straight from the karahi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, potato, carrot, onion, garlic, ginger, black pepper, whole spices, flour, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry onion in butter for 5 minutes, add chicken, ginger and garlic and fry 5 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add whole spices, potato and carrot chunks and 4 cups of water and simmer 25 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Mix flour in a little water and stir in to thicken, cook 5 minutes. Step 5: Season with black pepper and serve with bread or rice. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: garlic powder or garlic paste, paprika, crushed red chili flakes, blackpepper powder, chaat masala, salt or, tomato paste, white vinegar or lemon juice, boneless chicken breast, red onion, bellpeppers, cooking oil or any neutral oil of your choice, serrano green chilies slit open into halves
Instructions: Step 1: STOVE COOKING METHOD. Step 2: Marinate chicken cubes with all the ingredients in the "chicken marinade". Set aside for atleast 15 mins. Step 3: Heat a large skillet/grill pan/ frying pan of your choice at medium high heat on the stove. Step 4: Add oil and green chilies. Allow green chilies to change color slightly, takes around 1 mins. Step 5: Add marinated chicken, spread out evenly around the pan and leave for 2 to 3 mins without touching or sauteeing. Step 6: After 3 mins, when chicken forms a nice sear on one side, start sauteeing for another 2 mins or until chicken looks golden from all sides. Step 7: Add peppers and onions. Saute for another 2 to 3 mins or until you reach the desired color of the vegetables you prefer. For a slight char on the edges, 2 to 3 mins is enough. Step 8: Turn off flame and adjust seasoning according to your liking. At this stage you can add more lemon juice or chat masala if you like. You can also garnish with more chopped cilantro if you want. Step 9: Serve as is, or with a side of yellow rice and plain yogurt, or tortillas or baked potatoes. Step 10: OVEN BAKED STIR FRY. Step 11: Marinate chicken and vegetables together by mixing all the ingredients together in a giant bowl, including oil and green chilies. Step 12: Allow marination for 15 to 20 mins, or overnight if you like. Step 13: Preheat oven at 200°C (390°F). Step 14: Line a large baking tray with parchment paper and spray with cooking oil. Place the marinated chicken and vegetables on top and spray with a little oil. Step 15: Bake for a total of 15 to 20 mins, tossing the chicken and veggies once at the 10 min mark. Step 16: You can also broil for a min towards the end of the baking.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, pineapple, capsicum, onion, tomato ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, cornflour, egg, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Step 2: Batter chicken with egg and cornflour and fry 5 minutes until crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Step 4: Add pineapple, capsicum and onion cubes for 2 minutes, then the chicken; serve at once. Step 5: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless skinless chicken breast, garlic, ginger, kosher salt, freshly squeezed lemon juice, neutral oil, tomato ketchup, classic yellow mustard, ground black pepper, eggs, black pepper, white sandwich bread, mayonnaise, romaine lettuce leaves, cucumber, salad tomato
Instructions: Step 1: Place the chicken in a bowl. Add the Chicken Tikka Masala powder, garlic, ginger, salt, and lemon juice and toss to coat evenly. Step 2: Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and spread all over the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until just cooked through, about 6 minutes. (It’ll start to release moisture, then cook in its own liquid). Step 3: Add ketchup, mustard, and black pepper. Stir and cook for another 2 minutes until well combined and slightly thickened. (You don’t want it completely dry - it should still have a bit of sauciness.). Step 4: Remove from heat. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding salt to taste, pepper for spice, ketchup for sweetness, and lemon for tang. Step 5: Crack the eggs into a small bowl and season with salt and black pepper. Step 6: Heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Pour in the eggs; they should sizzle immediately. Allow the eggs to set for 1-2 minutes, tilting the pan and moving the uncooked egg to the outer rims for even thickness. Step 7: Divide into two portions and flip once the bottom is golden brown. Cook for another minute until set but still glossy on top. Cut the egg into 5 pieces (1 piece per sandwich). Step 8: Heat a panini grill or stovetop cast iron grill pan over high heat (no oil needed). Once smoking hot (it takes ~8 minutes for my pan to heat up), place 1-2 slices of bread in the middle and grill for 7-10 seconds, undisturbed. (If yours can fit more while grilling evenly, feel free to add more.) Gently press down to deepen grill marks. You want the grill marks close to blackened for more flavor and aroma. Use tongs to flip and grill the other side. Repeat for the remaining 14 slices (top and bottom slices of sandwiches). Step 9: Line up the slices of bread (I stack them in 3 so it's easier to keep track). Spread mayonnaise on one side of each of the 5 (or 6) base/bottom slices. Step 10: Place about 1/3-1/2 cup (45-70g - depending on the width of your bread) of the cooked chicken mixture onto each base slice. Step 11: Thinly spread mayonnaise on one side of the middle slices, then place them mayo-side down onto the chicken. Step 12: Top with romaine lettuce, two cucumber slices (placed at an angle so each half of the club sandwich gets one), tomato slices, and prepared eggs. Step 13: Spread mayonnaise on one side of the remaining top slices, then press them mayo-side down to complete the sandwiches. Step 14: Secure with toothpicks. Using a sharp knife, cut each sandwich diagonally into triangles.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, yogurt, tikka masala, tomato, onion, cream, butter, ginger garlic paste, kashmiri chili, garam masala, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the chicken into cubes and marinate in yogurt and tikka masala for 2 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 2: Grill or pan-roast the chicken for 12 minutes until charred at the edges. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 3: Melt butter and cook chopped onion, tomato and ginger garlic paste for 12 minutes; blend smooth. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Return the sauce to the pan with kashmiri chili and salt and simmer 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add the grilled chicken and cream and simmer 8 minutes. Step 6: Sprinkle garam masala and serve with naan. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken mince, rolled oats, bread crumbs, black pepper powder, cumin seeds or zeera, crushed red chili, salt, white pepper, bell pepper, big onion, carrot, coriander leaves, or, garlic, ginger, egg, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Start by adding carrot, bell pepper, onion, garlic, ginger in a chopper and chop coarsely. Step 2: In a bowl, add minced chicken, oats, chopped vegetables, spices, seasonings, egg and bread crumbs. Step 3: Mix all the ingredients and cover it. Leave it for 5 to 10 minutes. Step 4: Drop heaped tablespoons of the mixture onto plate or a tray to make patty portions. Step 5: Heat up the grill pan at medium heat with oil in it. Step 6: Grease the palms of your hands with oil and use it to flatten the kabab portions into flat patties. Step 7: Drop the kebab patties in the grill pan. Grill for 3 minutes and flip. Grill until golden and remove. Step 8: Serve hot with chutney or sliders on the side.

Ingredient Names: chicken, yogurt, cream, ginger garlic paste, green chili, white pepper, black pepper, cumin powder, lemon juice, butter, oil, salt, fresh coriander

Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 6: Keep cooking on high heat, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until the masala coats the meat and oil floats. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the dal 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Step 3: Boil with 3-4 cups water, turmeric, red chili, ginger and salt, skimming the foam, for 20 minutes until soft. Step 4: Cook the chicken in the masala for 20 minutes, then add the boiled dal and simmer 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Fry sliced garlic, cumin seeds and dried red chilies in ghee for 1-2 minutes until the garlic is golden (tarka/baghaar). Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 6: Add chopped onion and tomato to the tarka and cook 3 minutes if you like a thicker dal. Step 7: Pour the sizzling tarka over the dal, add green chili and fresh coriander. Step 8: Serve with plain rice or roti, achaar and salad. Ingredient Names: desi chicken, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, oil, salt

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, cornflour, egg, capsicum, onion, garlic, chili sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, red chili flakes, oil, salt

Ingredient Names: whole chicken, yogurt, fried onion, cashews, cream, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, green cardamom, saffron, ghee, salt

Ingredient Names: garlic, fresh coriander, fresh mint, yogurt, green chilies for a spicy kick, white vinegar, oil, boneless chicken, salt, coarsely

Ingredient Names: chicken, skin removed, lemon juice, salt, mustard powder, black pepper, potatoes, oil for cooking
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk all the marinade ingredients together, mix well and taste. It should be tart, salty, with the assertive warmth of the mustard and a little sharpness from black pepper. If you can't taste any of the elements then adjust the seasoning. Step 2: Take a fork and pierce holes into the chicken all over, these holes will allow flavour in but disappear once the chicken is cooked. Step 3: Place the chicken in a bowl and pour the marinade over, using your hands (gloves or not, upto you) to make sure the marinade works its way in. Leave it in the fridge covered and breast side down for a few hours. Step 4: After a few hours flip it over and rub the marinade in once more till ready to cook. I suggest marinating for at least 6 hours, but prefer overnight. Step 5: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes to an hour before cooking - it will cook more evenly when it is not cold. Step 6: Heat a generous lug of oil (about 1/4 cup) in a pot large enough to hold your chicken and veggies on medium high heat. Step 7: When the oil starts to shimmer carefully put the chicken in on it's back for 2-3 minutes, it will splutter so be careful! Step 8: When the back takes on a lovely gold brown then move the chicken on to one side (leg) to get that lovely colour on each side and then finally the breasts. If your oil is hot it takes about 3 minutes to get colour. If the chicken sticks then that means it is not cooked enough yet. Step 9: You can do this with your hands or with a tong, it is up to you, but building a little colour at this stage is absolutely key for flavour! Step 10: When the chicken breasts are beautifully browned then add your veggies to the pot along with a pinch of salt, and half a cup of water. Let them fall to the side of the chicken. Step 11: Bring to a boil then simmer tightly covered for 25-30 minutes. Step 12: The chicken should look well cooked through and the potatoes done. Test a potato for doneness and seasoning. If it tastes bland your chicken may too so in that case turn the chicken over, add a little sprinkle of salt and let it steam for another few minutes. Step 13: Serve hot with crusty bread.

Ingredient Names: oil, garlic, ginger, boneless chicken chunks, tomatoes, double cream, salt, red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, pods green cardamom, coriander, green chili
Instructions: Step 1: Heat up oil in a pan. Add the minced garlic and ginger and sauté for 1-2 minutes on high, till they are golden. Step 2: Add the chicken pieces and cardamom pods. Continue to sauté this on high heat till the chicken is no longer pink and is lightly browning, about 5 minutes. Step 3: Add the chopped tomatoes and all the spices. Continue to stir on high heat. The tomatoes will release a lot of their moisture, but you must continue to stir. Step 4: Continue to sauté till all the moisture has dried out and the tomatoes cling to the chunks of chicken, as shown below. Step 5: At this point, add the double cream. Once again, sauté this till it dries down till how it looked like in step 4. Step 6: Garnish with coriander, green chilli, long strips of ginger and a drizzle of cream.

Instructions: Step 1: In a chopper, add green chilies, onions, garlic and ginger. Chop finely. Step 2: Add boneless chicken into the chopper along with all the spices and all purpose flour. Step 4: Place the meatballs in a plate and into the freezer for about 10 mins. In the mean time start working on the curry. Step 5: Boil almond in water for about 5 to 10 mins. Step 16: Sprinkle some garam masala powder, garnish with ginger, chilies and dollop of ghee and wedges of lemon to sprinkle on top. Step 17: Serve with naan or roti or alfredo pasta.

Ingredient Names: chicken, moong dal, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak moong dal 20 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt and all the powdered spices and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add water, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the chicken is nearly tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the moong dal with enough water and simmer for 20-25 minutes until it is soft and the gravy is thick. Step 8: Temper with cumin fried in a little oil, add garam masala, green chili and coriander and serve hot. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, canned chickpeas, vegetable oil, onion, tomatoes, garlic paste, ginger paste, cumin seeds, salt, coriander powder, turmeric powder, to, garam masala powder, black pepper, cilantro, green chilies
Instructions: Step 1: Take a stockpot sized pot and put it on medium high heat, wait a few minutes, and then add the oil. When the oil is hot then add in the onions and the cumin seeds & cook until the onions start to turn golden brown at the edges. Highly recommend adding one of your green chilies (diced) in at this point. Step 2: Add the garlic and ginger pastes and saute for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes salt, chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Cover and keep it on medium high heat and then uncover, the tomatoes should have broken down and become jammy. Step 3: Stir your chicken pieces in and saute until the colour changes. Step 4: Now in goes a cup of hot water, the chickpeas, and a pinch of baking soda (for touch chickpeas), bring it to a boil, and then let it cook covered on low heat for another 25-30 minutes. Step 5: When the chicken is tender then adjust consistency of your gravy by adding water then add the garam masala, the black pepper, the green chillies and cilantro. Cook for 2 minutes then taste and adjust seasoning.

Ingredient Names: whole chicken, yogurt, onion, almonds, cashews, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, saffron, eggs, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Marinate a whole chicken in yogurt and spices for 4 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Fry whole chicken in ghee for 10 minutes until golden. Step 4: Cook in a gravy of fried onion and nut paste covered for 40 minutes, turning. Step 5: Garnish with boiled eggs and saffron. Step 6: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, cube, square, onions, big big onion, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, to, garam masala powder, black pepper powder, tomato paste, yogurt, water, salt, garlic and ginger paste, oil
Instructions: Step 1: In a pan roast 2 tsp of cumin seeds, with coriander seeds and whole red chilies for about 5 mins or until coriander seeds turn golden brown. Run the spices through a food process to get coarsely grounded spice mix. Step 2: Add finely chopped onion and 1 tsp whole cumin seeds in a pot along with oil. Allow the onions to turn golden brown. Step 3: Toss in cubed chicken and garlic ginger paste into the onions. Add the grounded spice mix and salt as well. Step 4: Saute the chicken for 2 to 3 mins at high flame or until the chicken turns white. Step 5: Add 1/2 cup of water with tomato paste and whisked yogurt in the chicken, cover it and let it cook for 10 mins. Step 6: In the meantime par-boil potato cubes in salt water for 3 to 4 mins. Step 7: In a frying pan, add 2 tbsp of oil and stir fry the parboiled potatoes, square cut onions and square cut capsicum. Step 8: Once the oil comes up around the chicken curry, add in the stir fried vegetables. Top it off with crushed black pepper and garam masala powder. Add more water if needed. Step 9: Serve with naan/roti or zeera pulao rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, spinach, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop finely. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the spinach and cook uncovered so the greens melt into the masala for 12 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, onion, green pepper or, garlic paste, ginger paste, salt, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, black pepper, white pepper, red chili powder, yogurt, cream, grated cheese, butter, freshly cracked pepper, sliced green chilies
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk your yoghurt well and keep near where you are cooking. Step 2: Heat a few tbsp of oil in a wok (with a lid) or saute pan. Step 3: Add your onions and cook on medium heat until they start to change color. Step 4: Now stir in your ginger and garlic paste and let it cook for a minute. Step 5: Add your chicken to that base and saute, moving frequently until the chicken pieces have all changed colour. Step 6: Go in with your spices and give it a quick cook, about a minute or so before adding in your yoghurt and a splash of water. Step 7: Let the chicken simmer, covered, until tender - this takes about 10 minutes tops. Step 8: Heat your charcoal and add your green peppers, butter, and cream into the chicken mix, cooking the peppers until just tender crisp. Step 9: Turn the stove off. Step 10: Place an onion peel or a piece of foil in the pan you are cooking in, place the charcoal on top, drizzle with oil and immediately shut the lid. Step 11: Remove the coal and foil/onion peel. If the handi is warm then just stir in the cheese, and if not then turn the heat on just enough to warm it and melt the cheese in. Step 12: Turn off immediately (cheese burns!), add your finishing touches of freshly cracked black pepper and green chilies and serve.

Ingredient Names: chicken, tomato, green chili, ginger, salt, black pepper, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the chicken into small pieces and wash. Step 3: Heat ghee in a karahi until very hot and fry the chicken with salt on high heat for 10 minutes. Step 4: Add whole tomatoes, cover for 5 minutes, then remove the skins and mash the tomatoes. Step 5: Bhuno on high heat for 10 minutes until the masala is thick and the ghee separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add crushed black pepper, ginger julienne and green chilies; no red chili is used in charsi karahi. Step 7: Serve straight from the karahi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, green beans, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the green beans, cover and cook for 12 minutes until soft. Step 8: Finish with garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and serve with roti. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, onion, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, wheat flour, red chili powder, garam masala, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat ghee and fry sliced onion for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry 10 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add yogurt, red chili, salt and water. Step 5: Transfer to a clay pot (kunna), cover and cook on low heat 30 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Stir in roasted flour slurry and cook 5 minutes until thick; sprinkle garam masala and serve with naan. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: desi chicken, onion, tomato, yogurt, garlic, ginger, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, black pepper, ghee, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry onion in ghee for 8 minutes, add chicken and garlic ginger and fry 10 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add tomato, yogurt and spices and bhuno for 10 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 4: Add a little water and cook covered for 30 minutes (desi chicken takes longer). Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Finish with black pepper and coriander and serve with roti. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, shezwan sauce, chili oil, salt, garlic, to, shallots, hoisin sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, ketchup, square, water, corn flour
Instructions: Step 1: In a wok, add oil, chopped garlic, shallots and whole red chilies. Saute at medium flame till they turn golden brown. Step 2: Add in boneless chicken and toss it around for 2 mins. Step 3: Add in the schezwan sauce, salt, sugar, oyster sauce, vinegar, ketchup and hoisin sauce. Saute for 3 to 4 mins or until the chicken loses its pink color. Step 4: Add in the bell peppers and saute for another 2 mins. Step 5: Pour in a cup of water mixed with corn flour. Step 6: Let the chicken simmer for another 5 mins or until the the gravy thickens. Step 7: Sprinkle sesame seeds and serve with fried rice or chow mein noodles.

Ingredient Names: chicken, broad beans, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: String the broad beans and cut into pieces. Step 3: Heat oil and fry sliced onion for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the chicken with ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken leg quarters, yogurt, fried onion, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, white pepper, garam masala, lemon juice, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make deep cuts in the chicken leg quarters. Step 3: Grind fried onion with yogurt and mix with ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, white pepper, garam masala, lemon juice and salt. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Rub the marinade into the chicken and marinate for 3 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 5: Heat ghee in a wide pan, place the chicken in one layer with all the marinade, cover and cook on low heat for 25 minutes, turning once. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Uncover and roast on high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until the masala sticks to the chicken and the ghee separates. Step 7: Serve as wedding-style roast with naan and salad. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, onion, yogurt, almonds, cashews, cream, saffron, cardamom, ginger garlic paste, white pepper, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes. Step 6: Grind almonds and cashews into a paste and stir it in with cream and saffron. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: chicken, turnip, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the turnips and cut into large cubes. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the turnip, cover and cook for 25 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, capsicum, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Deseed the capsicum and cut into squares. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the capsicum, cover and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, tomato, onion, ginger garlic paste, yogurt, red chili flakes, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black pepper, ghee, green chili, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry chicken in ghee with ginger garlic paste for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Add sliced onion and tomato and cook covered 6 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add yogurt and crushed coriander, cumin and chili flakes and bhuno 10 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Finish with black pepper and green chili. Step 6: Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies and serve hot with naan, roti or plain rice, with raita and kachumber salad on the side. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: whole chicken, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, garlic paste, basmati rice
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make deep cuts on a whole chicken and rub with salt, garlic paste, lemon juice and black pepper; marinate 2 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Parboil the basmati rice in salted water for 6 minutes and drain. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 4: Stuff the chicken cavity with the rice and close it with a skewer. Step 5: Roast on skewers around hot coals (or in an oven at 190°C) for 60-70 minutes, turning often, until golden. Step 6: Serve the chicken with the rice from inside, Sibi style. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, szechuan sauce, red chili paste, garlic, ginger, capsicum, onion, soy sauce, cornflour, egg, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry egg-and-cornflour coated chicken for 5 minutes. Step 3: Stir fry garlic, ginger, onion and capsicum 2 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add szechuan sauce, chili paste and soy sauce with water and thicken. Step 5: Toss in chicken; serve with fried rice. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, red onion, plain, whole-milk yogurt, tomato paste, neutral oil, crushed garlic, crushed ginger, tandoori masala powder, cumin seeds, paprika, asian red chili powder or cayenne, salt, green chili pepper, loosely packed cilantro leaves, freshly squeezed lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Use a knife to cut 2-3 slits into each chicken piece and place in a large bowl. Step 2: Add the rest of the ingredients listed in a food processor and blend until smooth. Pour this mixture onto the chicken and mix to ensure the chicken is thoroughly coated. Step 3: Cover and refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours, preferably overnight. Step 4: If possible, remove the chicken from the fridge to allow to come to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place the chicken pieces side by side (with its marinade) in a 9" x 13" oven-safe pan or roaster. Cover the pan tightly with aluminum foil and place the baking dish on the center rack of the oven. Bake for 30 minutes, then remove the foil and use a tong to turn over the chicken pieces. Cover with foil again and bake for an additional 25-30 minutes. Step 5: Remove the foil, turn your broiler on to high, and let the chicken broil for about 2-3 minutes. Then, turn the pieces over and broil again for 5-6 minutes, or until the chicken has a nice charred finish. Step 6: Serve with naan or French fries and a salad.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, onion, tomato, capsicum, ginger garlic paste, yogurt, red chili flakes, coriander seeds, butter, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the chicken into small boneless pieces. Step 3: Heat oil on a large tawa and cook the chicken with ginger garlic paste for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, crushed coriander seeds, chili flakes and salt. Step 5: Chop and mix with two spatulas for 8 minutes until the masala is thick. Step 6: Add onion and capsicum cubes and cook 3 minutes so they stay crunchy. Step 7: Finish with butter and serve with naan from the tawa. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, round gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the tinday and cut into quarters. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the round gourd, cover and cook for 18 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: chicken, ridge gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander

Step 4: Add the chicken with ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook for 12 minutes until soft. Step 8: Finish with garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and serve with roti. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: chicken, onion, yogurt, cream, almonds, white pepper, green chili, cardamom, ginger garlic paste, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes. Step 6: Use boiled (not fried) onion paste so the gravy stays white, and finish with cream. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: chicken, onions, peppercorns, cinnamon, green cardamoms, ginger, garlic, salt, coriander powder, black pepper, garam masala powder, yogurt, any neutral oil for cooking, a handful of washed, finely diced chilies
Instructions: Step 1: Heat the oil in a heavy bottomed pot. Step 2: Add the whole spices and cook until you can smell them (less than a minute). Step 3: In go the diced onions, saute till they soften and the edges start to change colour. Step 4: Stir in your ginger and garlic and cook for a minute. Step 5: Now add in your salt and coriander powder, saute for a minute and add your chicken pieces to the pot. Step 6: Cook the chicken on medium high heat stirring every 30 seconds or so until the chicken looks completely white on the outside, then turn the heat down a little and cook for five more minutes. Step 7: Add a cup of water to the chicken, bring to a boil and then simmer for 25-30 minutes or until tender. Add more water if needed to prevent sticking. Step 8: Now in goes the yoghurt. Tip: Yoghurt splits because it's a different temperature than the curry. Add two tbsp of the curry into the yoghurt, mix well, and then add the yoghurt into the salan. Step 9: Adjust the seasoning (salt) and add your garam masala and pepper. Step 10: Generously add in chopped chillies and cilantro and give it a good stir to allow the chillies to combine with the curry.

Ingredient Names: chicken breast, all-purpose flour, cornflour, eggs, milk, red chili powder, garlic powder, black pepper, burger buns, lettuce, mayonnaise, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Flatten chicken breast and marinate with chili, garlic, pepper and salt for 1 hour. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Dip in egg-milk and toss in seasoned flour with a few drops of water for flakes. Step 4: Deep fry 8-10 minutes until crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Serve in a toasted bun with lettuce and spicy mayo. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2-3 days; reheat with a splash of water.

Ingredient Names: raw mango, mustard oil, fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and completely dry the raw mango and cut into pieces; any water will spoil the achaar. Step 2: Rub with salt and turmeric and dry in the sun for 1 day. Step 3: Coarsely grind fennel, fenugreek, mustard and nigella seeds and mix with red chili. Step 4: Heat mustard oil until it smokes, cool it, and mix the spices and vegetables in it. Step 5: Fill a clean glass jar so the oil covers everything and keep in the sun for 7-10 days, shaking daily. Step 6: Serve a little with dal chawal or paratha. Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Soak and grind figs. Ingredient Names: wheat flour, sugar, ghee, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Roast wheat flour in ghee on low heat for 15 minutes until deep golden. Step 3: Shape rounds with a dent in the centre. Step 4: Fry on very low heat for 15 minutes until golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Dip in thick sugar syrup for 3 minutes. Ingredient Names: gram flour, milk, sugar, ghee, cardamom, almonds

Ingredient Names: gram flour, ghee, powdered sugar, cardamom, almonds

Ingredient Names: gram flour, sugar, ghee, cardamom, food color
Instructions: Step 1: Fry boondi from thin batter for 2 minutes. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 2: Soak in sugar syrup 10 minutes and shape into ladoos. Ingredient Names: white bread, fine semolina, baking powder, milk at room temperature, sugar, water, green cardamom or use, saffron threads, oil to fry the gulab jamun, shelled pistachios + a
Instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, add the slices of the bread, add the semolina and baking powder. Step 2: Gradually pour the milk and lightly knead until you get a smooth dough. A stiff dough will result in hard and unevenly cooked Gulab Jamun. Step 3: Cover the dough and allow it to rest for 15 minutes. The semolina will soak up some of the milk and become softer. Step 4: Make 10 equal size balls from the dough, gently flatten the balls, fill them with pistachio, and then close and form a smooth crack free ball. Cover the balls to prevent them from drying. Step 5: In a frying pan, heat enough oil to come halfway up the balls. Keep the heat on medium. Step 6: Fry the balls in batches until they turn brown. It will take a minute or two to brown. Step 7: Remove the balls from the oil and place them on a kitchen towel, or you can add the fried balls immediately in the syrup. Step 8: Heat the syrup and allow it to come to a simmer. Let the Gulab Jamun simmer in the syrup for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and cover. Step 9: It's best to leave the Bread Gulab Jamun in the syrup for at least 2 hours before serving. Step 10: In a pan, add the sugar and water. Step 11: When it comes to a boil, add the cardamom. Step 12: Let the syrup cook for 8 minutes on medium heat. Step 13: Add saffron threads and stir the syrup. Turn off the heat.

Ingredient Names: milk, half and half, plain croissants, tea rusks, cardamoms, saffron, sugar, minced pistachios, minced blanched almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Heat milk and half and half in a large heavy-bottomed pot on the stove (not nonstick). Step 2: Bring the mixture to a boil, tear the croissants and rusks into pieces and add them in. Step 3: Simmer until both breads are soft, about 5-6 minutes. Step 4: Puree with a handheld (immersion) blender or in a regular blender. Step 5: Pour back in the pot (if using a regular blender). Add the cardamom, saffron, sugar and half the nuts. Step 6: Simmer on low heat, stirring frequently, the mixture will darken and thicken. As it becomes thick it starts to bubble, so please do be careful! TIP: Leave a wooden spoon in the pot to prevent any bubbling over. Step 7: Cook it down by about 40 percent (nearly half) of what it was –this takes about 20-30 minutes depending on the pot you are using. Step 8: Put in your serving dishes/glasses, let cool, and scatter with the remaining nuts right before serving.

Ingredient Names: bread, milk, eggs, sugar, butter, raisins, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Soak buttered bread pieces in milk whisked with eggs, sugar and cardamom. Step 2: Add raisins and bake at 180°C for 35 minutes until set and golden. Step 3: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 4: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, basmati rice, sugar, cardamom, khoya, kewra water, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook crushed soaked rice in milk on low heat for 60 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar, khoya and cardamom and cook 10 minutes. Step 4: Add kewra and set in clay bowls in the fridge for 3 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sugar, water, milk, cream, eggs, vanilla extract, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Preheat your oven to 325 degrees F and place the roasting pan with an inch or two of water inside the oven. Step 2: Pour the water into a heavy bottomed pan and then sprinkle your sugar over top. Do not stir. Step 3: Keep the pan on medium heat and keep a close eye on the sugar, but again do not stir. Step 4: As the sugar turns a honey color watch carefully, you want a dark amber liquid, but this happens very fast. You can swirl the pan gently to even the caramelizing. Step 5: As soon as it turns a beautiful amber colour pour it into your custard dish. Step 6: There is loads of beautiful caramel flavour still in the pan you used for caramelizing the sugar so pour your liquids into the pan along with the sugar and the salt and warm through stirring occasionally. Take your milk off the heat. Step 7: Crack 6 eggs into your blender along with the vanilla extract and pulse/blend slightly to create an even mix. Step 8: Now while your blender is running on low pour the milk mix into the blender through the feed tube/opening, stop running the blender as soon as it is all in. If you are not comfortable pouring while blending then just wait for your milk to cool to room temperature and pour it directly into the blender. Step 9: Pour the mixture into your caramel dish, you can remove the foam from the top. Step 10: Place the pan inside the roasting pan with water and gently pour in more hot water so that only the top inch of the pan isn't submerged. Step 11: Bake until the sides are set and the center is still jiggly, 50- 55 minutes for a loaf pan, 40-45 for a round pan. When you touch the top it will seem soft but set. Step 12: Cool completely (4 hours+ in the fridge) then run a knife along the edges to separate them. Invert in a dish with high sides and pour the remaining caramel sauce in the pan into another small bowl for your grateful loved ones.

Ingredient Names: milk, lemon juice, sugar, khoya, coconut, cardamom, food color
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make chenna, knead and shape into ovals. Ingredient Names: milk, rice flour, sugar, cardamom, kewra water, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix ground rice with a little cold milk. Step 4: Add sugar, cardamom and kewra, pour into clay bowls and chill 2 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Ingredient Names: basmati rice, water, full fat milk, white sugar, condensed milk, evaporated milk, sliced or chopped pistachio and almonds, rose buds or petals
Instructions: Step 1: In the pot, add rice and water. Simmer at medium flame until all the water evaporates and rice doubles in size. Use a hand whisk to stir the rice. Step 4: You will see the rice grains will have broken down into smaller bits and the rice and milk would now be in a pudding consistency. Turn off the flame and let the kheer cool down. Step 5: Now add evaporated milk. Add as much as you like for the consistency you prefer.

Ingredient Names: milk, custard powder, sugar, sponge cake, jelly, mixed fruits, cream
Instructions: Step 1: Make thick custard and cool. Step 2: Layer sponge, fruits, jelly and custard in a bowl. Step 3: Top with whipped cream and chill 3 hours. Ingredient Names: bread slices, ghee, milk, sugar, saffron, cardamom, almonds

Ingredient Names: dates, almonds, cashews, pistachios, walnuts, ghee, poppy seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Roast the nuts in ghee 3 minutes and chop. Ingredient Names: full cream milk, sugar, khoya, cardamom, pistachios, almonds, kewra water

Ingredient Names: malai kulfi, falooda sev, rooh afza, basil seeds, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Slice kulfi onto a plate. Step 3: Top with cold falooda sev, basil seeds and rooh afza. Ingredient Names: milk, custard powder, sugar, banana, apple, grapes, pomegranate seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Boil milk with sugar, add custard powder mixed in cold milk and stir 3 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 2: Cool fully and fold in chopped fruit. Step 3: Chill and serve. Ingredient Names: sesame seeds, jaggery, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Roast sesame seeds 4 minutes. Step 2: Cook jaggery to a hard crack syrup in 8 minutes, add sesame and ghee. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 3: Pound and roll thin while hot, cut into pieces. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: carrots, milk, sugar, khoya, ghee, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Cook grated carrots in milk until dry, about 40 minutes. Step 2: Add sugar, ghee and khoya and cook until it leaves the pan. Step 3: Set in a tray and cut into squares. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: organic carrots, ghee, green cardamom pods, milk, heavy whipping cream, raw cane sugar or sweetener of choice, slivered pistachios, slivered almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Use the shredder attachment of food processor to thinly grate the carrots, in batches if necessary. Set aside. Step 2: Select the Sauté setting on the Instant Pot and set to More/High. Once hot, add 2 tbsp of the ghee, cardamom pods, and shredded carrots. Sauté for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the color starts to change and the carrots reduce down a bit. Add the whole milk and heavy whipping cream and stir to mix. Step 3: Cancel the sauté setting, secure the lid and set the Pressure Release to Sealing. Select the Pressure. Step 4: Cook setting and set the cooking time to 30 minutes on High pressure. Step 5: Allow the pressure to naturally release for 3-5 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure by moving the Pressure Release to Venting, select the. Step 6: Sauté setting and set to More/High. Sauté, stirring occasionally until most of the moisture has evaporated and the carrots start sticking to the bottom (~10 minutes). Step 7: Add the remaining 1 tbsp of ghee and sugar and sauté again, scraping the bottom of the pot as you go, for another 8-10 minutes. This step is imperative to bring out the color and flavor. Step 8: Once the the halwa is dry, the ghee starts to separate, and the carrot halwa turns a deep orange (closer to red) color, press the Cancel button to turn off the Instant Pot. Step 9: Scoop into a serving dish and decorate with pistachios and almonds, if desired.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, carrot, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Grate carrots and cook in milk for 30 minutes. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: edible gum, wheat flour, ghee, sugar, almonds, dried coconut, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry gond in ghee until it puffs, then crush. Step 3: Roast wheat flour in ghee 10 minutes until golden. Step 4: Add sugar syrup, gond, nuts and coconut and cook 5 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: edible gum, wheat flour, ghee, sugar, almonds, dried coconut, dates
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Fry gond in ghee until puffed and crush. Step 3: Roast wheat flour in ghee 10 minutes. Step 4: Mix with powdered sugar, gond, nuts and chopped dates and shape ladoos while warm. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: neutral oil, nido whole milk powder, original pancake mix, pinch cardamom powder, heavy whipping cream, water, sugar, cardamom pods, pinch saffron strands, rose water
Instructions: Step 1: Pour oil into a medium to large frying pan so that it's about 1.5-2”/4-5 cm deep. It should be deep enough so that the dough balls don't stick to the bottom. Turn the heat on to low (~200-220°F/93–104°C.) while you proceed with the dough balls. Step 2: Place the milk powder, pancake mix, and cardamom powder in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine. Step 3: Pour in the oil, using your hands to stir and rub the oil into the dry mixture as you go, until the mixture looks crumbly. (I find this works better when I use my hands but you can also use a spoon.). Step 4: Gradually mix in the egg, then heavy whipping cream and continue mixing with your hands or spoon for another 15-30 seconds, just until there aren’t any more lumps of dough. At this point it’ll be a non-cohesive, sticky mass. (Wipe your hands of excess mixture and add to the ball.) Cover and allow to rest while you prepare the sugar syrup (Mixture will rest around 10 min - more or less is fine). Step 5: Heat a wide saucepan, small wok, or small Dutch oven over medium-high heat (you need a pan deep enough so that it’ll submerge the jamuns but wide enough so they don’t lose shape). Add the water, sugar, cardamom, and saffron and bring to a boil while stirring occasionally, allowing the sugar to dissolve. This takes around 3 minutes. Reduce the heat to medium and continue to simmer until it thickens. Meanwhile, form and fry your jamuns. Step 6: Lightly oil your palms. Working quickly to prevent the dough from drying out, scoop around 2 tsp (10–12g) of dough — keeping the remaining mixture covered — and roll it into a smooth, round ball, ensuring there are no cracks or dents. Use firm pressure to eliminate air pockets and create a polished surface. (I like to transfer between my palms to eliminate air pockets, then begin rolling.) Place on a plate and repeat with the remaining dough. (Makes 14–16 small jamun balls). Step 7: Increase oil heat to low-medium (~270-300°F/132-138°C) and adjust heat level as needed to maintain this heat. Carefully add the dough balls to the hot oil (don’t worry about reshaping if flattened a bit - it’s more about adding quickly at this stage). Fry, stirring and turning constantly, until evenly golden brown and cooked through, about 6 minutes. Use a slotted spoon or spider strainer to remove the balls and place onto a paper-towel lined plate to absorb excess oil. Step 8: At this stage, the sugar syrup will have thickened slightly, but it’ll still be runny - keep in mind it will thicken even more once cooled. Turn off the heat. Transfer Jamuns to the hot syrup and gently toss to coat in the syrup.(If adding rose water, add now.) Let them sit in the syrup, covered with the lid ajar, for 30 minutes to absorb the syrup. Turn the jamun over 2-3 times while resting to evenly distribute syrup and prevent them from “sitting” and flattening out the bottom. Serve warm immediately. If serving later, reheat before serving for the softest texture.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, sugar, gulab jamun, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make a creamy kheer with rice and milk 45 minutes. Step 3: Chill and top with halved gulab jamun. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gulab jamun, custard powder, milk, sugar, sponge cake, cream, fruit cocktail, jelly
Instructions: Step 1: Make custard and cool. Step 2: Layer sponge, fruit, custard and halved gulab jamun. Step 3: Top with whipped cream and set jelly cubes; chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, jaggery, fennel seeds, milk, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Dissolve jaggery in warm milk. Step 2: Mix with flour and fennel into a thick batter. Step 3: Drop spoonfuls into oil and fry 5 minutes; a rainy-day treat. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: rice, jaggery, ghee, fennel seeds, coconut, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil rice 3/4 done and drain. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 3: Melt gur in ghee with fennel, add rice and steam 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 4: Top with coconut and almonds. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, basmati rice, jaggery, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 3: Cook rice in milk 45 minutes; stir in jaggery only after turning off the heat. Step 4: Cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the jaggery so the milk does not split. Step 5: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 6: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: aged, long-grain basmati rice, filtered water, unsalted butter, ghee, green cardamom pods, bay leaf, jaggery, nuts such as cashews/slivered almonds or raisins
Instructions: Step 1: Place rice in a medium-sized bowl and fill with water. Use your hand to swirl the rice around gently until the water becomes murky. Tip the bowl to take out the excess water and repeat until the water runs clear. Strain it and place it in a rice cooker with 1 3/4 cups of filtered water. Choose Normal (Regular/Sushi) Rice setting. Step 2: Halfway through cooking the rice, start the jaggery melting process. Heat a saucepan over medium heat and add butter, ghee, cardamom pods, and bay leaf. When the butter and ghee melt (be careful not to let the butter brown), add the remaining 1/4 cup of water along with the jaggery. Let it simmer while stirring to melt all the chunks, 4-5 minutes. Once the jaggery has melted and most of the water moisture has evaporated, remove it from heat and set aside. Step 3: When the rice is about 3/4th done and heavy steam starts escaping from the rice cooker, open the lid and add the jaggery syrup to the rice cooker. Stir carefully to coat the rice in the syrup. Close the rice cooker again, letting it finish cooking the rice. Step 4: After the rice has finished cooking, let the rice rest for 10 minutes before serving. If you feel that the jaggery still hasn't completely melted into the rice, close the lid and let it rest up to an hour. Serve with any garnishing of choice. I like to eat it plain with some crème (malai) or British double cream (if you can find it) on the side.

Ingredient Names: milk, sprouted wheat flour, sugar, ghee, cocoa powder, almonds, pistachios, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil milk and reduce for 1 hour, stirring. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Add samnak and sugar and cook 1 more hour on low heat until dark brown and grainy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add ghee and keep stirring until it leaves the sides; mix in cardamom and nuts. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: dried apricots, wheat flour, apricot oil, walnuts, honey
Instructions: Step 1: Soak and mash dried apricots. Step 2: Roast flour in apricot oil 8 minutes, add apricot pulp and honey and cook 10 minutes. Step 3: Add walnuts. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, walnuts, sugar, eggs, butter, baking powder, vanilla, milk
Instructions: Step 1: Beat butter and sugar for 3 minutes, add eggs one by one. Step 2: Fold in flour, baking powder, milk and chopped walnuts. Step 3: Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, sugar, cardamom, saffron, pistachios, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil milk in a wide karahi on low heat for 60-90 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Keep pulling the cream layers to the sides. Step 4: Add sugar, cardamom and saffron, mix in the layers and chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: urad dal, sugar, food color, saffron, rose water, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Soak urad dal 4 hours and grind to a very smooth batter; beat 10 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 2: Make a sugar syrup with saffron and rose water for 6 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 3: Pipe flower-shaped imartis into ghee and fry 2-3 minutes. Step 4: Soak in syrup for 3 minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: date syrup, salt or, dahi bara spice mix, crushed red chili flakes, chat masala powder, tamarind pulp block with seeds, tamarind pulp block without seeds, tamarind paste
Instructions: Step 1: Place a colander in a heat-proof bowl and put tamarind blocks inside the colander. Now, pour boiling water at least 2 cups or enough to soak the entire block completely. Set aside for 10 minutes. Step 2: Use a spoon or fork to break the block of tamarind into little pieces. Add another 1 cup of cold water to bring down the water temperature. Now use your hands to squeeze all the chunks of tamarind to release all the tamarind juices from the seeds etc. Test the water temperature first before dipping your fingers into it. Don't worry about how much water you are using, we'll cook it down eventually. Step 3: Pick up the colander and allow all the tamarind juice to strain into the bowl. Transfer the tamarind juice to a cooking pot. You can repeat the previous step if you think there is more juice to be extracted. Step 4: Add all the seasoning (minus the date syrup) and boil the tamarind juices at medium flame for 20 minutes. Your tamarind juice should be reduced to half its original quantity. Step 5: Now add date syrup, date paste or any other sweetener you prefer. Let the chutney simmer for another 10 minutes at medium-low heat. Step 6: Turn off the heat and do a taste test to check salt, heat and sweetness. Adjust salt according to your liking. Step 7: Allow the chutney to cool down uncovered. It'll thicken a bit more as it cools. Transfer into waterproof jars and store in the fridge. Step 8: Add all the ingredients in a cooking pot with 4 cups of water. Boil at medium high flame for 5 minutes. Step 9: Turn off heat and do a taste test to check salt, heat, and sweetness. Adjust salt according to your liking. Step 10: Allow the chutney to cool down uncovered. It'll thicken a bit more as it cools. Transfer into waterproof jars and store in the fridge.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, yogurt, cornflour, baking powder, sugar, saffron, cardamom, lemon juice, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix flour, cornflour and yogurt with water into a thick batter and ferment 8 hours (or add baking powder for instant). Step 3: Boil sugar and water with saffron, cardamom and lemon for 6 minutes to one-string syrup. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Pipe spirals into hot ghee and fry 2 minutes each side until crisp. Step 5: Dip in warm syrup for 1 minute and serve hot. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: jalebi, milk, sugar, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly.
