Step 2: Reduce milk to thick rabri for 1 hour with sugar and cardamom. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Serve hot crisp jalebi with chilled or warm rabri on top and pistachios. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sized pumpkin, cardamom powder, milk, ghee, sugar, nuts
Instructions: Step 1: Add the grated pumpkin, cardamom powder and whole milk to a pot or pan. Heat over a high heat, stirring often until the mixture becomes very dry,. Step 2: Add in the sugar. It'll melt and liquify - continue to stir and dry out the mixture over a high heat until it begins to look dry again. Step 3: Add the ghee/oil in. Continue to cook over a high heat, stirring often. The mixture will turn to a glossy, dark shade of orange. Step 4: Keep stirring the mixture until the it begins to pull away from the pan and looks fudgy. Step 5: Garnish with nuts and serve warm.

Ingredient Names: cashews, sugar, water, ghee, edible silver leaf
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Grind cashews to a fine powder. Step 3: Make a one-thread sugar syrup, add cashew powder and stir on low heat 8 minutes until it forms a dough. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Knead with ghee, roll thin, add silver leaf and cut diamonds. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: khoya, flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom, rose water, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Knead khoya with flour and a pinch of baking powder; shape balls. Step 2: Fry on low heat 10 minutes until very dark. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Soak in warm cardamom-rose syrup for 2 hours. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, lemon juice, sugar, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil milk and reduce for 30 minutes; add a little lemon to make it grainy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Add sugar and cook 15 minutes until thick. Step 4: Set in a tray for 3 hours and cut. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, falooda sev, basil seeds, rooh afza, kulfi, jelly, pistachios, sugar
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Soak basil seeds for 20 minutes and boil falooda sev for 5 minutes, then chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 3: In a tall glass add rooh afza, basil seeds, sev and jelly. Step 4: Pour chilled sweet milk, top with a slice of kulfi and pistachios. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: ice, rooh afza, kala khatta syrup, condensed milk, khoya, coconut
Instructions: Step 1: Shave a block of ice and press into a ball on a stick. Step 2: Pour rooh afza and kala khatta syrups on top. Step 3: Drizzle condensed milk and sprinkle khoya and coconut; eat quickly. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: cornflour, sugar, ghee, water, lemon juice, food colour, cashews, almonds, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix cornflour in water; make a sugar syrup with lemon juice. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 3: Add the cornflour mixture to the syrup and stir on medium heat for 30 minutes, adding ghee a little at a time. Step 4: When glossy and leaving the pan, add colour, nuts and cardamom and set in a greased tray; cut once cool. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice flour, sugar, saffron, cardamom, almonds, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Dissolve rice flour in milk and cook with sugar on low heat for 15 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add saffron and cardamom. Step 4: Set in clay bowls for 2 hours and top with nuts. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: paneer, dates, almonds, walnuts, coconut, sugar, saffron, cardamom, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Fry paneer cubes in ghee 2 minutes. Step 2: Add chopped dates and nuts and fry 2 minutes. Step 3: Add thick sugar syrup with saffron and cardamom and toss until coated. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ghee, sugar, milk, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Make a layered dough with ghee and roll into rounds. Step 2: Fry on low heat for 12 minutes until puffed and flaky. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Dust with sugar; eaten at Ramadan sehri with pheni. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: dates, milk, ghee, cardamom, walnuts
Instructions: Step 1: Deseed and mash the dates with warm milk. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, dates, rice, almonds, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak and blend dates with a little milk. Step 3: Cook rice in milk 40 minutes, add the date paste and cook 10 minutes (no sugar needed). Step 4: Add cardamom and almonds. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, lemon juice, sugar, khoya, rasgulla, coconut, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make small rasgullas and sweet khoya. Step 3: Wrap each rasgulla in khoya. Step 4: Roll in coconut. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, basmati rice, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak rice for 1 hour and crush lightly. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Boil milk, add rice and cook on low heat for 45-50 minutes, stirring often, until creamy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add sugar and cardamom and cook 10 minutes. Step 5: Add kewra, chill in clay bowls and garnish with nuts. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: khoya, sugar, cardamom, pistachios, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook khoya in a pan for 6 minutes until soft. Step 3: Add sugar and cardamom and stir 8 minutes until it leaves the sides. Step 4: Spread in a greased tray, top with pistachios, cool 2 hours and cut. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: khoya, sugar, ghee, semolina, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast semolina in ghee 5 minutes. Step 3: Add crumbled khoya and sugar and stir 10 minutes. Step 4: Finish with cardamom and pistachios. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, khoya, sugar, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Reduce milk 1 hour and mix in khoya and sugar. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Cool, add cardamom and pistachios. Step 4: Freeze in moulds overnight. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, sprouted wheat, ghee, sugar, almonds, walnuts, pistachios, cornflour
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Boil milk and add sprouted wheat paste; cook on low heat for 60 minutes, stirring. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar and keep stirring for 30 minutes until brown and grainy. Step 4: Add ghee and nuts and cook 20 minutes; press into a tray and cut after cooling. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, custard powder, sugar, vermicelli, jelly, mixed fruits, cream
Instructions: Step 1: Cook custard in milk with sugar for 5 minutes and cool. Step 2: Boil vermicelli 5 minutes; set jelly in a tray. Step 3: Fold custard, cream, vermicelli, fruit and jelly cubes together and chill 3 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gram flour, sugar, ghee, melon seeds, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Roast besan in ghee 15 minutes until golden and fragrant. Step 2: Cool slightly, add powdered sugar, cardamom and melon seeds. Step 3: Shape ladoos. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: bottle gourd, milk, sugar, khoya, ghee, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Grate the lauki, squeeze lightly and cook in milk for 35 minutes. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, bottle gourd, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Grate lauki and cook in milk for 30 minutes. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, jaggery, ghee, fennel seeds, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Melt jaggery in a little water for 4 minutes. Step 2: Knead flour with ghee, fennel, cardamom and the jaggery water. Step 3: Roll thick and cook on a tawa with ghee on low for 6 minutes each side. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, makhana, ghee, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Roast makhana in ghee 4 minutes, crush half and cook in milk 20 minutes. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: condensed milk, evaporated milk, thick cream, fresh bread with corners, green cardamom powder, rose water, pistachio powder, chopped almonds and pistachio
Instructions: Step 1: In a bowl add all the ingredients except pistachio powder and nuts. Step 2: Blend everything together with a hand blender to get a smooth kulfi base. (you can also do this step in a blender). Step 3: Cover the bowl with a cling wrap. Step 4: Put the bowl in the freezer for 6 to 7 hours. (the corners of your bowl should be frozen and the centre still liquid). Step 5: Preparing loaf pan. Step 6: Put your pistachios in a chopper and make almost like a pistachio powder. Step 7: Take out your non-stick bread loaf pan size and sprinkle the base the pistachio powder generously. Step 8: Take out the kullfi base and whip the base with an electric beater. Break all the ice crystals properly and cream a smooth base again. You can also add chopped nuts, etc at this point in your base if you want to. Step 9: Pour your kulfi base into the prepared loaf pan. Step 10: Place a layer of butter paper or cling wrap directly on top of the kulfi to avoid any air contact. Make sure to seal all the corners of the loaf properly. Step 11: Place the load back in the freezer and let it chill overnight. Step 12: Remove the frozen kulfi from the freezer and remove the cling wrap. Step 13: Place it inverted on the tray you want to serve your kulfi in. Step 14: Dip a kitchen towel in hot boiling water. Run the towel all around the loaf pan, including the sides and base for 2 to 3 mins. Step 15: Lift the mould up (it is still inverted) and press the center of the base with your thumbs. This should release the icecream of the pan and drop it onto your serving dish. If the ice cream doesn't drop, repeat the wet towel procedure once more and try again. Step 16: Once your ice cream is released, sprinkle some more chopped nuts of your choice on top and serve immediately. You can also drip some rose syrup on top.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, milk, sugar, fennel seeds, cardamom, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Make a thick batter with flour, milk, fennel and cardamom; rest 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry ladlefuls in ghee 2 minutes per side. Step 3: Dip in sugar syrup for 1 minute; a monsoon treat. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, rice flour, mango, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Cook rice flour firni for 12 minutes, cool and fold in mango puree. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, condensed milk, mango, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Reduce milk for 30 minutes with condensed milk. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 2: Cool and blend with mango pulp. Step 3: Freeze 8 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: mango pulp, milk, cream, sugar, gelatin, mango cubes
Instructions: Step 1: Dissolve gelatin in warm water. Step 2: Blend mango pulp, milk, cream and sugar and mix in the gelatin. Step 3: Set in a mould 4 hours and top with mango cubes. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, jaggery, cardamom, coconut, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook rice in milk for 45 minutes. Step 3: Turn off heat, stir in jaggery and cardamom. Step 4: Garnish with coconut and almonds. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, sugar, khoya, cardamom, pistachios, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Reduce milk to one-third for 1.5 hours. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Add sugar, khoya and cardamom and cool. Step 4: Pour into small clay matkas, cover and freeze 8 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: betel leaf, gulkand, fennel seeds, coconut, cardamom, sweet supari, cherry
Instructions: Step 1: Wipe the betel leaf and spread gulkand. Step 2: Add fennel, coconut, cardamom and sweet supari. Step 3: Fold into a triangle and pin with a clove; eaten after dinner. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, sugar, ghee, cardamom, cloves, raisins, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Par-boil rice 8 minutes and drain. Step 3: Cook with sugar, ghee and spices on low for 10 minutes. Step 4: Dum 15 minutes and top with nuts. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: plain flour, butter, water, dessicated coconut, white sugar, egg, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Begin with making the pastry. In a bowl, add the butter and use your fingertips to mix the butter into the flour, until it resembles breadcrumbs. Step 2: Add water, a few tbsp at a time. Use your hands to knead the dough until it forms a firm dough. Be very careful not to add too much water, as if the dough becomes too wet it will be too difficult to work with. Step 3: Allow the dough to rest for at least 30 minutes. Step 4: To make the filling, simply mix all the ingredients together until well incorporated and set aside. Step 5: Take small balls out of the dough and begin to roll them out into circles, much like making a small chapatti. Cut the circles into 4 quarters. Step 6: Working with each quarter, shape and fill the samosas as shown in the post until you have finished all the dough,. Step 7: Heat oil in a deep wok or pan on medium heat. Fry the samosas on medium heat, turning throughout the fry time. Step 8: Serve immediately,.

Ingredient Names: salted butter, ghee, vermicelli, water, green cardamom pods, slivered
Instructions: Step 1: Using your hands, crush the vermicelli within the closed packet. Step 2: Melt the butter and ghee in a nonstick Dutch oven or other deep pan over medium heat. Open the packet and add the crushed vermicelli to the pan. Toast for 6 minutes, until it goes from golden to dark caramel in color and becomes aromatic. Use a wooden spoon to further mash the vermicelli into small pieces within the pan. Turn off the heat. Step 3: Meanwhile, place another small saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the measured water, sugar, and cardamom pods and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and simmer until the sugar has dissolved, about a minute. Turn off the heat. Step 4: Pour the sugar water into the vermicelli and stir to combine. Turn on the heat to medium-high. Once the liquid comes to a boil, reduce the heat to low. Cover and gently simmer for 5-6 minutes, until all of the water has absorbed or evaporated. Turn off the heat and allow it to rest, covered, for another 5 minutes. Transfer to your serving dish and garnish with finely chopped nuts.

Ingredient Names: fenugreek seeds, wheat flour, jaggery, ghee, edible gum, almonds, dried ginger
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Soak methi seeds in milk overnight and grind. Step 3: Roast flour, methi paste and gond in ghee 15 minutes. Step 4: Add melted gur, dried ginger and nuts and shape ladoos (eaten in winter for warmth). Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gram flour, ghee, milk, khoya, sugar, cardamom, saffron, almonds, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Rub gram flour with a little ghee and milk and sieve to make it grainy. Step 3: Roast in ghee on low heat for 20 minutes until golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add khoya, then sugar syrup with saffron and cardamom and stir 5 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 5: Set in a tray topped with nuts and cut after 3 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: moong dal, milk, sugar, ghee, khoya, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Soak moong dal 4 hours, grind to a coarse paste and roast in ghee for 30 minutes. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: moong dal, ghee, sugar, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: pick through the dal for small stones and wash it 2-3 times; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Dry roast moong dal 6 minutes and grind. Step 3: Roast the flour in ghee 10 minutes until fragrant. Step 4: Mix with powdered sugar, cardamom and almonds and shape. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gram flour, sugar, ghee, food color, cardamom, melon seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Make a thin gram flour batter and drop tiny boondi through a slotted spoon into ghee; fry 1 minute. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 2: Soak the boondi in sugar syrup with cardamom for 10 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 3: Add melon seeds and shape into ladoos while warm. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: semolina, ghee, sugar, milk, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, food color
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast semolina in ghee for 12 minutes on low heat. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add milk and sugar and stir for 10 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add cardamom and color and cook 5 minutes until ghee separates. Step 5: Top with nuts and serve hot. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, sprouted wheat flour, sugar, ghee, cornflour, almonds, pistachios, walnuts, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix sprouted wheat flour and cornflour in milk to a smooth paste. Step 3: Bring milk to a boil, add the paste and sugar and cook on medium heat for 40 minutes, stirring constantly. Step 4: When it darkens and thickens, add ghee in batches and keep stirring for 20-30 minutes until ghee separates. Step 5: Add cardamom and half the nuts, spread on a greased tray and top with the rest. Step 6: Cool for 2 hours and cut into pieces. Step 7: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 8: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, sugar, ghee, khoya, cham cham, food color, cardamom, cloves, raisins, almonds, pineapple, coconut
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil rice with colors for 8 minutes. Step 3: Fry spices in ghee, add rice and sugar and cook 10 minutes. Step 4: Layer with khoya, cham cham, fruit and nuts and dum 15 minutes; a wedding sweet rice. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ajwain, ghee, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with ajwain, ghee and salt. Step 2: Roll and cut into diamonds. Step 3: Fry on low heat for 10 minutes; store in a jar for tea time. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: flour, gram flour, semolina, sugar, ghee, cardamom, baking powder, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cream ghee and sugar until fluffy. Step 3: Mix in flour, besan, semolina, baking powder and cardamom to a soft dough. Step 4: Shape rounds, top with pistachio and bake at 170°C for 20 minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, ghee, sugar, almonds, cashews, pistachios, makhana, gond, dried coconut, fennel seeds, carom seeds, dried ginger powder
Instructions: Step 1: Fry gond and makhana in ghee for 2 minutes each and crush. Step 2: Fry chopped nuts for 2 minutes and keep aside. Step 3: Roast wheat flour in ghee on low heat for 20 minutes until golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add fennel, carom seeds and dried ginger powder and roast 2 minutes. Step 5: Off the heat mix in sugar, nuts, coconut, gond and makhana; serve a spoonful in winter mornings. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gram flour, all-purpose flour, ghee, sugar, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast both flours in ghee for 15 minutes. Step 3: Cook sugar syrup to hard ball stage for 10 minutes and pull it. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Fold the flour into the hot syrup until flaky threads form; press and cut. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: khoya, sugar, cardamom, saffron, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook khoya with sugar for 8 minutes until it thickens. Step 3: Add cardamom and saffron, cool slightly and shape into pedas pressed with a pistachio. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: chana dal, milk, sugar, ghee, khoya, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: pick through the dal for small stones and wash it 2-3 times; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chana dal in milk for 40 minutes and grind into paste. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 3: Cook the paste in ghee on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add sugar, khoya and cardamom and cook 10 minutes until ghee separates. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, sugar, cornflour, cardamom, pistachios, ice, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil milk with sugar and cardamom for 20 minutes and thicken with cornflour. Step 3: Churn in a metal pot set in ice and salt for 30-40 minutes, the traditional hand-churned way. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Serve topped with pistachios. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, sugar, cardamom, pistachios, almonds, rose water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook rice in milk for 45 minutes on low heat, stirring. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar and cardamom and cook 10 minutes. Step 4: Finish with rose water and nuts. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: ash gourd, sugar, lime water, rose water, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Peel ash gourd, cut into pieces and prick; soak in lime water for 6 hours and rinse. Step 2: Boil in water for 10 minutes. Step 3: Cook in sugar syrup for 40 minutes until translucent; add rose water and dry. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: pheni, milk, sugar, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Warm milk with sugar and cardamom. Step 2: Pour over crushed pheni and let it soak 2 minutes. Step 3: Eat at sehri in Ramadan. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, ghee, sugar, gond, almonds, walnuts, pistachios, coconut, melon seeds, cardamom, khoya
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry gond in ghee for 1-2 minutes until it puffs, then crush. Step 3: Roast wheat flour in ghee on low heat for 20-25 minutes until dark golden and fragrant. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add crushed nuts, coconut, melon seeds, khoya and cardamom and roast 5 minutes more. Step 5: Cool for 10 minutes, mix in powdered sugar and gond. Step 6: Press into round pinnis while warm; store in a tin for the winter. Step 7: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 8: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: pistachios, milk powder, sugar, ghee, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Grind pistachios coarsely. Step 3: Make a one-string sugar syrup for 6 minutes, add milk powder, pistachios and ghee and stir 5 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Set in a tray for 2 hours and cut. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: pistachios, milk, sugar, ghee, khoya, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak and peel pistachios, grind to a coarse paste. Add water only a little at a time, just enough to get a smooth paste. Step 3: Cook in ghee 5 minutes, add milk and cook until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add sugar, khoya and cardamom and stir 10 minutes until it leaves the pan. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, sugar, pistachios, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Reduce milk for 60 minutes. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Add sugar, ground pistachios and cardamom. Step 4: Freeze in moulds for 8 hours. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, sugar, cardamom, pistachios, rose water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make a thin kheer of rice and milk for 40 minutes. Step 3: Separately reduce milk to rabri with its cream layers for 1 hour. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Combine, add sugar, rose water and pistachios and chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, evaporated milk, cardamom pods, small, milk powder, all-purpose flour, baking powder, pinch fine ground cardamom powder, ghee, neutral oil, egg, finely chopped pistachios, finely chopped blanched almonds, saffron strands or dried edible rose petals
Instructions: Step 1: Place the ingredients listed under ‘Milk’ in a large, wide (11-13”) nonstick pan. Turn the heat on to medium-high and stir to mix. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring occasionally at first, and more frequently as it begins heating up. This takes about 13 minutes, depending on your heat. Keep scraping the sides and bottom of the pot as you go. Step 2: Once the milk comes to light boil, reduce the heat to low-medium and allow the milk to gently simmer. Stir occasionally as you proceed with the next step. If any brown film rises to the surface, scoop it out with a mini strainer. Step 3: Meanwhile, place the whole milk powder, flour, baking powder, and cardamom powder in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine. In another small bowl, mix the ghee and oil. Step 4: Using your hands, gradually add the ghee and oil mixture to the dry ingredients, stirring and rubbing the ghee into the dry mixture as you go. Ensure each addition is fully incorporated before adding more. Step 5: Slowly pour in the whisked egg and continue mixing with your hands. At first, the crumbly dough will become somewhat of a sticky mass, but as you continue to mix for 1-2 minutes, it’ll start coming together. It should form into a sticky, cohesive ball that's moist with the egg and ghee/oil. (Wipe your hands of excess mixture and add to the ball.). Step 6: Wash your hands, then oil your palms lightly. Working quickly to prevent the dough from drying out, scoop around 1 teaspoon (5-7g) of dough and roll it into a smooth ball, ensuring there are no cracks on the surface. Optional for flatter balls - Gently press it between your palms to flatten to a thick disc shape. Place the dough ball on a plate and cover with a lid or cling wrap to prevent it from drying out. Repeat until you’ve used up the remaining mixture. (Forms 25-30 dough balls.). Step 7: Adjust heat so that the milk is at a steady, gentle simmer-neither too vigorous nor completely still (210°F/99°C). (Heat too high = quick cooking on the outside, uncooked centers on the inside. Heat too low = more chances of disintegration.) Carefully drop all the dough balls at the same time into the gently simmering milk. Without stirring, cover the pot and allow them to gently simmer on medium heat for 4-5 minutes. They'll begin to puff up. Step 8: Uncover the pot and gently flip the dough balls using a ladle or a spoon (some of them may have naturally flipped/rotated). You can also tilt or move the pan around to gently stir without actually stirring. Cover again and let them gently simmer (low-medium heat) for another 12-14 minutes. No need to uncover/stir throughout. Once cooked, to prevent any milk from sticking or scorching, gently scrape the bottom. Step 9: Remove from heat and let the Ras Malai rest, covered, for at least 10 minutes.(To check for doneness, remove one dough ball and test its texture - it should be spongy, fully cooked through. Don’t worry about any egginess, it’ll completely go away once cool.). Step 10: Allow to cool to room temperature, then transfer to a lidded serving dish. Step 11: Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight (this is key for developing flavor and texture!). Garnish with nuts and saffron strands/rose petals (if using) just before serving. Serve chilled.

Ingredient Names: milk, lemon juice, sugar, cardamom, rose water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Curdle boiled milk with lemon, strain and knead the chenna 10 minutes. Step 3: Roll smooth balls. Step 4: Boil in thin sugar syrup covered for 15-18 minutes until doubled. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 5: Cool in the syrup with rose water. Step 6: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sugar, jaggery, sesame seeds, ghee, rose water
Instructions: Step 1: Cook sugar and jaggery syrup to hard ball stage in 10 minutes. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 2: Pull and stretch until pale, shape small discs and coat with roasted sesame. Step 3: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 4: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, sago pearls, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Soak sago 1 hour and cook in milk 15 minutes until transparent. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: vermicelli, sugar, ghee, cardamom, food colour, raisins, almonds, khoya
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry vermicelli in ghee 3 minutes until golden. Step 3: Add water, colour and sugar and cook until dry. Step 4: Add khoya, nuts and raisins and steam 5 minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, vermicelli, ghee, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 2: Fry vermicelli in ghee 3 minutes and cook in milk for 10 minutes. Step 3: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 5: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, sugar, khoya, almonds, pistachios, saffron, kewra water, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook soaked broken rice in milk for 45 minutes on low heat until creamy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar, khoya and saffron and cook 10 minutes. Step 4: Add kewra, cardamom and nuts and chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: bread slices, ghee, milk, sugar, khoya, cardamom, saffron, pistachios, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry bread triangles in ghee for 2 minutes each side and dip in sugar syrup. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 3: Reduce milk with khoya, sugar and saffron for 30 minutes into rabri. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Pour rabri over the bread and top with nuts. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sweet potato, milk, sugar, ghee, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Boil and mash the sweet potatoes. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sweet potato, jaggery, ghee, cardamom, almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil and mash sweet potatoes. Step 3: Cook in ghee 10 minutes, add gur and cardamom and cook 10 minutes. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ghee, sugar, milk, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with ghee, sugar and milk. Step 2: Roll thick and cut into diamonds. Step 3: Fry on low heat for 10 minutes until crisp. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice, sugar, cardamom, rose water, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook rice in milk for 40 minutes until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 3: Add sugar, cardamom and rose water. Step 4: Serve warm with pistachios. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, heavy whipping cream, butter, ghee, or oil, green cardamom pods, pakistani or indian vermicelli, blanched, slivered almonds, rose water or kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: (Optional) If using dried dates or other optional add-ins, prepare them first. Step 2: In a medium nonstick Dutch oven or large nonstick saucepan, bring milk and heavy whipping cream to a boil. (Cover to encourage faster boiling.) Reduce to a simmer (medium heat on my stove) and stir occasionally so the milk doesn’t stick to the bottom. Proceed to next step, being careful not to let the milk boil over. Step 3: Meanwhile, heat a medium to large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Melt butter/ghee or heat oil and add the cardamom and vermicelli. Toast, stirring often, for 5-6 minutes, until the vermicelli deepens in color and becomes aromatic. Turn off the heat. Step 4: Add the toasted vermicelli, optional add-ins, and sugar to the simmering milk. Step 5: Raise the heat to high to bring to a boil. Cook, stirring constantly, for 5-6 minutes. As soon as it starts to thicken, remove from heat. (It should be runnier than you prefer since it thickens greatly as it cools.) Once it settles down, the surface should still be largely milky with some vermicelli resting on top. Step 6: Add the slivered almonds and rose/kewra water and stir. Serve hot or chilled (my preferred way). Garnish with additional nuts, if desired.

Ingredient Names: semolina, sugar, ghee, milk, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, saffron
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast semolina in ghee for 12-15 minutes until golden. Step 3: Add milk and sugar and stir for 15 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add saffron and cardamom and cook 5 minutes until ghee separates; top with nuts. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, rice flour, sugar, cardamom, saffron, almonds, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Dissolve rice flour in cold milk. Step 3: Boil remaining milk, add sugar, cardamom and saffron. Step 4: Stir in the rice flour paste and cook for 10 minutes on low heat until thick. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Pour into clay bowls, chill 2 hours and top with nuts. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: flour, ghee, sugar, cardamom, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with ghee into a stiff dough, roll seven thin layers with ghee between. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Cut into rounds and fry on low heat until crisp. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Dip in thick sugar syrup. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: gram flour, all-purpose flour, ghee, sugar, cardamom, pistachios
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast both flours in ghee on low heat for 15 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Cook sugar syrup to hard ball stage for 12 minutes and pull it. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 4: Fold in the warm flour until thin flakes form; press and cut. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: semolina, carrot, sugar, ghee, milk, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Grate carrots and cook for 15 minutes; roast semolina separately for 10 minutes. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: semolina, sugar, ghee, coconut, cardamom, raisins, milk
Instructions: Step 1: Roast sooji in ghee 8 minutes until golden. Step 2: Add coconut, powdered sugar and cardamom. Step 3: Sprinkle a little warm milk, shape ladoos and press a raisin in each. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: milk, semolina, sugar, cardamom, almonds, raisins
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast sooji lightly in ghee. Step 3: Add boiling milk and stir 8 minutes until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add sugar, cardamom, nuts and raisins. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: semolina, sugar, ghee, cardamom, almonds, raisins
Instructions: Step 1: Roast semolina in ghee on low heat for 10-12 minutes until golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 2: Cook on low heat in ghee, stirring continuously so nothing sticks, until the mixture comes together. Step 3: Add sugar (or the milk-sugar mix) and cardamom and keep stirring for 10-15 minutes until glossy. Step 4: Cook until the ghee starts to separate from the sides, about 5 more minutes. Step 5: Garnish with sliced nuts and serve warm. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: sesame seeds, jaggery, ghee, cardamom
Instructions: Step 1: Dry roast sesame seeds for 4 minutes. Step 2: Melt jaggery with ghee for 4 minutes, add sesame and cardamom. Step 3: Shape quickly into ladoos; a winter sweet. Step 4: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 5: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: flour, ghee, yogurt, baking powder, sugar, honey, cardamom, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead flour with ghee, yogurt and baking powder into a stiff dough and rest 30 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Shape small thick rounds and fry on low heat 10 minutes until golden and crisp inside. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Dip in a thick sugar-honey syrup with cardamom and let set. The syrup is ready when a drop between two fingers feels slightly sticky. Step 5: Garnish with sliced almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled as you like. Step 6: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: full cream milk, basmati rice, saffron, sugar, cardamom, almonds, pistachios, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Step 3: Cook crushed rice in milk 45 minutes and add soaked saffron. Step 4: Add sugar and crushed cardamom and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 5: Add a few drops of kewra water and sliced nuts. Step 6: Chill in clay bowls for 2 hours and serve. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 7: Store covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.

Ingredient Names: aged long-grain basmati rice, ghee, green cardamom pods, water, milk, raw cane sugar, yellow or orange food color, kosher salt, orange blossom water or kewra essence, malai, slivered almonds
Instructions: Step 1: Place the rice in a bowl and thoroughly wash until the water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes, then strain. Step 2: Parboil the rice: Place a medium pot or nonstick Dutch Oven over high heat and bring 5 cups (1.25 quarts) of water to a rolling boil. (Cover the pot with a lid to speed this up.). Step 3: Add the rice and bring it back up to a boil. Once it comes to a boil again, boil for 6 minutes and 30 seconds (no more than 7 minutes), or until the rice is fully cooked but has a slight bite to it. Instead of breaking into pieces, it should get slightly mushy when pressed between your fingers. Drain and set aside. Step 4: Heat a medium nonstick Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once hot, heat ghee and add the cardamom pods. Stir for a few seconds to infuse the oil. Then add the sugar, water, food coloring, and salt. Stir and allow the sugar to completely dissolve (1-2 minutes). Add the milk and bring the mixture to a simmer (~1-2 minutes). The thickness of your pot will affect this timing. You’re looking to dissolve the sugar, but not thicken the syrup. Step 5: Add the rice and use a rice paddle to fold very gently until all the rice is coated evenly in sugar syrup. (Careful here not to break the rice. If you can, lift the pot and swirl around to mix.) Bring to a gentle boil and allow to simmer, undisturbed, for 2 minutes, until the sugar syrup has reduced and the rice is no longer watery. Sprinkle in orange blossom/kewra water, if using. Step 6: Layer the lid with a kitchen cloth (or aluminum foil) and seal tightly to contain the steam. At first, keep the pan on medium heat to allow to build steam for 1-2 minutes. You’ll start to feel the steam escaping the sides of the pot. Then turn down to the lowest heat and allow it to cook in its steam (‘dum’) for 10-15 minutes. The liquid should be fully absorbed and the rice fully cooked. Step 7: Turn off the heat and allow it to rest with the lid on for another 10 minutes. Serve with malai (cream), if desired.

Ingredient Names: eggs, potato, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil eggs 10 minutes and peel. Put the boiled eggs in cold water straight away so they peel easily. Step 3: Cook onion, tomato and spices for 10 minutes. Step 4: Add potato cubes and water and cook 15 minutes. Step 5: Add halved eggs and simmer 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve hot with paratha or bread and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: eggs, finely chopped cilantro, kosher salt, neutral oil, yellow onion, garlic cloves, serrano or jalapeno pepper, red chili powder or cayenne, coriander powder, cumin powder, black pepper, turmeric powder, vine or roma tomato
Instructions: Step 1: Crack the eggs in a medium bowl and whisk until uniform. Add the cilantro and ½ tsp of the salt and whisk again to combine. Step 2: Heat oil in a medium nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until soft and translucent. Step 3: Add garlic, green chili, and remaining ¼ tsp salt. Continue to sauté for another 2 minutes, until the onions start to turn golden on some edges. No need to brown the onions. Step 4: Reduce the heat to low. Add the spices (red chili, coriander powder, cumin powder, black pepper, and turmeric) and stir for 1 minute to allow them to bloom. Step 5: Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the tomato and sauté for a minute, until softened. Step 6: Pour the whisked eggs into the onions. Stir constantly until set but still glossy, about 2 minutes. Turn off the heat and garnish with more cilantro, if desired. Serve immediately with any type of bread, paratha, or roti.

Ingredient Names: eggs, green peas, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in water, peel and make small slits. Put the boiled eggs in cold water straight away so they peel easily. Step 3: Fry chopped onion for 6 minutes, add ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato, red chili powder, turmeric and salt and cook 8 minutes. Step 5: Add the peas and 1.5 cups water and cook 10 minutes. Step 6: Add the halved eggs and simmer 3 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Sprinkle garam masala and serve with roti.

Ingredient Names: eggs, spinach, onion, garlic, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash the leafy greens in plenty of water to remove all grit. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash and chop the spinach finely. Step 3: Heat oil and fry chopped onion and garlic for 4 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the spinach and cook 8 minutes until all its water dries. Step 5: Add green chili, red chili powder, turmeric and salt. Step 6: Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble gently for 3 minutes. Step 7: Serve with paratha.

Ingredient Names: eggs, onion, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, cardamom, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add ginger garlic paste and fry 1 minute. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 8 minutes with the main ingredient added. Step 6: Use boiled, peeled and lightly fried eggs. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: eggs, capsicum, onion, tomato, black pepper, red chili flakes, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Chop the onion, capsicum and tomato. Step 2: Heat oil and fry the onion and capsicum for 3 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes. Step 4: Pour in the eggs beaten with black pepper, chili flakes and salt. Step 5: Scramble on low heat for 3 minutes until soft and just set. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve with toast or paratha.

Ingredient Names: eggs, tomato, onion, green chili, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin seeds, fresh coriander, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Chop the onion, tomatoes and green chili. Step 3: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds and fry the onion for 3 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the tomatoes, green chili, turmeric, red chili powder and salt and cook 5 minutes until soft and pulpy. Step 5: Make small wells in the masala and crack the eggs into them. Step 6: Cover and cook on low heat for 4 minutes until the whites set. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Garnish with coriander and serve with paratha.

Ingredient Names: eggs, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, peel, prick and fry for 2 minutes until golden. Put the boiled eggs in cold water straight away so they peel easily. Step 3: Fry onion for 8 minutes, add ginger garlic paste, tomato, yogurt and spices and bhuno 8 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 4: Add 1.5 cups water and simmer 8 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add eggs and cook 5 minutes; finish with garam masala and coriander. Step 6: Serve hot with paratha or bread and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: okra, eggs, onion, tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry the cut okra for 8 minutes. Step 3: Add onion, tomato, red chili, turmeric and salt and cook 5 minutes. Step 4: Add beaten eggs and stir 3 minutes. Step 5: Serve with roti.

Ingredient Names: eggs, cheddar cheese, black pepper, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper until frothy. Step 2: Melt butter in a non-stick pan on medium heat. Step 3: Pour in the eggs and cook 2 minutes, pulling the edges in, until almost set. Step 4: Sprinkle grated cheese on one half, fold over and cook 1 minute until the cheese melts. Step 5: Serve with toast and chai.

Ingredient Names: noodles, eggs, cabbage, carrot, spring onion, garlic, soy sauce, chili sauce, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the noodles for 4 minutes and drain. Step 3: Scramble the eggs in a hot wok and push to the side. Step 4: Stir fry garlic, cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes. Step 5: Add the noodles, soy sauce, chili sauce, black pepper and salt and toss everything together. Step 6: Finish with spring onion. Step 7: Serve hot with paratha or bread and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: eggs, butter, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Melt a teaspoon of butter in a small non-stick pan on medium heat. Step 2: Crack the eggs gently into the pan, keeping the yolks whole. Step 3: Cook for 2-3 minutes without touching until the white is set and the edges are lightly crisp; the yolk should stay runny. Step 4: Spoon a little hot butter over the white near the yolk to help it set. Step 5: Season with salt and black pepper and slide onto a plate. Step 6: Serve with toast or paratha and chai.

Ingredient Names: spring onion, eggs, green chili, red chili flakes, turmeric, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Chop the spring onions with their green tops. Step 2: Fry the white part of the spring onion 2 minutes, then the greens 2 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add beaten eggs with chili, turmeric and salt and scramble 3 minutes. Step 4: Serve with paratha.

Ingredient Names: eggs, onions slices, oil, turmeric powder, red chili flakes, red chili powder, salt, green chilies, tomato, coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Break 3 eggs in a bowl and set aside. Step 2: Add oil in a pan along with sliced onions. Saute the onions for 3 to 4 mins at medium flame, or until they turn translucent. Step 3: Add in your green chilies, spices. Saute for another 2 mins. Step 4: Add tomatoes and allow it to soften for 2 mins. Step 5: Add the eggs in the pan and let it sit for 2 mins before mixing with a spatula. Step 6: Cook the eggs for another 2 mins and add chopped coriander. Mix well. Step 7: Drain all the excess oil on a towel paper and serve the eggs with paratha or bread.

Ingredient Names: eggs, red chili powder, chaat masala, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and put them in cold water. Put the boiled eggs in cold water straight away so they peel easily. Step 2: Peel and prick each egg with a fork so the masala goes in. Step 3: Heat a little oil, add red chili powder, chaat masala, black pepper and salt. Step 4: Add the eggs and fry for 2 minutes, rolling them, until coated. Step 5: Serve as a snack with chai.

Ingredient Names: eggs, kosher salt, red chili powder, black pepper, yellow or red onion, roma tomato, serrano or, cilantro leaves, neutral oil, salted or unsalted butter
Instructions: Step 1: Crack the eggs into a medium bowl and season with the salt, red chili powder, and black pepper. Step 2: Place the onion, tomato, green chili pepper, and cilantro in a food processor. Pulse to chop just until the mixture is diced (you don’t want finely chopped or watery veggies (~10-12 pulses). You may have to stop to scrape the sides and redistribute the mixture. Step 3: Heat oil in a medium (~12”) nonstick skillet over med-high heat. Add the chopped vegetables mixture. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, until most of the water evaporates from the vegetables. Step 4: Using a rubber spatula, scoop out the vegetables from the pan and add to the eggs. (You don’t need to get every last bit of veggies.) Whisk everything until well combined. (For fluffier eggs, add 1 tbsp of water.). Step 5: If needed, increase heat back to med-high - getting the pan hot is important for crispier edges. Heat butter in the same pan and quickly swirl it around to sizzle and melt. Pour all the omelet mixture in the pan and spread it out evenly. Cook, tilting the pan and pushing the edges with a spatula to distribute the uncooked egg under the outer rim. Let the eggs cook until the edges set and the bottom develops golden brown spots, 2-3 minutes. (You want some browning on the underside before turning.). Step 6: Using the sharp edge of a large, flat spatula, divide the omelet into 3-4 portions (I do this roughly). Then turn each section over. Cook the other side for another 1-2 minutes until it's golden brown yet tender. Serve immediately with paratha or bread.

Ingredient Names: eggs, onion, green chili, red chili flakes, turmeric, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Slice 2 onions thinly. Step 3: Melt butter and fry the onions for 6 minutes until soft and light brown. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add green chili, chili flakes, turmeric and salt. Step 5: Pour in the beaten eggs and cook 3 minutes, stirring gently. Step 6: Serve with paratha and chai.

Ingredient Names: beef mince, eggs, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, green chili, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry chopped onion for 6 minutes, then add the mince and ginger garlic paste and fry 12 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add tomato, red chili powder, green chili and salt and cook until dry, about 8 minutes. Step 4: Sprinkle garam masala and spread the qeema evenly in the pan. Step 5: Make 4 wells and crack an egg into each. Step 6: Cover and cook on low heat for 4 minutes until the eggs set. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Serve with paratha.

Ingredient Names: toor dal, onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin seeds, dried red chili, green chili, ghee, salt, fresh coriander, tamarind
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the dal and soak for 30 minutes. Step 3: Boil with 3-4 cups water, turmeric, red chili, ginger and salt, skimming the foam, for 30 minutes until soft. Step 4: Fry sliced garlic, cumin seeds and dried red chilies in ghee for 1-2 minutes until the garlic is golden (tarka/baghaar). Instructions: Step 1: Place lentils in a small-medium bowl and fill with water. Use your hand to swirl the dal around until the water becomes murky. Tip the bowl to take out the excess water and repeat until the water runs clear. Remove any debris and strain the excess water. Step 2: In a medium pot, add dal along with 3 1/4 cups (~769 ml) of water. Bring this to a boil over medium-high/high heat. Once it comes to a boil, reduce the heat to low-medium so that it simmers. Use a slotted spoon to remove any white scum that rises to the top of the pan. Cover with the lid ajar. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes, until the dal has no bite to it and can easily be mashed. Top with 1/4 cup water if you feel the dal is getting too thick. Turn off the heat. Step 3: Add lentils along with 1 1/2 cups (355 ml) of water. Select Pressure Cook - Low setting and set the timer to 7 minutes. Manually release the pressure. Step 4: In a separate large pan, heat oil over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the cumin seeds and sauté for about 15 seconds. Add the onions and sauté until slightly golden, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and continue to sauté until the raw smell disappears (~30 seconds). Add the tomatoes, green chili pepper, and spice powders (cumin, coriander, red chili, turmeric) and salt. Cook until soft and you see the oil leaving the sides, about 3 minutes. Step 5: Stir the cooked dal into the tarka. Add 1 cup water (more or less), depending on how thick the dal got while cooking and how runny you like the consistency. Mix to combine. Step 6: Bring the dal to a simmer. Allow the dal to reduce and the flavors to meld for about 5 minutes, or until you achieve the desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt, if needed. Step 7: Add in the ghee or butter. If using fenugreek leaves, crush them between your hands and sprinkle into the dal. Turn off the heat. Add lemon juice, chopped cilantro, and garam masala, if using. Give it a stir. Step 8: Serve dal hot with rice, roti, naan or anything else your heart desires. I like to serve it with a mix of chopped onions, carrots, and cucumber on the side.

Instructions: Step 1: Place the dal(s) in a small bowl and wash thoroughly until the water runs clear. Soak in warm water for 30 minutes, up to 2 hours. The dal will have swelled up. Step 2: Rinse, drain, and place the dal in a stock pot or Dutch oven. Add the remaining ingredients under ‘For the Dal’ (stock, water, garlic, spices, and salt) and stir to mix. Bring the dal to a boil over high heat, covering with a lid to make it boil faster. Use a slotted spoon to skim off any scum that rises to the surface. Step 3: Reduce the heat to medium/medium-high, cover with the lid ajar, and simmer (gentle boil) for 25-30 minutes, until tender. At this point, the water content will have reduced to about half of its original volume, and you’ll be able to see the dal on the surface. The dal will mush easily when pressed between your fingers. Step 4: Turn off the heat. Blend around half to ¾ of the dal using an immersion handheld blender. (Alternatively, transfer and blend half of the dal in a food processor using the pulse function.) You don’t want a completely smooth puree, but you want it to be mostly smooth, without too many visible granules of dal. If the dal is still too runny – it should be soupy, but not runny – then continue to simmer until thickened to your liking. Step 5: Stir in the cream (or milk). Taste and adjust salt, if needed, adding more salt to taste, or additional water if too much salt. At this point, the dal will be a soupy consistency, but not runny. Step 6: Turn on the low-medium and allow the dal to simmer and thicken while you proceed with the Tarka. Stir occasionally to make sure it’s not sticking to the bottom of the pot. Step 7: Heat oil and ghee in a small skillet over medium heat. Once hot, add the cumin seeds and whole dried chilies (if using). Sauté for 1 minute, until the cumin seeds sizzle. Add the garlic and green chili pepper and sauté for another minute, until the garlic turns golden brown around the edges and the green chili blisters (the longer it cooks, the less sharp its bite). Turn off the heat and sprinkle in the Kashmiri Chili or paprika. It’ll bloom in the hot oil. Step 8: Pour the Tarka over the gently simmering dal. (To capture any remaining tarka, use a ladle to pour some dal into the tarka pan, then pour everything back into the dal.) Garnish with garam masala and cilantro, and sprinkle the lemon juice on top. Stir gently, so the tarka remains on top. Serve with Basmati Rice, Kachumber Salad, and lemon wedges.
