Give it a good stir. Step 7: Heat the oil in a small frying pan and add the sliced onion, garlic, curry leaves, dried red chillies and cumin seeds. Step 8: When the onions have turned a beautiful brown then pour the baghaar/tadka/tempering over the boiled lentils and cover. Step 9: Serve with rice or roti.

Step 3: Boil with turmeric and salt on low heat for 20 minutes so the grains stay separate. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Fry onion, garlic and ginger in ghee for 5 minutes, add chili flakes and cumin. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 5: Fold in the dal and cook on low heat for 5 minutes without mashing. Step 6: Finish with lemon juice, green chili, ginger julienne and coriander. Step 7: Taste and adjust salt and serve hot with plain boiled rice or chapati, with achaar and sliced onion. Ingredient Names: pearl millet, moong dal, ghee, cumin seeds, salt, water
Instructions: Step 1: Soak 1 cup pearl millet overnight, drain and pound lightly in a mortar to loosen the husk; wash away the husk. Step 2: Wash half a cup moong dal. Step 3: Put the millet and dal in a heavy pot with 5 cups of water and salt. Step 4: Cook on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often and adding hot water when needed, until soft and porridge-like. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Heat 2 tablespoons ghee and crackle cumin seeds for 30 seconds. Step 6: Pour the tarka over the khichdi and serve hot with buttermilk (chhachh), as eaten in Thar. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 7: Dal thickens in the fridge; add a little hot water when reheating. Keeps for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: mutton, chickpeas, potato, onion, tomato, turmeric, salt, black pepper, bread
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the chickpeas overnight. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Put the mutton, chickpeas, sliced onion, turmeric, salt and 8 cups water in a pot and cook on low heat for 2 hours. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add cubed potatoes and tomatoes and cook 25 minutes. Step 5: Pour the broth over torn bread in bowls and eat it first. Step 6: Then mash the meat, chickpeas and potatoes together, season with black pepper and eat as the second course. Step 7: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, potato, eggplant, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cube the potatoes and eggplant. Step 3: Heat oil and fry sliced onion for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton with ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the potato and eggplant, cover and cook for 15 minutes until soft. Step 8: Finish with garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and serve with roti. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, onion, garlic, salt, black pepper, green chili, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix mutton mince with grated onion (squeezed), crushed garlic, green chili, finely chopped dumba fat, salt and black pepper. Step 3: Knead 5 minutes and chill 30 minutes. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Shape on skewers. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 10 minutes, turning. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Serve with naan and onion. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, dumba fat, salt, black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the mutton into large chunks, keeping some fat on. Step 2: Season only with salt and rest 30 minutes. Step 3: Thread on long skewers with pieces of dumba fat between the meat. Step 4: Grill over hot coals for 12-15 minutes, turning often, until browned outside and juicy inside. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 5: Sprinkle black pepper and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, green chili, salt, black pepper, butter

Instructions: Step 1: Wash the mutton and chop the onion, tomato and garlic. Step 2: Heat oil, fry the onion for 6 minutes, add mutton and garlic and fry 10 minutes. Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Slice 4 large onions thinly; wash and drain 1 kg mutton. Step 3: Fry the onions in ghee on medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until deep brown (bhugal) but not burnt. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton and crushed garlic and fry for 15 minutes until the meat turns dark. Step 5: Add whisked yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno 5 minutes. Ingredient Names: goat liver, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin seeds, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash and cube the liver. Step 3: Fry onion and cumin 4 minutes, add ginger garlic and the liver and fry 5 minutes on high. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato and spices and cook 6 minutes only; overcooking makes liver hard. Step 5: Finish with green chili and pepper. Step 6: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: goat kidney, goat heart, goat brain, testicles, onion, tomato, green chili, ginger garlic paste, red chili flakes, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, garam masala, butter, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil kidney and heart for 20 minutes and cut small; blanch brain 5 minutes. Step 3: Heat oil and butter on a big tawa and fry onion and ginger garlic 4 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add meats, tomato, green chili and spices and chop with two steel spatulas for 12 minutes (the kata-kat sound). Step 5: Fold in the brain at the end, finish with garam masala and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, kewra water, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry sliced onion in ghee for 12 minutes, remove and crush with yogurt. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Fry whole spices and mutton with ginger garlic for 10 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste and powdered spices and bhuno 10 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Add water and cook on low for 60 minutes until ghee floats; finish with kewra. Step 6: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, bitter gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, fennel seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Scrape and slice the karela, rub with salt and rest 30 minutes, then squeeze out the bitter water and fry for 8 minutes. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the bitter gourd, cover and cook for 20 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, mutton fat, yogurt, cardamom, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, mustard oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Pound boneless mutton with mutton fat on a stone with a wooden mallet for 20 minutes into a very smooth paste, adding cardamom and salt. Step 3: Shape into large, smooth balls with wet hands. Step 4: Whisk yogurt with fennel powder, dried ginger powder and a little water. Step 5: Heat mustard oil, add the yogurt and bring it to a boil, stirring continuously so it does not split. Step 6: Add the meatballs and simmer for 40 minutes until cooked through and the gravy is creamy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Serve with plain rice as the last dish of a wazwan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton ribs, milk, fennel seeds, dried ginger, cardamom, cloves, yogurt, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the ribs into pairs. Step 2: Simmer them in milk with fennel seeds, dried ginger, cardamom, cloves and salt for 45 minutes until tender and the milk has reduced. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Drain and cool the ribs. Step 4: Whisk yogurt with a little salt and coat the ribs. Step 5: Fry in hot ghee for 4 minutes until golden and crisp; serve as a wazwan starter. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton tripe, dried fenugreek, fennel seeds, dried ginger, mustard oil, kashmiri chili, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Clean the tripe very well in several changes of water. Step 2: Boil it with salt for 1 hour until soft, then chop finely. Step 3: Heat mustard oil until it smokes, then cool slightly. Step 4: Add the tripe, lots of dried methi, fennel seeds, dried ginger, kashmiri chili and salt. Step 5: Cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring, until dry and fragrant; serve with rice. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, yogurt, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, dried mint, mustard oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the mutton with cardamom, cloves, bay leaf and salt in 4 cups water for 40 minutes. Step 3: Whisk yogurt with fennel and dried ginger powder. Step 4: Heat mustard oil, add the yogurt and stir constantly for 8 minutes until it thickens without splitting. Step 5: Add the mutton and its stock and simmer 20 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Finish with dried mint and serve with rice. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, mutton fat, kashmiri chili, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom, onion, mustard oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Pound mutton mince with fat until smooth and shape large meatballs. Step 3: Heat mustard oil and fry onion paste with kashmiri chili for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add water, fennel powder, dried ginger, cardamom and salt and boil. Step 5: Add the meatballs and simmer 40 minutes in the red gravy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve with rice. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, turnip, onion, yogurt, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, saffron, cardamom, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Peel the turnips, cut into large pieces and lightly fry them in ghee for 5 minutes; keep aside. Step 3: In the same ghee brown the mutton with sliced onion and cardamom for 12 minutes. Step 4: Add whisked yogurt, fennel powder, dried ginger powder and salt and cook 5 minutes, stirring. Step 5: Add the turnips, saffron and 3 cups of water. Step 6: Seal the pot with dough and cook overnight on the lowest possible heat for 6-8 hours. Step 7: Serve hot in the morning with rice or bread. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: lamb ribs, milk, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the lamb ribs into pairs and wash. Step 2: Put them in a pot with milk, a little water, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom and salt. Step 3: Simmer on low heat for 60 minutes until the meat is tender and the milk has almost dried; stir now and then so it does not catch. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Lift out the ribs and let them dry for 10 minutes. Step 5: Heat ghee in a wide pan and fry the ribs for 6-8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden on both sides. Step 6: Serve hot as a starter with rice. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: whole lamb, basmati rice, salt, black pepper, garlic, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean a whole lamb and rub inside and out with salt, garlic and black pepper. Step 3: Fill the cavity with parboiled seasoned rice and pieces of dumba fat, then sew it closed. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 4: Heat stones in a fire, line a pit (khaddi) with them and lower the lamb in. Step 5: Cover the pit and cook underground for 4-6 hours until the meat is very soft. Step 6: Serve the lamb with the rice in large platters for a gathering. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: beef boti, a medium onion, garlic paste, ginger, cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, black pepper, black cardamoms, ts salt, chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, yogurt - whipped and at room temp, green chilies & cilantro for garnishing, neutral oil for cooking
Instructions: Step 1: Heat a very generous glug of oil in a pot or pressure cooker, add sliced onion. Step 2: Fry till the edges are golden. Step 3: Put the beef in the pot, saute and add the ginger and garlic. Step 4: Add the whole spices, the red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Step 5: Cook till tender - for a pressure cooker add about a cup of hot water and cook till the meat is tender. For a regular pot add about a cup and a half, bring to a boil and simmer for 50 minutes to an hour until tender. Keep an eye on water levels to prevent burning! Step 6: Turn the heat up and dry up the water, when the masala is at the "right" level the oil will rise above the spice paste. Step 7: At that point stir in the yogurt, the oil will quickly rise to the top. Step 8: Add diced chillies (according to taste), a handful of cilantro, black pepper and garam masala powder. Step 9: Give it a quick whirl and eat with roti!

Ingredient Names: lamb, dumba fat, tomato, green chili, salt, black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the lamb into small pieces and dice the dumba fat. Step 3: Render the fat in a karahi on medium heat for 5 minutes. Step 4: Add the lamb and salt, cover and cook for 35 minutes in its own juices. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add tomatoes and bhuno on high heat for 10 minutes until thick. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Finish with black pepper and green chilies and serve with naan. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Add the purslane (kulfa) and cook for 12 minutes. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, ivy gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Slice the kundru lengthwise. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the ivy gourd, cover and cook for 15 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, ghee, wheat flour, garam masala, green chili, ginger julienne
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Put mutton, sliced onion, ginger garlic paste, spices and ghee into a clay kunna (or heavy pot). Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Add water to cover, seal the lid with dough and cook on very low heat for 3 hours. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Open, stir in wheat flour slurry and cook 10 minutes until the gravy turns thick. Step 5: Sprinkle garam masala, green chili and ginger and serve with tandoori roti. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: lamb leg, salt, black pepper, garlic, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make deep cuts in the lamb leg. Step 3: Rub generously with salt, crushed garlic and black pepper, pushing it into the cuts. Step 4: Rest for 1 hour. Step 5: Thread on a wooden skewer and roast slowly beside an open fire for 2-3 hours, turning, until the fat drips and the outside is crisp. Step 6: Slice and serve with naan. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton liver, gram flour, carom seeds, red chili powder, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, chaat masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean the kaleji and cut into thin slices. Step 3: Marinate with ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili and salt for 20 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Make a thick batter of gram flour, carom seeds and water. Step 5: Dip the slices in the batter and fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes until crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 6: Sprinkle chaat masala and serve hot. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: lamb ribs, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, raw papaya paste
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the lamb ribs into pieces (or make deep cuts in larger pieces). Step 3: Mix all the marinade ingredients and rub well into the meat. Step 4: Marinate for 6 hours or overnight in the fridge. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 5: Thread onto skewers. Step 6: Grill over hot coals for 18-25 minutes, turning and basting with oil, until charred at the edges. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 7: Give a coal smoke (dhuwan) for 2 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and serve with naan and raita. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: whole lamb, salt, onion, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Step 2: Salt the whole lamb heavily inside and out. Step 3: Hang it in the dry, cold open air for 2-3 months of winter until fully dried. Step 4: Before eating, wash, cut and boil the dried meat for 2 hours. Step 5: Fry with onion in dumba fat for 10 minutes, or cook it into pulao. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 6: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, chana dal, bottle gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak chana dal 1 hour; peel and cube the lauki. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry onion, add mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry 10 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato, red chili, turmeric and salt and cook with water for 40 minutes. Step 5: Add the chana dal and more water and cook 25 minutes. Step 6: Add the lauki and cook 15 minutes until soft. Step 7: Sprinkle garam masala and serve with roti. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.
