Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add the spinach and half a cup of water, cover and cook on low heat for 24 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Uncover, add garam masala and green chili and dry the masala for 3 minutes; serve with chapati. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, capsicum, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Deseed the capsicum and cut into squares. Step 3: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and chopped onion and fry for 7 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton mince and ginger garlic paste and fry for 12 minutes, breaking lumps, until the water dries. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno 6 minutes until oil shows. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add the capsicum and half a cup of water, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Uncover, add garam masala and green chili and dry the masala for 3 minutes; serve with chapati. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf, kewra water, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 60 minutes. Step 6: Keep the gravy medium-thick with a layer of ghee on top. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: boneless mutton, cream, yogurt, egg, white pepper, cardamom, onion, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a clay handi or heavy pot and fry chopped onion for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the boneless mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add a little water, cover and cook for 45 minutes until tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Whisk cream, yogurt and an egg together and cook on very low heat for 8 minutes so it turns silky. Step 6: Cook uncovered for 3 minutes until thick, sprinkle garam masala and coriander. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 7: Serve in the handi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, cream, egg, cashews, ginger garlic paste, white pepper, green chili, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Grind the mutton mince twice with cashews, cream, egg, ginger garlic paste, white pepper, green chili and salt until silky. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Chill for 30 minutes. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Shape on skewers with wet hands. Step 5: Grill over coals for 12 minutes, basting with butter. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Serve with mint chutney and naan. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, yogurt, kashmiri chili, fennel powder, dried ginger, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, asafoetida, mustard oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat mustard oil until it smokes, cool slightly and add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and a pinch of asafoetida. Step 3: Add the mutton and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until browned. Step 4: Add whisked yogurt little by little, stirring, then kashmiri chili mixed in water, fennel powder and dried ginger. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 60 minutes until tender and the gravy is deep red. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve with plain rice. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, mutton fat, onion, green chili, ginger garlic paste, fresh coriander, roasted gram flour, garam masala, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mince the mutton mince twice for a smooth texture. Step 3: Finely chop the onion and squeeze out all its water in a cloth. Step 4: Mix everything well and knead for 5 minutes, then chill for 1 hour so it holds on the skewer. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Wet your hands and press the mixture around flat skewers. Step 6: Grill over glowing coals for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes and brushing with butter or fat. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 7: Serve with paratha, onion rings, lemon and green chutney. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, chana dal, onion, ginger, garlic, dried red chili, whole spices, egg, mint leaves, green chili, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Put the mutton, soaked chana dal, onion, ginger, garlic, dried red chilies, whole spices and salt in a pot with 3 cups water. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Cook covered for 45-60 minutes until the meat and dal are completely soft, then dry off any water on high heat for 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Cool and grind into a smooth dough. Step 5: Mix in chopped mint, green chili, coriander and an egg (or potato for the vegetable version). Step 6: Shape into round flat kebabs, dip in beaten egg and shallow fry for 2-3 minutes each side. Step 7: Serve with green chutney or in a bun kebab; they freeze well for Ramadan. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, tomato, dumba fat, green chili, black pepper, ginger, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil and fat in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the mutton and fry for 8 minutes until sealed. Step 4: Cover and cook on medium heat for 35 minutes until the mutton is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Cook only with dumba fat, tomatoes and salt for 10 minutes, then add black pepper and green chili. Step 6: Keep cooking on high heat, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until the masala coats the meat and oil floats. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander, ginger julienne and green chili and serve straight from the karahi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton leg, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, black pepper, chaat masala, red chili flakes, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make deep cuts on the mutton leg. Step 3: Mix yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, black pepper, red chili flakes and salt and rub it deep into the cuts; marinate overnight in the fridge. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Place the leg in a steamer (or on a rack in a covered pot with water below) and steam for 2 hours until very tender. Step 5: Heat oil in a wide pan and shallow fry the steamed leg for 5 minutes, turning, until golden. Step 6: Sprinkle chaat masala and serve with naan, salad and raita. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, potato, carrot, onion, garlic, ginger, black pepper, whole spices, green chili, flour, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry onion lightly for 5 minutes, add mutton, ginger and garlic and fry 8 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add whole spices and 5 cups of water and cook covered for 60 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add potatoes, carrots and green chili and cook 20 minutes. Step 5: Thicken with flour slurry for 5 minutes and season with black pepper. Step 6: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: boneless mutton, raw papaya paste, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless mutton into pieces (or make deep cuts in larger pieces). Step 3: Mix all the marinade ingredients and rub well into the meat. Step 4: Marinate for 6 hours or overnight in the fridge. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 5: Thread onto skewers. Step 6: Grill over hot coals for 18-25 minutes, turning and basting with oil, until charred at the edges. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 7: Give a coal smoke (dhuwan) for 2 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and serve with naan and raita. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, yogurt, cream, ginger garlic paste, green chili, white pepper, black pepper, cumin powder, lemon juice, butter, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes until sealed. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Cover and cook on medium heat for 35 minutes until the mutton is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add whisked yogurt, cream, green chilies and white and black pepper and cook on low heat for 8 minutes until creamy (no tomato, no red chili). Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 6: Keep cooking on high heat, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until the masala coats the meat and oil floats. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander, ginger julienne and green chili and serve straight from the karahi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, tomato, ginger garlic paste, cumin seeds, roasted cumin, green chili, yogurt, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes until sealed. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Cover and cook on medium heat for 35 minutes until the mutton is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add a tablespoon of cumin seeds with tomatoes and yogurt and bhuno 10 minutes; finish with roasted cumin. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Keep cooking on high heat, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until the masala coats the meat and oil floats. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander, ginger julienne and green chili and serve straight from the karahi with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, dumba fat, tomato, green chili, salt, black pepper, ginger
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Melt dumba (sheep tail) fat in a karahi for 8 minutes. Step 3: Add mutton pieces with salt and cook covered on medium heat for 30-35 minutes in their own juices. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add whole tomatoes, cover 5 minutes and pull off the skins. Step 5: Bhuno on high heat for 8 minutes until the tomatoes melt and fat separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add green chili and plenty of crushed black pepper; no other spices. Step 7: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton with bones, tomato, garlic cloves, green chili whole, ghee, ginger, cumin powder, coriander powder, black pepper powder, black peppercorns, boiling water
Instructions: Step 1: In a large pan, heat some ghee. Once it's hot, add the mutton and fry it until light brown patches form. Next, add the minced ginger and garlic, cooking on medium-low heat for about a minute. Step 2: Add the green chili, whole garlic, and tomatoes. Stir well for one minute, and then add the spices and black peppercorns. Mix the ingredients for two minutes, then cover the pan and let the mixture cook on low heat for two minutes. Step 3: Use kitchen tongs to remove the tomato skins, then continue to mix for another two minutes on low heat. Pour in three cups of water and allow the meat to cook until tender, which may take 45 to 60 minutes. You may need to add an additional two cups of water while the meat is cooking. Step 4: Serve with homemade bread or rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton on bone, dumba fat, onion, tomato, salt, black pepper, water
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Put mutton, fat, whole onion and salt in a large pot with water. Step 3: Boil and skim the froth for 10 minutes. Step 4: Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until the meat is tender and the broth rich. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add tomato for the last 15 minutes and black pepper; serve with bread soaked in the broth. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, spinach, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop finely. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the spinach and cook uncovered so the greens melt into the masala for 12 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton leg, dumba fat, onion, salt, black pepper, garlic
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Rub mutton with salt, pepper and garlic. Step 3: Place in a heavy pot with dumba fat and whole onions. Step 4: Seal the lid with dough and cook on very low heat for 3-4 hours. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Serve the soft meat with its juices and naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, garlic, ginger, red chili powder, turmeric, dried ginger powder, fennel powder, wheat flour, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry sliced onion in ghee for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add mutton, crushed garlic and ginger and fry for 10 minutes on high heat. Step 4: Add red chili powder, turmeric, dried ginger powder, fennel powder and salt and fry 3 minutes. Step 5: Transfer to a clay pot (kunna), add 4 cups of water, cover and cook on very low heat for 2.5 hours until the meat falls off the bone. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Mix wheat flour with water into a smooth slurry and stir it in; simmer 10 minutes until the gravy thickens. Step 7: Serve hot with naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, mutton fat, salt, black pepper, tomato, green chili
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the mutton into cubes and dice the fat. Step 3: Render the fat, add the mutton and salt, cover and cook on low heat for 50 minutes in its own juices. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add tomato and green chili and cook 10 minutes. Step 5: Season with black pepper and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, yogurt, garlic paste, papaya paste, salt, black pepper, red chili flakes, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the mutton into cubes. Step 3: Mix yogurt, garlic paste, papaya paste and salt and marinate the mutton for 3 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 4: Thread on skewers, alternating with small pieces of dumba fat. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 12 minutes, turning, until browned. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Sprinkle black pepper and red chili flakes and serve with naan and onion. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, ash gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Peel the petha, remove seeds and cut into cubes. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry 10 minutes; add tomato, yogurt and spices and bhuno 8 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Add water, cover and cook 45 minutes until the mutton is nearly tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Add the ash gourd and cook for 18 minutes. Step 7: Finish with garam masala and green chili. Step 8: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, green beans, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the green beans into small pieces. Step 3: Heat oil and fry sliced onion for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton with ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the green beans, cover and cook for 12 minutes until soft. Step 8: Finish with garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and serve with roti. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, dumba fat, onion, tomato, salt, black pepper, garlic
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Put the mutton, diced dumba fat, sliced onion, tomato, garlic and salt in a heavy pot; no water is needed. Step 3: Seal the lid with dough or foil. Step 4: Cook on very low heat for 3 hours so the meat cooks in its own fat and juices. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Open, season with black pepper and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, dumba fat, tomato, green chili, salt, black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the mutton into small pieces. Step 3: Render dumba fat in a karahi and cook the mutton with salt, covered, for 35 minutes. Step 4: Add tomatoes and cook on high heat for 10 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 5: Finish with black pepper and green chilies and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton leg, raw papaya paste, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, garam masala, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make deep cuts in the leg and marinate with papaya, yogurt, ginger garlic and spices overnight. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Pressure cook or boil with a little water for 60 minutes until tender. Step 4: Roast in the oven at 200°C for 30 minutes, basting, until browned. Step 5: Serve with naan and salad. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, kidney beans, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak rajma overnight and boil 45 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt and all the powdered spices and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add water, cover and cook for 45 minutes until the mutton is nearly tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the kidney beans with enough water and simmer for 20-25 minutes until it is soft and the gravy is thick. Step 8: Temper with cumin fried in a little oil, add garam masala, green chili and coriander and serve hot. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton on bone, onion, tomato, salt, water, dumba fat
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and chop the tomatoes. Step 2: Put mutton, fat and salt in a big pot with water. Step 3: Cook on low heat for 2-3 hours until the meat is soft and the broth is clear and rich. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add tomato and onion in the last 20 minutes. Step 5: Serve with bread torn into the broth. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, spinach, mustard greens, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chopped spinach and mustard greens for 20 minutes, then blend coarsely. Step 3: Fry onion in ghee for 8 minutes, add mutton and ginger garlic paste and bhuno for 10 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 4: Add tomato and spices and cook for 5 minutes until oil separates. Step 5: Add water and cook covered for 50-60 minutes until the meat is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Add the greens and green chili and cook for 15 minutes until thick; finish with garam masala. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 7: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, white chickpeas, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander, cumin seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak chickpeas overnight and boil 40 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add tomato, yogurt and all the powdered spices and bhuno for 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add water, cover and cook for 45 minutes until the mutton is nearly tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add the white chickpeas with enough water and simmer for 20-25 minutes until it is soft and the gravy is thick. Step 8: Temper with cumin fried in a little oil, add garam masala, green chili and coriander and serve hot. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, ghee, wheat roti, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook mutton with onion, tomato, yogurt and spices in ghee for 15 minutes. Step 3: Add water and simmer for 60 minutes into a thin, rich shorba. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Tear stale rotis into a large deep platter. Step 5: Pour the hot shorba and meat over the rotis and let them soak for 5 minutes. Step 6: Serve from one plate so everyone eats together, the Saraiki way. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, mustard greens, spinach, onion, garlic, ginger, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, maize flour, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash and boil the mustard greens and spinach for 45 minutes and mash. Step 3: Fry onion, add mutton, garlic, ginger and spices and cook with water for 50 minutes until tender. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the greens and green chilies and mix. Step 5: Sprinkle maize flour and cook 15 minutes, stirring. Step 6: Top with ghee and serve with makai roti. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, broad beans, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: String the broad beans and cut into pieces. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the broad beans, cover and cook for 18 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, green chili, fresh coriander, yogurt, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Layer mutton, sliced onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, green chili, coriander and spices in a pot with oil and yogurt. Step 3: Cover and cook on very low heat for 60-75 minutes without adding water; the meat cooks in its own juices. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Uncover and bhuno for 5 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Finish with garam masala. Step 6: Garnish with ginger julienne and fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti and a fresh salad. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, turnip, onion, yogurt, fennel seeds, dried ginger, cardamom, saffron, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Lightly fry turnip pieces in ghee and keep aside. Step 3: Cook the mutton with onion, yogurt, fennel, dried ginger, cardamom and salt for 40 minutes. Step 4: Add the turnips and saffron. Step 5: Seal the pot and cook overnight on the lowest heat. Step 6: Serve in the morning with bread. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, yogurt, almonds, cashews, cream, saffron, cardamom, ginger garlic paste, white pepper, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Fry thinly sliced onions in ghee for 12 minutes until golden brown; take them out, crush with the yogurt and keep aside. Step 2: In the same ghee fry cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes. Step 4: Add the onion-yogurt paste with red chili and coriander powder and bhuno on low heat for 10 minutes until the ghee separates. Step 5: Add 1-2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 60 minutes. Step 6: Grind almonds and cashews into a paste and stir it in with cream and saffron. Step 7: Sprinkle kewra water or garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on dum and serve with naan or sheermal.

Ingredient Names: mutton, turnip, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the turnips and cut into large cubes. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the turnip, cover and cook for 25 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: onion, garlic, ginger, neutral oil, ghee, to, tomato, green chili pepper such as serrano, kosher salt, turmeric powder, green bell pepper, freshly, chaat masala, lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Using the pulse setting, finely chop onion, garlic, and ginger in a food processor, select the. Step 2: Sauté - More/High setting on the Instant Pot. Once Hot, add the oil, ghee, and chopped onion mixture and sauté until the onion is lightly golden, about 5-6 minutes. Step 3: While the onions are cooking, pulse to finely chop the tomato and green chili pepper in the food processor and set aside. Step 4: Add the goat meat to the Instant Pot and sauté for 4-5 minutes or until it changes color. Step 5: Add the chopped tomato mixture, apple cider vinegar, salt, and turmeric powder. Mix well to combine and submerge the meat in the liquid as much as possible. Step 6: Press the Cancel button to turn off the Instant Pot. Secure the lid and set the pressure release to Sealing. Select the Meat/Stew Pressure Cook setting and set the timer for 25 minutes on High pressure. Step 7: Once finished, use a tong or wooden spoon to move the Pressure Release to Venting to manually release the pressure. Step 8: Open the pot and select Sauté setting on More/High. Let the remaining moisture evaporate for about 5-6 minutes, then add the green bell pepper and sauté for another 5 minutes or until the curry cooks down and turns glossy. Stir only as necessary to allow the moisture to evaporate. Step 9: Press the cancel button to turn off the Instant Pot. Mix in the black pepper, chaat masala (if using) and lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt seasonings for spice and tartness. Serve with naan, paratha, roti, or rice.

Ingredient Names: lamb, dumba fat, tomato, green chili, salt, black pepper, ginger
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the lamb into small pieces with the bone and wash. Step 3: Melt the dumba fat in a karahi until it releases oil. Step 4: Add the lamb and salt, cover and cook on medium heat for 30 minutes in its own juices; no water or spices are added. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add whole tomatoes, cover for 5 minutes, then pull off the skins and mash the tomatoes into the meat. Step 6: Bhuno on high heat for 10 minutes until the gravy is thick and the fat floats. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 7: Finish with black pepper, ginger julienne and green chilies and serve with naan straight from the karahi. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, gram flour, tamarind, tomato, green chili, curry leaves, turmeric, red chili powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Boil 750 g mutton with salt, turmeric and 6 cups of water for 50 minutes until tender; keep the stock. Step 2: Roast 5 tablespoons gram flour in oil on low heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Add chopped tomato and green chilies and cook 3 minutes. Step 4: Whisk in the mutton stock little by little so the gram flour does not form lumps. Step 5: Add the mutton and red chili powder and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the kadhi is smooth and medium thick. Step 6: Add tamarind pulp and simmer 5 minutes more. Step 7: Temper curry leaves and cumin in hot oil, pour over and serve with plain rice. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, spinach, dill leaves, fenugreek leaves, onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and chop spinach, dill and fenugreek leaves; wash the mutton. Step 2: Heat oil and brown the mutton with sliced onion, garlic and ginger for 12 minutes. Step 3: Add chopped tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook 8 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 4: Add the greens and half a cup of water; they will release more water as they cook. Step 5: Cover and cook on low heat for 50 minutes until the mutton is tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Uncover, mash the greens lightly with a spoon and cook until most of the water dries. Step 7: Add slit green chilies and serve with phulka. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, dried fenugreek, garam masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash 1 kg mutton and drain well; slice 2 onions and chop 2 tomatoes. Step 2: Heat oil and fry the onions for 8 minutes until golden brown. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add the tomatoes, whisked yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 10 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Add 3 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 50 minutes until the mutton is tender and the gravy is medium thick. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Crush dried fenugreek between your palms and add it with the garam masala; simmer 3 minutes. Step 7: Serve hot with phulka or plain rice; teevan is a simple Sindhi everyday mutton salan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: beef stewing cubes / beef boti, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, green chili, garlic, ginger, water, sprigs curry leaves, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, oil, diced green chilies, minced cilantro, a squeeze of lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Combine all the ingredients in the tenderizing section in your pot of choice. Instant Pot: Manual for 22 minutes then natural releaseStovetop: Bring to a boil and simmer on medium low heat until the meat is tender - 50-60 minutes usually, but you don't need to do much for the most of it. Step 2: Crank up the heat and dry up your masala. Step 3: Once the masala starts sticking to the bottom of the pot then add your sauteeing ingredients and saute on medium high heat for a few minutes. Your meat and masala will darken and take on a rich aroma and flavour. Step 4: Psst feel free to add a splash of water here if you want a more wet masala! Step 5: Taste, adjust seasoning, then add a squeeze of lemon juice, your chilies and cilantro and.

Ingredient Names: stewing beef/ beef cubes, diced onion, garlic - if using fresh then, ginger - if using fresh then use, black peppers, cinnamon, cumin seeds, tomatoes, salt, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, tomato paste, garam masala, fistful of cilantro, green chilies, a squeeze of lemon juice, neutral oil like canola
Instructions: Step 1: Heat your oil in a large pot or wok. Step 2: Add the whole spices - cumin seeds, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick. Step 3: When they start to crackle then add the onions, saute till the edges turn golden brown. Step 4: Add the ginger and garlic, saute for a minute or two. Step 5: Now put in your powders/spices. Step 6: Cook till it forms a cohesive paste, adding a splash of water till necessary. It's done when a film of oil rises above the onion paste. Step 7: Throw in your tomatoes cooking on medium high heat until they soften, caramelize and become one with the spice paste. Step 8: Time to add your meat, make sure to brown it evenly, once it is browned on each side add two cups of very hot water and cover your pot. For instant pot add 1.5 cup water. Step 9: Bring the liquid in the pot to boil, then simmer for 45 minutes or an hour to get the meat super tender. If using the instant pot put it on manual (pressure) for 20 minutes then quick release. Step 10: Dry up the water in the pot till the masala looks decidedly jammy and add your tomato paste, now check for seasoning. Step 11: Add your garam masala, half your green chillies and half your cilantro. Give it a whirl and let it cook on low for 3-4 minutes then take it off the heat. Step 12: Squeeze over a little lemon juice if you want then top with remaining chillies and cilantro.

Ingredient Names: mutton liver, onion, tomato, green chili, ginger garlic paste, red chili flakes, black pepper, cumin seeds, lemon, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean the kaleji and cut into small pieces. Step 3: On a hot tawa fry onion for 3 minutes, add kaleji and ginger garlic paste and fry 5 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato, green chili and spices and cook 5 minutes (overcooking makes kaleji hard). Step 5: Squeeze lemon and serve with naan. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: boneless mutton, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili flakes, cumin seeds, black pepper, onion, tomato, green chili, lemon, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Marinate the mutton boti in yogurt, ginger garlic paste, chili flakes, cumin and salt for 2 hours. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 3: Cook on a hot tawa with oil, covered, for 25 minutes until tender. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Add sliced onion, tomato and green chili. Step 5: Toss on high heat for 5 minutes. Step 6: Season with black pepper, squeeze lemon and serve. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, ghee, roti, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook mutton with onion, tomato, yogurt and spices in ghee for 15 minutes. Step 3: Add water and simmer 60 minutes into a generous shorba. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Tear rotis into a deep dish and pour the shorba and meat over; rest 5 minutes and serve, a Sunnah dish loved in Ramadan. Step 5: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: mutton, round gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the tinday and cut into quarters. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the round gourd, cover and cook for 18 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton, ridge gourd, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, oil, salt, yogurt, green chili, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Peel the ridges of the turai and slice into rounds. Step 2: Heat oil and fry sliced onion on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Step 3: Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and fry on high heat for 10 minutes until the meat changes colour. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 8 minutes until the oil separates. Step 5: Add 2 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the mutton is almost tender. Step 6: Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook for 12 minutes until soft. Step 7: Adjust the gravy, sprinkle garam masala, green chili and fresh coriander and simmer 2 minutes. Step 8: Serve hot with roti or plain rice.

Ingredient Names: mutton, yogurt, fried onion, ginger garlic paste, green cardamom, cloves, garam masala, ghee, salt, cream, white pepper, cashews
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Blend fried onion with yogurt and the nuts. Step 3: Heat ghee with cardamom and cloves and add ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Add the mutton and fry 8 minutes. Step 5: Add the onion-yogurt paste and bhuno 8 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add water and cook covered 50 minutes until tender. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Finish with cream and kewra. Step 8: Serve with naan or sheermal. Step 9: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and taste even better the next day; reheat gently.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, apricot kernel oil, butter, dried apricots, walnuts, yogurt, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Make a stiff dough and pinch into small thumb-pressed pasta. Step 3: Boil for 8-10 minutes and drain. Step 4: Toss with butter, apricot kernel oil and crushed walnuts; serve with yogurt.

Ingredient Names: beef, basmati rice, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, biryani masala, whole spices, mint leaves, fresh coriander, saffron, oil, salt, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry thinly sliced onions in oil for 12-15 minutes until deep brown; take out half for layering. Step 3: Add ginger garlic paste and whole spices, then tomato, yogurt, chili, turmeric and biryani masala and bhuno 10 minutes. Step 4: Add the beef and fry 10 minutes, then add water and cook covered 75 minutes until tender. Step 5: Stir in coarsely crushed fennel, nigella and mustard seeds with lemon juice for the pickle flavour. Step 6: Boil the rice in salted water with whole spices for 7-8 minutes until 3/4 cooked and drain. Step 7: Layer half the rice, the masala, the rest of the rice, then mint, coriander, fried onion and saffron milk. Step 8: Cover tightly and cook on dum on very low heat for 18-20 minutes; mix gently and serve with raita and salad.

Ingredient Names: chicken, basmati rice, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, biryani masala, whole spices, mint leaves, fresh coriander, saffron, oil, salt, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry thinly sliced onions in oil for 12-15 minutes until deep brown; take out half for layering. Ingredient Names: mutton, garlic, black cardamom pod, green cardamom pods, coriander seeds, black pepper corns, cumin seeds, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, salt, oil, onions, basmati rice, water, sized carrots, raisins or sultanas, nuts, sugar
Instructions: Step 1: Add all the ingredients for the yakhni to a pot and cover with enough water to submerge all the meat. Bring to a boil and then cover, simmering for 1.5-2hrs, till the meat is tender but not falling off the bone. Keep checking after the 1.5hr mark to get till the right doneness. Step 2: Meanwhile, in a pan heat 3-4tbsp of oil and add your julienne-cut carrots. Saute these on medium heat for 5 minutes, till they are tender, and then add the raisins. Cook for an additional 5 minutes, till the raisins begin to swell up. Finally, add 2 tbsp of sugar and the lightly crushed nuts and cook for just a minute. Turn off the heat. Step 3: Take a clean sheet of aluminium foil and place the carrot mixture with all the oil onto it. Fold it around the edges tightly into a parcel shape. Set aside. Step 4: When the mutton is tender, strain out the liquid stock using a colander and discard the whole spices. Reserve the stock. Step 5: In a heavy based pot, heat 4-5 tbsp of oil and add the thinly sliced small onions. Sauté this on medium-high till the onions become lightly brown. The darker the onions become, the darker the rice will be. I prefer my Kabuli Pilau to be a light shade of brown, therefore I sauted my onions this much. You can saute them more if you prefer a darker shade. Add in the cumin seeds when your onions are just approaching your desired colour, so they get 1-2 minutes of frying. Instructions: Step 1: Take all the ingredients listed in Biryani Masala and grind them to a powder. A small taste should give you a mix that's spicy and punchy! Step 2: Marinate the chicken in the biryani masala, lemon juice, olive oil, yoghurt, and green chili paste for at least 30 minutes. Step 3: Heat 1/4 cup of oil in a large saute pan and add your ginger and garlic pastes and cook on medium high heat until they no longer smell raw - about a minute. Step 6: Add your potatoes, aloo bukharay (if using), half a cup of water, cover the pot, and bring it to a simmer, cooking for 25 minutes or so or until the chicken is tender. Check on it halfway through to see if the masala is sticking (add more water if it is), but otherwise there's no need to disturb it. Step 7: When the chicken is tender, turn up the heat to dry out any excess water, turn the stove off as soon as it starts to stick a little and the oil is above the masala. I like to add half my green masala from the layering (mint, cilantro, chilies) now along with a squeeze of lemon juice. Step 8: Rinse your basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak it for at least 30 minutes. We will start on the rice halfway through the chicken cooking time. (you can skip this step for an even quicker biryani). Step 2: Secondly, a blender add tomatoes, green chillies with a little bit of water and blend well. Step 3: Add tomato puree to the oil pot along with all the masalas and chicken and cover the lid. Let it cook at medium flame for about 20 to 25 minutes or when the oil separates from the curry. Step 4: Beat yoghurt well and add to the curry and leave at medium flame for another 10 minutes or until the gravy thickens. You can remove the lid at this point and keep stirring until you reach the desired consistency of the gravy or you can let it cook on it own. Step 5: While your chicken gravy cooks, soak rice for around 20 minutes before cooking (or as long as your brand or rice demands). Step 6: In a large pot, boil water with all the ingredients for the rice. Step 7: Add rice as water starts to boil and allow to boil for 4 to 5 minutes. Step 8: Check to see if you can break a rice grain with your hand, that’s the point where you remove your rice from the flame and strain it. Set it aside. Step 9: Add a layer of rice at the bottom of the large pot. Step 10: Sprinkle garam masala powder on the rice along with a little bit of fried onions, sliced tomatoes, green chilies and mint leaves. Step 11: Layer with chicken qorma and repeat the process. Your top layer should be that of rice. Step 12: Add all the garnishes on the top along with the food color this time. Step 13: Cover the lid well and put on the stove to steam with a frying pan or a base beneath the pot. Step 14: Keep the flame on medium to high for 5 minutes and reduce it to low medium for another 10. Finally, turn off the heat and let the Biryani rest for 5 to 10 minutes to seal the flavors before opening the lid.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, sugar, ghee, milk, saffron, cinnamon, cardamom, cashews, almonds, raisins
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the rice and soak saffron in warm milk. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Parboil the rice with cinnamon and cardamom and drain. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 4: Fry cashews, almonds and raisins in ghee. Step 5: Layer rice with ghee, sugar, saffron milk and the nuts. Step 6: Steam 20 minutes; a sweet Kashmiri wedding pulao. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 7: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 8: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, apple, pomegranate seeds, raisins, almonds, cashews, saffron, milk, whole spices, sugar, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the nuts for garnish. Step 2: Soak rice 30 minutes and boil with whole spices until 3/4 done. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 3: Fry nuts and raisins in ghee 2 minutes, and sauté apple cubes 2 minutes. Step 4: Layer rice with fruit and nuts, saffron milk and a little sugar and steam 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 5: Top with pomegranate. Step 6: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 7: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, mutton, yogurt, kashmiri chili, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom, saffron, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes and soak a pinch of saffron in warm milk. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Make goshtaba: pound boneless mutton with fat, cardamom and salt into a smooth paste and shape large balls. Step 4: Make rista: shape the same paste into slightly smaller balls. Step 5: For the white gravy, boil whisked yogurt in ghee with fennel and dried ginger powder, stirring constantly, and simmer the goshtaba in it for 40 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: For the red gravy, boil water with kashmiri chili, fennel, dried ginger and cardamom in ghee and simmer the rista in it for 40 minutes. Step 7: Boil the rice until 3/4 done, drain, drizzle saffron milk and ghee and steam for 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 8: Serve the rice with rista and goshtaba together on one large platter (trami), as at a wazwan feast. Step 9: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, lean, cumin seeds, black peppers, cinnamon stick, regular sized onions or two small, garlic paste, ginger paste, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, to matoes, garam masala powder, yogurt, green chilies, juice of, cilantro, mint, oil for cooking
Instructions: Step 1: * wash and soak your rice. Step 2: * parboil your rice in briny (gnerously salted) water and drain. Step 3: * whip your yogurt in a small bowl to make smooth and set aside. Step 4: * dice your onion & tomatoes then chop your cilantro, mint and chillies and set aside. Step 5: * heat a lug of oil in a large bottomed pan or a wok - it will make for faster cooking than a small pot. Step 6: * add the cloves, peppers, cinnamon and cumin seeds. Step 7: *when the dry spices start to sizzle and give off an aroma then add the onion and saute till translucent. Step 8: * in go the ginger and garlic paste, stir fry for a minute. Step 9: * add the salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder. saute for another minute. Step 10: * now in goes the ground beef, cook on medium high till well browned. this takes 5 minutes or so, if it starts to stick add more oil and continue to cook stirring frequently till the beef takes on a darker brown color. Step 11: * add the yogurt and diced tomatoes and cook on medium heat till the tomatoes become one with the ground beef, you may see v thin tomato 'skin' pieces and that's fine. Step 12: * now in go the garam masala powder, green chillies (start w 3-4), cilantro, mint, and lemon juice, cook for 1 minute and taste. It should be slightly salty, spicy, and tangy. If not then adjust seasoning. Step 13: Put half the rice in a large pot, then add a layer of ground beef, then top it with the remaining rice. If you want you can scatter over some green chillies and lemon pieces for their aroma. Leave the pilaf to cook on low temperature for about 20 minutes and then fix carefully so as to not break the rice.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, masoor dal, beef mince, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the rice and masoor dal together and soak 30 minutes. Step 3: Cook them with turmeric, salt and 5 cups of water for 25 minutes until soft and creamy. Step 4: For the qeema, fry chopped onion for 6 minutes, add the mince and ginger garlic paste and fry 12 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 5: Add tomato and spices and bhuno until dry, about 8 minutes. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Serve the khichdi topped with qeema, a spoon of ghee, achaar and papad. Step 7: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: beef mince, basmati rice, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, biryani masala, whole spices, mint leaves, fresh coriander, saffron, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry thinly sliced onions in oil for 12-15 minutes until deep brown; take out half for layering. Step 3: Add ginger garlic paste and whole spices, then tomato, yogurt, chili, turmeric and biryani masala and bhuno 10 minutes. Step 4: Shape spiced mince into small koftas and simmer them in the masala for 25 minutes. Step 5: Boil the rice in salted water with whole spices for 7-8 minutes until 3/4 cooked and drain. Step 6: Layer half the rice, the masala, the rest of the rice, then mint, coriander, fried onion and saffron milk. Step 7: Cover tightly and cook on dum on very low heat for 18-20 minutes; mix gently and serve with raita and salad.

Ingredient Names: beef mince, egg, basmati rice, onion, garlic, ginger, whole spices, cumin seeds, green chili, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Shape spiced mince into small koftas and cook them in the yakhni for 20 minutes. Step 3: In a heavy pot fry sliced onion in ghee for 8-10 minutes until golden, then add whole spices and cumin for 30 seconds. Step 4: Add the meat with a little of the yakhni and fry 5 minutes. Step 5: Add measured stock or water (about 1.5 cups for every cup of rice) and salt and bring to a full boil. Step 6: Add the drained rice and cook on high heat until the water dries and small holes appear on top. Step 7: Cover tightly and steam on very low heat (dum) for 15 minutes. Step 8: Fluff gently and serve with raita and kachumber salad.

Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 7: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, buttermilk, salt, cumin seeds, green chili, curry leaves, ghee
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Ingredient Names: chicken malai boti, basmati rice, yogurt, cream, green chili, white pepper, fried onion, mint leaves, whole spices, oil, salt

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, cream, serrano green chilies, cumin powder, coriander powder, all spice powder, black pepper powder, white pepper powder, salt, lemon juice, yogurt, garlic ginger paste, ghee/cooking butter or oil for grilling, basmati rice, cloves, green cardamom, black cardamom, black peppers, cinnamon stick, star anise, cumin seeds, onions, ghee or cooking butter, green chilies, red chilies
Instructions: Step 1: In a blender, add green chilies, cream, all the spices, garlic ginger paste, lemon juice and salt. Blend until the green chilies are completely blended. Step 2: In a bowl, whisk yogurt until smooth and add the chili cream. Your marination is ready. Step 3: Marinate the chicken with 1/2 of the marination sauce and reserve half for rice. Step 4: You can smoke the chicken with coal at this point if you want. Step 5: Refrigerate the chicken and let it marinate for at least 2-3 hrs or overnight. Step 6: Put the chicken cubes on skewers. Step 7: Add 1 tbsp of cooking butter or ghee in a pan and grill the skewers from all sides at medium flame to high flame. Step 8: Cover the cooked chicken and set aside. Step 9: Wash and Soak the rice for 20 minutes in water, or until needed. Step 10: In a pot or cooker, add ghee/oil. Step 11: Add all the whole spices, zeera and onions and let the onions turn golden brown at medium flame. Step 12: Turn off the flame and remove half of the onions from the pot and set aside. Step 13: Add the rice, garlic ginger paste, salt, whole red and green chilies. Step 14: Now add 3 to 4 green chilies to the Malai mixture that was left over from the chicken and blend it. Step 15: Add this malai mixture to the rice. Step 16: Add enough water to the rice so that the water level is just slightly (1/2 inch) above the rice in the pot. Step 17: Cover the lid and and cook at medium to high heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until all the water evaporates. Step 18: Once all the water evaporates but the rice is still soggy, cover the lid again and reduce the flame to low. Keep a girdle or an insulating pad below the rice and cook for another 4 to 5 mins or until the rice is done.

Ingredient Names: rice, boneless chicken, eggs, carrot, capsicum, red chili flakes, chili garlic sauce, soy sauce, garam masala, spring onion, oil, salt
