Ingredient Names: onions, garlic, freshly, full fat yogurt, lamb or mutton, bone in, bay leaf, salt, cumin, green cardamom, garam masala, black pepper, sized cinnamon stick, red chili flakes, potatoes, dried plums, white basmati rice, green cardamoms, black cardamoms, mint, coriander, lemon, tomato, star anise, kewra water
Instructions: Step 1: Halve and deep fry the potatoes until they are pretty much fully cooked, but careful not to overcook them! Set aside for late. Step 2: In a deep pot, heat the oil and add all the onions. Fry these on medium/high till they are golden brown. Remove 50% of these onions and set aside. Step 3: In the pot with the remaining onions, add the minced garlic and ginger and cook till they turn golden. Step 4: Add the lamb/mutton. Sear in the oil on high heat till it no longer remains pink. Step 5: Add all the yogurt, dried plums and the spices. Saute this on high for a few minutes, then add about 3-4 cups of water. Bring to a boil, cover and then cook for 1-1.5 hour, till the lamb/mutton becomes tender. Mutton may take up to 1hr 45 minutes to become tender, but keep checking to make sure it doesn't become too soft and starts falling off the bone. Step 6: Once the meat is tender, add in half a bunch of chopped mint, half a bunch of chopped coriander and the potatoes. Stir in and turn the heat off. Step 7: In a separate pot, bring water to a boil alongside all the whole spices and the oil. There isn't a set amount of water - just enough for the rice to cook in. Once the water is at a boil, add in the rice and boil rapidly for 5-7 minutes, till the rice is 75% cooked. Drain in a colander immediately. Step 8: In a pot, layer half your biryani curry/masala. Step 9: Then add half of your rice. Step 10: Sprinkle over 2-3 pinches of food colouring and 1/2 tsp kewara water. Step 11: Half of the reserved fried onions. Step 12: 3 slices of lemon and 3 slices of tomatoes. Step 13: 1/4 bunch of chopped mint and a 1/4 bunch chopped coriander. Step 14: Repeat that layering process again. Step 15: Now, turn the heat to the lowest possible setting, cover the Biryani and allow it to steam on low for about 15-20 minutes. Once steamed, allow it to rest for 15 minutes before serving. Step 16: Serve with raita and salad. I also like serving my Biryani with fried raisins and cashews. Enjoy and lap up the compliments!

Ingredient Names: gram flour, tamarind, onion, potato, spinach, cumin seeds, curry leaves, turmeric, basmati rice, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the leafy greens in plenty of water to remove all grit. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes; soak a lemon-size ball of tamarind in hot water. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: For the kadhi, roast 5 tablespoons gram flour in oil on low heat for 8 minutes until golden and fragrant. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Add cumin seeds and curry leaves, then slowly whisk in 5 cups of water so no lumps form; add turmeric and salt. Step 5: Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring often; add the strained tamarind water in the last 5 minutes. Step 6: For the pakoras, mix sliced onion, thin potato slices and chopped spinach with gram flour, salt and a little water and fry spoonfuls for 5 minutes until crisp. Step 7: Boil the rice in salted water for 12 minutes until done and drain. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 8: Add the pakoras to the hot kadhi just before serving and serve over the rice; a Sindhi rainy-day meal. Step 9: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: prawns, basmati rice, potato, tomato, yogurt, dried plums, green chili, biryani masala, mint leaves, fried onion, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; pick and wash the mint leaves; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Peel the prawns and soak the rice. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Make a tangy masala with tomato, yogurt, aloo bukhara, green chilies and biryani masala for 10 minutes. Step 4: Add the prawns for 3 minutes and fried potatoes. Step 5: Boil the rice until 3/4 done. Check a grain between your fingers: it should break easily but still have a firm centre. Drain immediately. Step 6: Layer with mint and fried onion and steam 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 7: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 8: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: chicken, basmati rice, onion, tomato, green chili, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, whole spices, dried plums, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry onion until golden in 10 minutes; add whole spices, chicken and ginger garlic paste and fry 8 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add tomato, yogurt and green chili and cook 8 minutes. Step 4: Add water and soaked rice with aloo bukhara; cook until dry, then dum for 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 5: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 6: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: rice, potato, onion, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin seeds, whole spices, green chili, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the rice 30 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry cumin, onion and whole spices for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add potato cubes, turmeric, red chili, green chili and salt and fry 5 minutes. Step 5: Add measured water and the rice and cook until dry. Step 6: Steam 12 minutes and serve with yogurt. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 7: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: basmati rice, soy sauce, pepper, vinegar, spaghetti or chow mein noodles, mixed vegetables - i use, ginger garlic paste, boullion cube, chicken, cayenne/chili powder, ketchup, asian style hot sauce, water, salt for adjusting seasoning, garlic thinly, green chilies, thinly, mayo, hot sauce, a handful of
Instructions: Step 1: Boil the rice, drain excess water and stir in soy, pepper, and vinegar. Step 2: Boil noodles per package directions. Step 3: While they are boiling heat 2 tbsp of oil in a pan on medium high heat and add the ginger garlic paste. Step 4: After sauteing the ginger garlic paste for 30 seconds add your vegetables and remaining seasonings (including crumbled boullion cube) and saute till tender crisp. Step 5: Add the drained noodles to the vegetable mix. Set aside. Step 6: Saute the ginger garlic in hot oil then add the sliced chicken. Step 7: Keep the heat on medium high and saute until all the chicken changes colours. Step 8: Now add the soy sauce, vinegar, pepper, chili powder, cook for another two minutes. Step 9: Stir in the ketchup, hot sauce and water, cook on low for 4-5 minutes. You want a chicken that has a light sauce so neither watery nor dry. Step 10: Taste and adjust seasoning - I usually add 1/2 tsp of salt. Step 11: Whisk all the ingredients together and set aside. Step 12: Take a large platter/rice dish then spoon out a layer of rice followed by the noodles then the chicken and a drizzle of your sauce (you'll have extra leftover). Step 13: Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a small pan and add garlic cooking on medium heat till golden. Step 14: Add your green chilies, they may sputter so be careful as you saute them for 30 seconds. Step 15: Carefully spoon your garlic chips and chilies over the dish - you don't need to pour the oil over!

Ingredient Names: mutton, basmati rice, onion, whole spices, chickpeas, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Make yakhni by boiling the mutton with an onion, whole spices and salt in 6 cups of water for 60 minutes; strain and keep the stock. Step 2: Soak the rice for 30 minutes and use boiled chickpeas. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry sliced onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the mutton and fry 3 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the chickpeas and measured yakhni and bring to a boil. Step 5: Add the rice and cook on high heat until the water dries. Step 6: Steam on low heat (dum) for 15 minutes and serve with salad. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: mixed vegetables, basmati rice, onion, tomato, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, biryani masala, whole spices, mint leaves, fresh coriander, saffron, oil, salt, carrot, green peas, green beans, potato
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry thinly sliced onions in oil for 12-15 minutes until deep brown; take out half for layering. Step 3: Add ginger garlic paste and whole spices, then tomato, yogurt, chili, turmeric and biryani masala and bhuno 10 minutes. Step 4: Add carrots, peas, beans and potatoes and cook in the masala for 12 minutes. Step 5: Boil the rice in salted water with whole spices for 7-8 minutes until 3/4 cooked and drain. Step 6: Layer half the rice, the masala, the rest of the rice, then mint, coriander, fried onion and saffron milk. Step 7: Cover tightly and cook on dum on very low heat for 18-20 minutes; mix gently and serve with raita and salad.

Ingredient Names: rice, carrot, green peas, capsicum, cabbage, spring onion, garlic, soy sauce, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; and wash the rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Use rice that was boiled earlier and cooled, so the grains stay separate. Step 3: Dice the carrot, capsicum and cabbage; shell the peas. Step 4: Stir fry garlic and the vegetables in a hot wok for 3 minutes. Step 5: Add the rice, soy sauce, black pepper and salt and toss on high heat for 3 minutes. Step 6: Finish with spring onion. Step 7: Fluff the rice gently with a fork from the sides and serve hot with raita and kachumber salad. Step 8: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Step 2: Fry thinly sliced onions in oil for 12-15 minutes until deep brown; take out half for layering. Ingredient Names: cumin seeds, basmati rice, onion, garlic, ginger, whole spices, green chili, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; peel and crush the garlic; and peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Fry 2 teaspoons of cumin seeds in ghee for 30 seconds. Step 4: In a heavy pot fry sliced onion in ghee for 8-10 minutes until golden, then add whole spices and cumin for 30 seconds. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 5: Add the prepared cumin seeds and stir gently. Step 6: Add measured stock or water (about 1.5 cups for every cup of rice) and salt and bring to a full boil. Step 7: Add the drained rice and cook on high heat until the water dries and small holes appear on top. Step 8: Cover tightly and steam on very low heat (dum) for 15 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 9: Fluff gently and serve with raita and kachumber salad. Step 10: Leftover rice keeps in the fridge for 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered.

Ingredient Names: white chickpeas, onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, lemon juice, chaat masala, fresh coriander, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil soaked chickpeas 40 minutes and cool. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Toss with chopped vegetables, lemon and chaat masala. Step 4: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: chicken, sweet corn, capsicum, cabbage, mayonnaise, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil and shred the chicken. Step 3: Mix with corn, capsicum, cabbage, mayo, pepper and salt and chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise, cream, sugar, vinegar, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Finely shred the cabbage and carrot. Step 2: Mix with mayonnaise, cream, sugar, vinegar, pepper and salt and chill 30 minutes. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 3: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: roma or vine tomato, regular cucumber or, red onion, cilantro leaves, fresh lemon or lime juice, fine sea salt, ground black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Place all the ingredients in a small serving bowl and toss to combine. Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Step 2: Serve immediately or allow the flavors to meld and juices to release before serving, about 10 minutes. Store covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

Ingredient Names: cucumber, tomato, onion, green chili, lemon juice, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Slice cucumber, tomato and onion in rounds. Step 3: Season with lemon, pepper and salt and serve with every meal.

Ingredient Names: black-eyed beans, onion, tomato, cucumber, lemon juice, olive oil, chaat masala, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil soaked lobia 30 minutes and cool. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Toss with chopped vegetables, lemon, oil and chaat masala. Step 4: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: macaroni, chicken, mayonnaise, cream, cabbage, carrot, capsicum, pineapple, black pepper, sugar, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil macaroni 8 minutes and cool. Step 3: Mix with shredded boiled chicken and chopped vegetables and pineapple. Step 4: Dress with mayonnaise, cream, pepper, a little sugar and salt and chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: white radish, carrot, green chili, lemon juice, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Grate the radish and carrot. Step 3: Mix with green chili, lemon and salt just before serving.

Ingredient Names: potato, carrot, green peas, apple, pineapple, macaroni, mayonnaise, cream, sugar, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Step 2: Boil cubed potato, carrot and peas for 10 minutes and cool. Step 3: Boil macaroni 8 minutes and cool. Step 4: Mix with apple, pineapple, mayonnaise, cream, a little sugar and salt; chill 1 hour. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 5: Toss just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

Ingredient Names: dried fish, tamarind, onion, garlic, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Soak the dried fish in water for 1 hour, then wash well. Step 2: Soak tamarind in hot water and strain. Step 3: Fry chopped onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes, add red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the tamarind water and 2 cups of water and boil. Step 5: Add the fish and simmer 20 minutes until soft and the gravy is sour and spicy. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve with rice.

Ingredient Names: mackerel, lemon juice, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, carom seeds, rice flour, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean the bangra and make deep cuts on both sides. Step 3: Rub lemon, ginger garlic paste, red chili, turmeric, carom seeds and salt into the cuts. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Rest 30 minutes. Step 5: Dust with rice flour. Step 6: Fry 5 minutes per side until crisp and serve with lemon.

Ingredient Names: mackerel, onion, tomato, tamarind, garlic, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, curry leaves, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean and cut the bangra into pieces; soak tamarind and strain. Step 3: Fry onion and garlic for 5 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook 5 minutes. Step 5: Add the tamarind water and 1 cup water and simmer 8 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Add the fish and cook 8 minutes without stirring; temper with curry leaves. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 7: Serve immediately with lemon wedges, onion rings and green chutney; seafood gets hard if it is kept on the heat.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, eggs, flour, bread crumbs, lemon juice, garlic paste, black pepper, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the fish into finger-size strips. Step 3: Marinate in lemon juice, garlic paste, black pepper and salt for 20 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 4: Coat each piece in flour, then beaten egg, then bread crumbs. Step 5: Chill 15 minutes so the coating sticks. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 6: Deep fry for 4 minutes until golden and serve with tartar or chili sauce. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, onion, ginger garlic paste, salt, oil, achaar masala, yogurt, mustard oil, nigella seeds, fennel seeds
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry onion lightly in oil 5 minutes and add ginger garlic paste. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the boneless fish and fry 3 minutes, then take it out. Step 4: Cook yogurt with achaar spices in mustard oil for 8 minutes. Step 5: Return the seafood and simmer 4 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve in the handi with naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, tomato, ginger garlic paste, yogurt, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, lemon juice, green chili, mustard oil, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the boneless fish and ginger garlic paste and fry for 4 minutes until sealed. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Remove the seafood and keep aside so it does not overcook. Step 5: Add tomatoes, yogurt and the coarsely crushed achaar spices (fennel, nigella, mustard, fenugreek) and bhuno 10 minutes; finish with lemon and stuffed green chilies. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Return the seafood and cook for 3-4 minutes only. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander, ginger julienne and green chili and serve straight from the karahi with naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, yogurt, achaar masala, mustard oil, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, lemon juice, red chili powder, salt, oil, onion, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless fish into bite-size pieces. Step 3: Marinate in yogurt, achaar masala, crushed fennel and nigella seeds, red chili, lemon and mustard oil for 1 hour. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 4: Thread on skewers. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 10 minutes, turning and basting with butter or oil, until cooked and lightly charred; or cook on a hot tawa. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Give a smoke of hot coal for 2 minutes for the BBQ aroma. Step 7: Serve with onion rings, lemon, mint chutney and naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, tomato, ginger, green chili, red chili flakes, lemon juice, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the fish into cubes, rub with salt and lightly fry for 3 minutes; keep aside. Step 3: In the same oil cook chopped tomatoes with lots of ginger julienne, chili flakes and green chili for 8 minutes until thick. Stir continuously and scrape the sides of the pan so the milk does not catch at the bottom. Step 4: Add the fish and cook 3 minutes, shaking the pan. Step 5: Finish with lemon juice and more ginger. Step 6: Serve immediately with lemon wedges, onion rings and green chutney; seafood gets hard if it is kept on the heat.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, potato, onion, green chili, fresh coriander, eggs, bread crumbs, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the fish for 5 minutes and the potatoes until soft. Step 3: Mash both together with chopped onion, green chili, coriander and salt. Step 4: Shape round cutlets. Step 5: Dip in beaten egg and coat in bread crumbs. Step 6: Shallow fry 3 minutes per side until golden and serve with ketchup.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, onion, tomato, yogurt, cream, green chili, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the fish into cubes and rub with salt. Step 3: Fry chopped onion, add ginger garlic paste, tomato, yogurt and spices and cook 10 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the fish and cook 6 minutes gently, shaking the pan rather than stirring. Step 5: Finish with cream, butter and green chili. Step 6: Serve with naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, green chili, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, fresh coriander, mint leaves, lemon juice, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; pick and wash the mint leaves; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the boneless fish and fry 3 minutes, then take it out so it does not overcook. Step 4: Add a paste of green chilies, coriander and mint with yogurt and cook 8 minutes until green and thick. Step 5: Return the seafood and cook 3 minutes only. Step 6: Garnish with coriander, ginger and green chili and serve with naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, mint leaves, fresh coriander, green chili, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, salt, oil, onion, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; pick and wash the mint leaves; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless fish into bite-size pieces. Step 3: Blend mint, coriander and green chilies with yogurt, ginger garlic paste and lemon; marinate for 1 hour. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 4: Thread on skewers. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 10 minutes, turning and basting with butter or oil, until cooked and lightly charred; or cook on a hot tawa. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Give a smoke of hot coal for 2 minutes for the BBQ aroma. Step 7: Serve with onion rings, lemon, mint chutney and naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, black pepper, green chili, cream, butter, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the boneless fish and fry 3 minutes, then take it out so it does not overcook. Step 4: Add yogurt and a full tablespoon of coarsely crushed black pepper and cook 8 minutes; finish with cream. Step 5: Return the seafood and cook 3 minutes only. Step 6: Garnish with coriander, ginger and green chili and serve with naan.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, fresh coriander, bread crumbs, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin seeds, tamarind, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the fish 5 minutes, mash with green chili, coriander, bread crumbs and salt and shape koftas. Step 3: Lightly fry the koftas for 3 minutes. Step 4: Make a thin masala with cumin, onion, tomato, spices and tamarind and simmer 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Add koftas and simmer 8 minutes; serve with rice.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, tomato, ginger garlic paste, green chili, red chili flakes, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black pepper, ghee, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil in a karahi on high heat. Step 3: Add the boneless fish and ginger garlic paste and fry for 4 minutes until sealed. Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Ingredient Names: boneless fish, lemon juice, lemon zest, black pepper, garlic, yogurt, butter, salt, oil, onion, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the boneless fish into bite-size pieces. Step 3: Marinate in lemon juice and zest, black pepper, crushed garlic and a little yogurt for 2 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 4: Thread on skewers. Step 5: Grill over hot coals for 10 minutes, turning and basting with butter or oil, until cooked and lightly charred; or cook on a hot tawa. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 6: Give a smoke of hot coal for 2 minutes for the BBQ aroma. Step 7: Serve with onion rings, lemon, mint chutney and naan.

Ingredient Names: thin firm white fish fillets, to, carom seed powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, salt, coriander powder, ginger garlic paste, oil, carom seeds, cinnamon stick, black cardamom, green cardamom, star anise, long grain basmati rice, turmeric, onions, tomatoes, chopped coriander leaves for garnish
Instructions: Step 1: Marinate fish with all the marinating spices and set aside for 30 mins to 1 hour. Step 2: Wash rice 2 to 3 times and soak for 20 mins. Step 3: In a pot, add oil, whole spices and sliced onions. Saute at medium flame till the onions turn light golden. (NOT BROWN). Step 4: Add chopped tomatoes, garlic ginger paste, salt, turmeric, coriander powder and red chili powder. Saute for 2 to 3 mins. Step 5: Add a cup of water and cover the pot. Allow the tomatoes and onion to soften up for about 10 mins. Step 6: Check to see if the tomatoes and onions have softened up to make a smooth curry base. IF not, add another cup of water and leave for another 10 mins. Turn off flame. Step 7: In the meantime, take another pan and add oil. Shallow fry fish at high flame, flipping only when one side is golden brown in color. It should take about 6 to 7 mins in total. Remove fish from oil and set aside. Step 8: Strain the leftover oil from fish and add around 1/3 cup of this oil in the curry base. Step 9: Turn on the flame for curry pot and cook the curry base for another 2 mins. Step 10: Add drained rice and water to the pot. Make sure the water level is about an inch over the rice. (check by inserting your finger in the water, the water level should touch your first joint in the finger when your fingertip touches the rice). Step 11: Add green chilies and Cover the pot. Turn the flame to high. Allow the rice to cook for about 6 to 7 mins. You can open lid and check in between to see if there is still water. Step 12: Once most of the water dries up and only a little moisture remains, reduce the flame to low and cover it again. Let the rice cook for another 6 to 7 mins. Remove the lid and fluff up the rice with a flat spatula or a fork. If your rice are done, turn off the flame. IF they still need more time to cook, splash a little water and let it sit for another 5 mins at low heat before turning off flame. Step 13: Place the pieces of fried fish on top of the rice and sprinkle chopped coriander. Cover the lid and let the rice and fish sit in the pot for about 10 mins before serving. This will allow the fish to heat up again and the rice to soak up the aroma from the fish. Step 14: Serve with raita and salad on the side. Step 15: Alternate cooking methodsYou can also make the rice in an instant pot. Step 16: You can air fry the fish, or grill it or bake it.

Ingredient Names: skinless salmon, plain whole-milk greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon or lime juice, garlic cloves, paprika or kashmiri chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, black pepper, red chili powder or cayenne, fine sea salt, minced parsley or cilantro leaves, mint coriander raita, red or yellow onions
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the salmon into 1 1/2-inch/4 cm pieces. Step 2: Place all the ingredients except the salmon in a medium bowl and whisk to combine. Add the salmon pieces and toss to coat. Marinate for at least 10 minutes, up to 1 hour. Step 3: When you’re ready to cook the salmon, preheat oven broiler to high (550°F / 289°C) for 10 minutes. Place your oven rack on the top shelf so it’s close to the heat source. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil. Step 4: Place the salmon pieces on the lined baking sheet 1” apart. Brush the excess marinade over the salmon. Step 5: Broil for 7-8 minutes, until golden brown and slightly charred on top (internal temperature 145°F). Keep an eye on the salmon because it goes from charred to burnt within seconds, and you want to make sure not to overcook. I find I need to rotate my pan midway for even browning. Step 6: Garnish with more parsley/cilantro if you’d like. Serve immediately with mint raita, sliced onions, lemon wedges, and choice of sides.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, potato, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, lemon juice, green chili, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Ingredient Names: oil, onion, garlic, tomatoes, white fish, coriander, green chili, cumin seeds, salt, ground coriander powder, chili powder, cumin powder, pepper
Instructions: Step 1: In a pot, heat the oil on medium-high, about 3 minutes. Step 2: Add in the chopped onions, minced garlic and whole cumin seeds. Allow to brown, stirring often. Step 4: Once the gravy has thickened and there isn't a lot of water left, add in the fish chunks. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. The fish will release a lot of its own water, therefore there should be no need to add any extra water. Step 5: Begin to stir the curry and break the fish chunks with your spoon. This should not take a lot of effort as the fish will have softened considerably by now. Continue breaking until the fish resembles keema (mince). Step 6: Keep cooking the curry on medium/low heat till the water evaporates. The curry is complete when there is little to no soupy water. Step 7: Serve with rice or chapattis and garnish with chopped fresh coriander and green chilli (optional).

Instructions: Step 1: Heat the oil in a pan. Add the onions and fry on a medium high heat, till the onions are translucent and are beginning to become golden. Ingredient Names: squid, onion, tomato, garlic, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, lemon, oil, salt

Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 4: Add 1.5 cups water and simmer 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Slide in the fish and simmer on low heat for 8-10 minutes without stirring; shake the pan instead. Step 6: Garnish with coriander and green chili and serve with rice.

Ingredient Names: yogurt, potato, roasted cumin, red chili powder, salt, fresh coriander, mint leaves
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash and chop the fresh coriander; pick and wash the mint leaves; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil potatoes 15 minutes and cut into small cubes. Step 3: Whisk chilled yogurt with a little water until smooth. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Mix in the prepared ingredient with salt and roasted cumin. Step 5: Sprinkle red chili and herbs and serve cold with biryani, pulao or kebabs.

Ingredient Names: yogurt, pomegranate seeds, salt, roasted cumin, black pepper, mint leaves
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk chilled yogurt with salt and a little water until smooth. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 2: Add the pomegranate seeds. Step 3: Sprinkle roasted cumin, black pepper and chopped mint and chill 15 minutes before serving with biryani or pulao.

Ingredient Names: eggplants, yogurt, salt, red chili powder, garlic, chaat masala, cumin seeds, red chilies, sprig curry leaves, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Slice the eggplant into slim rounds, about 1/2 cm. Step 2: Heat oil in a frying pan and fry on medium heat until one side turns golden (about 2 minutes), then flip and cook the other side (closer to 1 minute). Cook in batches & drain on paper towels. Step 3: Sprinkle lightly w salt (or chaat masala if you wish!) and put a layer down in the dish you are using. Step 4: Now whip the yogurt, salt, red chilli powder and garlic together with a little water. Adjust for consistency and then adjust seasoning. It should taste positively tangy. Step 5: Gently pour over your sliced eggplant. Step 6: If you did not burn your eggplant you can reuse some of that oil, it will be less pretty than 'fresh' oil but tastier. Either way put 1 1/2 tbsp of oil in a small pan and heat. Step 7: Slice the garlic into thin rounds and add to the pan along with the rest of the ingredients. Step 8: Cook the garlic so that it is golden on each side and then gently pour the baghaar/tadka on top of the raita. Step 9: TIP: If you want the baghaar to be a prettier color add a tiny bit of red chilli flakes after you take it off the heat, they will give the oil a redder color.

Ingredient Names: bathua leaves, yogurt, roasted cumin, black salt, red chili powder
Instructions: Step 1: Pick and wash the bathua leaves and chop. Step 2: Boil the bathua leaves 5 minutes, squeeze and chop fine. Step 3: Mix into whisked yogurt with roasted cumin, black salt and a pinch of red chili; chill. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 4: Serve chilled alongside biryani, pulao or kebabs.

Instructions: Step 1: Finely chop the spinach - I like to run my spinach and green chilies through a mini food processor. Step 2: Heat a pan with 2 teaspoons or so of oil, add your garlic clove and chili flakes, saute for 30 seconds. Step 3: Add your spinach/green chilies and cook for 4-5 minutes on medium high heat until the spinach wilts and the excess water evaporates. Transfer it to a bowl. Step 4: Wait 2-3 minutes for the mix to cool and then add in your yoghurt, mix it well to smooth out lumps, and then adjust consistency and seasoning. Step 5: Heat oil for the baghaar, add the curry leaves, cumin seeds, garlic, and chilies and saute on medium heat until the garlic is golden and pour over the raita. Keeps well for 3-4 days.

Instructions: Step 1: Put all the ingredients in the blender but ONLY 3 tbsp of the yogurt. Puree till smooth. Step 2: I tend to use it in two batches, but for one big batch whisk the remainder of the 1 cup yoghurt into the chutney base. Step 3: Thin it out - I like 1/4 cup water for a thicker raita, and adjust salt. The more you thin it out the more salt you may need!

Ingredient Names: chapli kebab, burger bun, onion, tomato, green chutney, yogurt, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 2: Fry a thin chapli kebab for 4 minutes each side. Step 3: Toast the bun and spread green chutney and yogurt. Step 4: Add the kebab with onion and tomato. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: potato, onion, tomato, green chili, imli chutney, chaat masala, red chili powder, roasted cumin, fresh coriander, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil potatoes 20 minutes and cube. Step 3: Toss with onion, tomato, chili, imli chutney and spices. Ingredient Names: yogurt, sugar, salt, water, cilantro, mint, cumin powder, green chilies, lemon juice, garlic clove, chickpeas, oil, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, chili flakes, chili powder, strained tamarind pulp or, chaat masala, onion, thinly, potato, minced green chilies, papri - about, tamarind chutney, dry roasted and coarsely, ajwain
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk the yogurt ingredients and set aside. If you feel the yogurt is very thick then add 1/4 cup more water. Step 2: Blitz the green chutney ingredients in a mini blender along with 2-3 tbsp of water. Adjust seasoning if needed. Step 3: Mix your dry masala (if making) and set aside. Step 4: Heat the oil in a small pan for the chickpeas on medium heat. Step 5: When the oil is hot add the mustard seeds and nigella seeds. Step 6: Add the chili flakes, give it a quick stir and add the chickpeas. Step 7: Now add the salt, chili powder, cumin powder and 1/2 cup of water and cook on low heat till the chickpeas are tender. If they start to dry up then add more water - you want the mixture to have some liquid. Step 8: When the chickpeas are tender mix in the chaat masala and imli (chutney or pulp), taste, adjust, and set aside. Step 9: Assembly: You can start with yogurt first or just layer chickpeas then potatoes then yoghurt. Follow these with your chutneys, sliced onions, papri, chaat masala and/or extra dry masala, cilantro and green chilies. Serve with extra chutneys and chaat masala on the side.

Ingredient Names: potato, gram flour, ajwain, red chili powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Slice potatoes very thin. Step 2: Dip in thin besan batter with ajwain and fry until crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 3: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: potato, gram flour, rice flour, ajwain, red chili powder, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, baking soda, green chili, fresh coriander, salt, oil, chaat masala
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Slice the potatoes very thin. Step 3: Mix gram flour, a spoon of rice flour, ajwain, chili, crushed coriander, anardana, a pinch of soda and salt with water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes. Step 4: Coat the pieces in the batter (or mix everything together for mixed pakoras). Step 5: Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 4-6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 6: Drain, sprinkle chaat masala and serve hot with imli or green chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: potato, onion, gram flour, red chili flakes, ajwain, coriander seeds, green chili, fresh coriander, baking soda, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix gram flour with crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, chili flakes, salt and a pinch of baking soda. Step 3: Add the potato and onion with green chili and coriander; add water little by little for a thick batter. Step 4: Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Drain and serve hot with imli chutney and chai on a rainy evening.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ajwain, ghee, potato, green peas, onion, green chili, cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, red chili flakes, fresh coriander, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Knead flour with ajwain, salt and ghee using cold water into a stiff dough; rest 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Cook boiled potatoes and peas with cumin, onion, chili, crushed coriander and anardana for 5 minutes; cool. Step 4: Roll ovals, cut in half, form cones, fill and seal. Step 5: Fry on low heat for 12-15 minutes until blistered and golden. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: potato, red chili powder, amchoor, chaat masala, cumin powder, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Ingredient Names: paratha, eggs, onion, green chili, ketchup, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Beat an egg with onion and chili and cook it on the tawa, press a half-cooked paratha on top. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 3: Flip and cook 1 minute, then roll with ketchup. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: burger buns, shami kebab, eggs, onion, cabbage, ketchup, mayonnaise, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Step 2: Fry the shami kebab 2 minutes per side. Step 3: Make a thin omelette and fold it over the kebab. Step 4: Toast buns with butter, add sauces, cabbage, onion and the kebab-egg; the Pakistani street burger. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, leek, green onion, beef mince, yogurt, garlic, dried mint, oil, salt, red chili flakes
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fill thin dough rounds with chopped leeks and green onion; fold into half moons. Step 3: Boil the dumplings for 8 minutes. Step 4: Spread garlic yogurt on a platter, add dumplings and top with spiced mince sauce cooked for 15 minutes and dried mint. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: eggplant, gram flour, rice flour, ajwain, red chili powder, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, baking soda, green chili, fresh coriander, salt, oil, chaat masala
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Slice the eggplant into thin rounds. Step 3: Mix gram flour, a spoon of rice flour, ajwain, chili, crushed coriander, anardana, a pinch of soda and salt with water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes. Step 4: Coat the pieces in the batter (or mix everything together for mixed pakoras). Step 5: Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 4-6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, chilled unsalted butter, chilled water, salt, boiled potato mash with a fork; this way, green peas frozen or canned, carrot, onion, garlic cloves, ghee, ginger paste, green chili, garam masala, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, black pepper, turmeric powder, oil
Instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, add the flour, salt, and chilled butter. Rub the mixture together well. Step 2: Samosa's dough shouldn't be soft, so slowly add enough chilled water to make a pliable dough. Knead the dough until combined, do not over-knead. The samosa dough should be a little stiff. Step 3: Divide the dough into 4 balls. Cover and keep aside for 20 minutes. Step 4: Heat a frying pan and add 2 tablespoons of ghee. Add the onion and fry until translucent. If you are using fresh carrots, add them with the onion. Step 5: Add the potato and cook for two minutes on medium-high heat. Add the ginger, garlic, chili, green peas, and carrot (if frozen). Cook for two minutes. Step 6: Add the spices and cook for a minute on medium-low heat. Step 7: Roll one ball out with a rolling pin into a 6-inch circle. (This dough won't need dry flour to roll). Step 8: Cut the circle in half. Take one-half and fold it into a cone. Seal along the fold. Step 9: Place this cone between your thumb and index finger. Fill the cone with the stuffing. Step 10: Wet along the edges of the dough with water and pinch to seal. It is best to place the filled samosas in the fridge for 10 minutes before baking. Step 11: Brush or spray the samosas with oil and bake in a preheated oven, 350F/180C, for 20 minutes. Or place in an air fryer for 15 to 17 minutes at 350F. Until golden in color.

Ingredient Names: paratha, beef bihari boti, mint chutney, mayonnaise, onion
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Step 2: Grill the bihari boti strips on coals 10 minutes. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 3: Roll in a paratha with chutney, mayo and onion. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: boneless beef, pita bread, yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, black pepper, cumin powder, cabbage, cucumber, garlic sauce, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; wash the beef and cut it into even pieces so it cooks at the same pace; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Marinate thin beef strips in yogurt, garlic, lemon and spices 3 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Cook on a hot pan 8 minutes until browned. Step 4: Wrap in pita with cabbage, cucumber and garlic sauce. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: lotus stem, gram flour, rice flour, red chili powder, ajwain, chaat masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Slice lotus stem thin and soak 10 minutes. Step 2: Dip in thick gram and rice flour batter with spices. Step 3: Fry 4 minutes until crisp and sprinkle chaat masala. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: corn on the cob, lemon, salt, red chili powder
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Roast the corn on coals for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred. Step 3: Rub with lemon dipped in salt and chili; the classic rainy-day street snack. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: eggs, onion, tomato, green chili, chaat masala, lemon juice, fresh coriander, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Boil eggs 10 minutes, peel and cut in quarters. Put the boiled eggs in cold water straight away so they peel easily. Step 2: Toss with chopped onion, tomato, green chili, coriander, chaat masala and lemon. Step 3: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: bread slices, potato, gram flour, rice flour, ajwain, red chili powder, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, baking soda, green chili, fresh coriander, salt, oil, chaat masala
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Sandwich spiced mashed potato between bread slices and cut into triangles. Step 4: Coat the pieces in the batter (or mix everything together for mixed pakoras). Step 5: Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 4-6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 6: Drain, sprinkle chaat masala and serve hot with imli or green chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: chana dal, beef mince, potato, egg, onion, green chili, fresh coriander, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, cumin seeds, burger buns, ketchup, green chutney, cucumber, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and pick through the dal for small stones and wash it 2-3 times. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chana dal and mince with spices and ginger garlic for 30 minutes until dry; grind. Step 3: Mix with boiled mashed potato, green chili and coriander and shape into patties. Step 4: Dip patties in beaten egg and shallow fry 3 minutes each side. Step 5: Toast buns on a tawa with butter, spread chutney and ketchup, add the shami, onion and cucumber. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 6: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: burger buns, aloo tikki, eggs, onion, ketchup, green chutney, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Step 2: Fry aloo tikki, top with a fried egg. Step 3: Put in a toasted bun with onion, ketchup and chutney. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: white chickpeas, onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, imli chutney, chaat masala, lemon juice, fresh coriander, salt

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, lemon juice, ginger garlic paste, gram flour, rice flour, ajwain, red chili powder, crushed coriander seeds, anardana, baking soda, green chili, fresh coriander, salt, oil, chaat masala
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut chicken into strips and marinate in lemon, ginger garlic and salt for 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Mix gram flour, a spoon of rice flour, ajwain, chili, crushed coriander, anardana, a pinch of soda and salt with water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes. Step 4: Coat the pieces in the batter (or mix everything together for mixed pakoras). Step 5: Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 4-6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 6: Drain, sprinkle chaat masala and serve hot with imli or green chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: boneless, skinless, chicken breast, water, kosher salt, ground black pepper, garlic clove, unsalted butter, avocado oil, cumin seeds, yellow onion, to large serrano pepper and, all-purpose flour, milk, heavy whipping cream, cilantro, packages puff pastry, egg, water or milk
Instructions: Step 1: Boil chicken: Place the chicken, measured water, 3/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and garlic clove in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, and allow to boil, uncovered, until the chicken is cooked through and the water completely evaporates (~25 min). If the water evaporates too quickly, add a little water until it cooks through. If the chicken cooks and starts shedding while water remains, increase the heat to evaporate remaining water. Turn off the heat. Step 2: Shred: Transfer the chicken with any leftover juices to an electric mixer bowl with a paddle attachment. Turn the mixer ON to low-medium speed (4). Mix until the chicken is shredded and no large chunks remain (~1-2 min). Alternatively, finely shred on a cutting board using 2 forks. Step 3: Make filling: Wipe the saucepan clean and place it back over medium heat. Add the butter and oil. Once the butter melts, add the cumin seeds (if using), onion, and green chili pepper. Sauté until translucent (~6 min), taking care not to brown the onion. Season with the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Step 4: Finish filling: Add flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute to remove the floury taste. Pour in the milk and heavy whipping cream and bring to a gentle simmer (~1-2 min). Once it starts to thicken, turn off the heat and add the shredded chicken. Stir to combine. Mix in cilantro, if using. Taste and add more pepper, if you'd like. (Be generous with the seasoning because it will mellow out within the pastries.) Cover and allow to completely cool. You can place in the fridge to speed up chilling. Step 5: Prep oven: Preheat oven to 375°F/190°C and place 2 oven racks toward the center of the oven. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Step 6: Make egg wash: In a small bowl, whisk egg with water/milk. Step 7: Prep pastry sheets: Unfold and lay 1 box of pastry sheets flat on a parchment-lined surface or directly on your baking sheet (keep the other box refrigerated). Use a pastry brush to brush the top of the sheets with the egg wash. Use a sharp knife or pizza cutter to gently cut (try not to slide the knife down) the pastry sheets into approximately 3.25" X 3.25" squares. Step 8: Add filling: Use a cookie scoop to add about 1 tbsp of the chicken to each square. Then close the pastry by folding one edge of the square over to the opposite edge, distributing the chicken toward the edges as needed. Seal the edges by indenting with a fork. Brush the top of each pastry with a light coat of egg wash. Repeat with remaining pastries. Step 9: Bake: Place both baking sheets toward the center of your oven (keep space between them). Bake for 30 minutes, or until the pastries on the top sheet are golden brown and flaky. Remove the top tray from the oven and shift the bottom tray to the top rack until it's also golden and flaky (~3-5 min). Serve warm (preferable) or at room temperature.

Instructions: Step 1: Mix everything together from the chicken marination list and marinate the chicken in it for about 20 mins. Instructions: Step 1: Slice kalari (Kashmiri milk cheese). Step 2: Fry in butter on a pan for 2 minutes each side until golden and stretchy. Step 3: Sprinkle chili and salt and eat with bread. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: white chickpeas, potato, papdi, onion, tomato, yogurt, imli chutney, green chutney, chaat masala, red chili powder, fresh coriander, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; wash and chop the fresh coriander; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Step 4: Top with crushed papdi, yogurt, both chutneys and coriander. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: urad dal, moong dal, yogurt, sugar, salt, roasted cumin, red chili powder, chaat masala, imli chutney, oil, baking soda
Instructions: Step 1: Soak both dals for 4 hours and grind into a fluffy batter; beat 5 minutes. Step 2: Fry spoonfuls for 5-6 minutes until golden and soak in warm salted water for 20 minutes; squeeze. Step 3: Whisk yogurt with sugar and salt; arrange baray and cover with yogurt. Step 4: Top with imli chutney, chaat masala, cumin and chili. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: chicken boneless, yogurt, ginger garlic paste, tikka masala, lemon juice, paratha, onion, mint chutney, garlic mayonnaise, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Marinate chicken strips in yogurt, ginger garlic, tikka masala and lemon for 2 hours. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge; a longer marination makes the meat softer and more flavourful. Step 3: Cook on a hot tawa for 10 minutes until charred. Keep the tawa on medium heat; if it is too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks. Step 4: Fry parathas on the tawa until crisp. Step 5: Fill with chicken, onion, mint chutney and garlic mayo and roll tightly in paper. Step 6: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, ghee, moong dal, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, red chili powder, asafoetida, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Soak and coarsely grind moong dal; fry with spices for 8 minutes until dry. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 2: Knead flour with ghee into a crumbly dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Stuff, flatten and fry on very low heat for 12 minutes until flaky. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: cucumber slices, gram flour, red chili flakes, ajwain, coriander seeds, green chili, fresh coriander, baking soda, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Mix gram flour with crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, chili flakes, salt and a pinch of baking soda. Step 3: Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 4: Drain and serve hot with imli chutney and chai on a rainy evening.

Ingredient Names: pakistani/indian okra, chaat masala, oil
Instructions: Step 1: - Heat oil in a wide bottomed pan or wok, you want a generous lug for stir frying. Ingredient Names: bun, eggs, onion, green chili, cabbage, ketchup, mayonnaise, butter, salt

Ingredient Names: black-eyed beans, onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, chaat masala, lemon juice, imli chutney, salt

Ingredient Names: paratha, chicken malai boti, mint chutney, mayonnaise, onion, lemon

Ingredient Names: onion, russet potato, serrano pepper or thai green chili pepper, cilantro leaves, mint leaves, neutral oil, lemon juice, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, crushed red chili flakes, table salt, baking soda, scant, water, neutral oil such as grapeseed or avocado, carom seeds, dried fenugreek leaves, red chili powder, simple green chutney
Instructions: Step 1: Combine all the ingredients up until the chickpea flour in a bowl. Step 2: In another bowl, add the chickpea flour and 2/3 cup water and stir to combine so that no large lumps remain (small lumps are okay). Add additional water if needed to have a pourable consistency. Pour this mixture into the vegetables and mix well. Step 3: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add enough oil to thinly coat the bottom of the pan. Step 4: Add the pakora mixture a heaped tablespoon at a time, making sure not to overcrowd the pan (I do 4 at a time). Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side, adding oil as needed. Repeat until all pakoras are cooked. Step 5: Place on a plate topped with paper towels to absorb excess oil. Serve with green chutney (recipe in the notes) and/or ketchup. Step 6: To prepare the simple green chutney, add all ingredients in a spice/coffee grinder or blender and blend until smooth. Add water as needed to thin it out. Put the mixture in a bowl and whisk with yogurt, if desired.

Ingredient Names: samosa patti, boneless chicken, onion, green chili, black pepper, garam masala, fresh coriander, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chicken with salt and pepper and shred. Step 3: Mix with onion, green chili, coriander and garam masala. Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly.
