Ingredient Names: ground beef, onion, potato, green peas, salt, turmeric powder, coriander powder, chili powder, ginger powder, garam masala powder, oil, all-purpose flour, cumin seeds, melted butter, warm water
Instructions: Step 1: In a pan, add the ground beef and saute for few minutes or until it releases oil. Step 2: Add the onion and potatoes, and stir until the onion is translucent. Add all the spices and salt, and saute some more on medium-high heat. Step 3: Reduce the heat and cook until the onion turns light brown, the beef is cooked, and the potatoes are tender. Step 4: Add the green peas and cook for another three minutes. Keep aside to cool. Step 5: NOTE: No oil was added to the filling since the beef had enough fat to cook everything with. If you are using ground beef with less fat add two tablespoon oil when sauting the beef. Step 6: In a bowl, add all the ingredients (except water) and mix by rubbing the ingredients together with your hands. Step 7: Gradually add the water and knead until you get a smooth and not sticky dough. The dough should have a little firmness to it. Step 8: Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes. Step 9: Make six equal balls from the dough. Take one ball and roll it out with the rolling pin into a medium thickness circle around 6 inches. (This dough won’t need dry flour to roll). Step 10: Use a knife to cut the circle in half. Step 11: Take one half and fold it into a cone. Seal along the fold by pressing it between your fingers. Step 12: Place this cone between your thumb and index finger. Fill the cone with the filling. It might take two tablespoons or a little less. Do not overfill. Step 13: Wet the open edges of the cone with water and pinch the sides together to seal. Now you should have a triangle shaped samosa. Repeat this step with the rest of the dough and filling. Step 14: Cover the samosa with a cloth and keep it aside for 20 minutes. preferable in the fridge if your kitchen is hot. Step 15: In a medium frying pan, heat the oil. Add the samosas but do not crowd the pan. Fry on medium heat until the samosa is golden brown from all sides. The frying time may take from 7 to 8 minutes.

Ingredient Names: flour, onion, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, red chili powder, amchoor, ghee, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make a spicy onion filling with fennel, coriander, chili and amchoor. Step 3: Stuff into a ghee-rich dough and fry slowly 10 minutes until flaky. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: beef mince, potato, onion, green chili, fresh coriander, garam masala, eggs, bread crumbs, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil mince with spices until dry and mash with boiled potatoes, onion, chili and coriander. Step 3: Shape cutlets, dip in egg and bread crumbs. Step 4: Shallow fry 3 minutes per side. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: cooked beef mince, gram flour, red chili flakes, ajwain, coriander seeds, green chili, fresh coriander, baking soda, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix gram flour with crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, chili flakes, salt and a pinch of baking soda. Step 3: Add the cooked beef mince with green chili and coriander; add water little by little for a thick batter. Step 4: Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Drain and serve hot with imli chutney and chai on a rainy evening.

Ingredient Names: puff pastry, beef mince, onion, green peas, garam masala, green chili, eggs, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook mince with peas and spices for 20 minutes until dry. Step 3: Fill pastry squares, seal and egg wash. Step 4: Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: puff pastry, beef mince, onion, green chili, garam masala, eggs, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and keep the mince in a colander to drain any water. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook mince with onion and spices for 20 minutes until dry; cool. Step 3: Wrap in puff pastry strips, brush with egg. Step 4: Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: lean, onions, garlic, inches ginger, salt, coriander powder, cumin powder, chili powder, yogurt, garam masala, chopped cilantro, chopped mint, chopped green onions, green chilies, samosa strips, flour, water
Instructions: Step 1: Heat 3-4 tbsp of oil in a wok or saute pan on medium heat. Step 2: Add onions, ginger, garlic and saute until just softened. Step 3: Add ground meat, 1 tsp salt, cumin, and coriander powders and turn the heat up to medium high or high and aggressively break down the meat into smaller pieces. Step 4: When the meat is cooked through turn the stove off, add yoghurt if needed, and then add 1 tsp of garam masala. Step 5: Stir in everything in the spicy herb mix group, it will seem like a lot but it cooks down. Step 6: Taste, adjust seasoning (chicken keema may need 1 more tsp garam masala) and leave to cool. You can also store this in the fridge for two days. Step 7: Combine the flour and water to form a slurry that will be the glue for your samosa. Step 8: Two approaches:Form a cone as shown in the pictures in the blog post and then place 1.5 tbsp of meat mixture in the samosa and seal the samosa. Place the meat mix on the samosa strips and keep folding triangles until only a little is left. Seal with the slurry. In both approaches keep an eye on your 'corners' to make sure they are nice and tight. Step 9: Air Fry: Spray both sides with oil and air fry at 390F for 12-14 minutes, flipping halfway through. Step 10: Pan Fry: Heat an even film of oil up to half an inch high in a pan on medium high. Once the oil is hot fry for 2-3 minutes per side or until golden. You will have some darker spots and that's okay. Just remember not to over crowd your pan. Step 11: Deep Fry: Heat a generous amount of oil in a wok and once the oil is sizzling hot add your samosas and fry until golden. Step 12: Remember to drain on a wired rack!

Ingredient Names: white chickpeas, potato, onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, fresh coriander, imli chutney, yogurt, chaat masala, roasted cumin, red chili powder, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil soaked chickpeas for 40 minutes and potatoes for 20 minutes; cube the potatoes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Mix chickpeas, potatoes, onion, tomato, cucumber and green chili. Step 4: Add chaat masala, cumin, chili and salt. Step 5: Top with yogurt, imli chutney and coriander and serve immediately.

Ingredient Names: samosa, white chickpeas, onion, yogurt, imli chutney, green chutney, chaat masala, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Crush hot samosas on a plate. Step 3: Top with chickpea curry, onion, yogurt, chutneys and chaat masala. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: paratha, beef seekh kebab, onion, mint chutney, imli chutney, lemon, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Step 2: Grill seekh kebabs 10 minutes. Turn the skewers every 2-3 minutes so they cook evenly and do not burn on one side. Step 3: Roll in a paratha with onion and chutneys. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: sweet potato, lemon juice, chaat masala, black salt, red chili powder
Instructions: Step 1: Roast sweet potatoes in hot sand or coals for 30 minutes (or boil 20 minutes). Step 2: Peel and slice, then sprinkle lemon, chaat masala and black salt; a winter street snack. Step 3: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: capsicum rings, gram flour, red chili flakes, ajwain, coriander seeds, green chili, fresh coriander, baking soda, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix gram flour with crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, chili flakes, salt and a pinch of baking soda. Step 3: Add the capsicum rings with green chili and coriander; add water little by little for a thick batter. Step 4: Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Drain and serve hot with imli chutney and chai on a rainy evening.

Ingredient Names: potato, onion, imli chutney, green chutney, yogurt, chaat masala, red chili powder, fresh coriander, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; wash and chop the fresh coriander; peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Make double-fried aloo tuk: half-boil, slice, fry, press and fry again for 8 minutes total. Step 3: Top with onion, yogurt, both chutneys, chaat masala and coriander. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: flattened rice, peanuts, curry leaves, green chili, turmeric, sugar, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Fry the flattened rice in batches for 30 seconds until puffed. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 3: Fry peanuts, curry leaves and green chili. Step 4: Mix with turmeric, a little sugar and salt. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: taro root, tamarind, red chili powder, chaat masala, roasted cumin, salt, lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil arvi for 15 minutes, peel and slice. Step 3: Toss with tamarind water, chili, chaat masala, cumin and lemon. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: masoor dal, onion, green chili, ginger, fresh coriander, cumin seeds, rice flour, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak dal 2 hours and grind coarsely. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Mix with onion, green chili, ginger, coriander, cumin and rice flour. Step 4: Shape small tikkis and shallow fry for 3 minutes each side. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: all-purpose flour, onion, potato, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, red chili powder, amchoor, ghee, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook onion, potato and spices for 10 minutes into a dry filling. Step 3: Stuff into a ghee-rich dough and flatten. Step 4: Fry on low heat for 12 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: semolina batter, gram flour, red chili flakes, ajwain, coriander seeds, green chili, fresh coriander, baking soda, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Mix gram flour with crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, chili flakes, salt and a pinch of baking soda. Step 3: Add the semolina batter with green chili and coriander; add water little by little for a thick batter. Step 4: Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Drain and serve hot with imli chutney and chai on a rainy evening.

Ingredient Names: boneless chicken, salt, kashmiri red chili powder, salt or, coriander powder, turmeric powder, roasted and grounded cumin seeds, black pepper powder, garam masala powder, garlic ginger paste, bread, yogurt, vinegar, lemon juice, egg, panko bread crumbs, all purpose flour, oil
Instructions: Step 1: In a food processor add bread and pulse to form crumbs. Step 2: If you are using boneless chicken, add the chicken and spices and yogurt directly in the food processor and grind until you get a smooth mix. Step 3: If you are using chicken mince, add bread crumbs and mince in a bowl, along with spices and yogurt and mix well by hand. Step 4: Grease a butter paper with oil and place on a tray. Step 5: Dump the chicken mince on the tray. Step 6: Grease your hand with oil and spread out the chicken mix around the tray to form an even layer. Keep the layer as thick as you want. Step 7: Pop the tray in the freezer for an hour or 2 or until the mixture becomes rock solid. Step 8: Take the tray out and cut the mix into square pieces. Step 9: Coat all the nuggets in all purpose flour. Step 10: Make a mixture of egg, salt and 1/2 cup of water. Dip the nuggets in this egg wash and then coat with bread crumbs evenly. Step 11: Deep fry in hot oil at medium flame and serve with lemon and a dip of your choice. Step 12: You can also bake them at 200 °C for 20 mins in a greased tray. Step 13: Put the remaining nuggets back on a tray and pop it back in the freezer. Step 14: When they harden up, transfer into a zip-lock bag and freeze for future use.

Ingredient Names: potato, carrot, green peas, onion, green chili, bread crumbs, eggs, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil and mash vegetables with spices. Step 3: Shape, coat and fry 3 minutes per side. Step 4: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: noodles, oil, garlic, carrots, bell pepper, green chili, cabbage, spring onions, soy sauce, sriracha sauce, oyster sauce, salt, red chili flakes, brown sugar, crushed black pepper, chicken powder, egg roll wrappers/spring roll sheets, all-purpose flour
Instructions: Step 1: In a pan heat some oil and saute the minced garlic. Step 2: On high heat, fry the carrot and bell pepper. Don't cook for more than 2 mins. You don't want to lose the crunch. Step 3: Add the cabbage. Saute for a minute. Then toss in the green chilies and the noodles. Step 4: Then put in all your spices and sauces, keeping the heat on high. Toss around well. Step 5: Now add the spring onions and continue to stir. Dry any moisture and turn off heat. Put this filling in a bowl and let cool. Step 6: Make a thick paste with flour and water. This will be used to seal the spring rolls. Step 7: Take a sheet of spring roll. Put it in a shape of a diamond on your working surface. At one end add around 2 tbsp of the filling. Roll the corner over the filling, fold the two sides and roll tightly all the way up. Brush some flour paste on the edges to seal off. Step 8: Repeat for the rest of the filling. Keep all the spring rolls aside. Step 9: At this stage, you can freeze them in a single layer and when frozen transfer to a ziplock bag. Step 10: These spring rolls can be deep fried, shallow fried, air fried and even baked. I shallow fried them here. See air frying and baking instructions in the notes. Step 11: For frying, heat oil in your pot. Then fry these rolls on medium heat till golden on all sides. Step 12: Take out on a paper towel to drain excess oil. Step 13: Serve with your favourite chutney and.

Ingredient Names: samosa patti, potato, green peas, onion, green chili, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, chaat masala, fresh coriander, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook cubed boiled potatoes and peas with cumin, crushed coriander, chili and chaat masala for 5 minutes. Step 3: Fill samosa patti in triangles and seal. Step 4: Fry on medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: spring roll sheets, cabbage, carrot, capsicum, boneless chicken, soy sauce, black pepper, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: cut the boneless chicken into even bite-size cubes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Stir fry chicken 4 minutes, add shredded vegetables and soy and toss 2 minutes; cool. Step 3: Roll tightly in sheets and seal. Step 4: Deep fry 5 minutes until golden. The oil should be medium-hot: a drop of batter should rise to the top in 2-3 seconds. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot, and drain on kitchen paper. Step 5: Serve hot with green chutney, imli chutney and a cup of chai.

Ingredient Names: wheat flour, yak meat, onion, potato, turnip, salt, black pepper, butter
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; and peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the meat with onion and salt in 6 cups of water for 60 minutes until tender. Step 3: Knead wheat flour into a stiff dough and roll and cut thick noodles by hand. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 4: Add cubed potato and turnip to the broth and cook 20 minutes. Step 5: Add the noodles and boil 10 minutes until cooked. Step 6: Finish with black pepper and a knob of butter; a warming Baltistani noodle soup. Step 7: Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of lemon and a little black pepper. Step 8: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: mutton, wheat, kashk, onion, dried mint, garlic, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Step 2: Soak the wheat overnight. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Cook the mutton and wheat with plenty of water and salt on low heat for 3 hours until very soft. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Remove bones and beat with a wooden masher until smooth and stretchy. Step 5: Dissolve the kashk in a little warm water. Step 6: Fry sliced onion and garlic in oil until golden and add dried mint. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 7: Serve the haleem topped with the kashk and the fried onion mixture. Step 8: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: beef bones, beef, onion, garlic, ginger, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, black pepper, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the beef and cut it into even pieces so it cooks at the same pace. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the bones and meat. Step 3: Put them in a pot with onion, garlic, ginger and a muslin bag of fennel and coriander seeds. Step 4: Cover with 10 cups of water and simmer 2.5 hours, skimming the foam. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Strain, season with black pepper and salt. Step 6: Drink hot in winter or use as stock for pulao. Step 7: Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of lemon and a little black pepper. Step 8: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: kurut, bread, onion, garlic, dried mint, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Soak the dry kurut (sun-dried yogurt balls) in hot water for 1 hour and rub into a smooth sour sauce. Step 2: Fry sliced onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the kurut sauce and salt and simmer 5 minutes, stirring. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Tear dry bread into a deep plate. Step 5: Pour the hot kurut over the bread and top with dried mint and the fried onion oil. Step 6: Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of lemon and a little black pepper. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: chicken, sweet corn, eggs, cornflour, chicken stock, white pepper, soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chicken in stock for 20 minutes and shred. Step 3: Add creamed corn and simmer 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Thicken with cornflour slurry for 2 minutes and slowly pour in beaten egg while stirring. Step 5: Serve with soy, vinegar with green chili, and chili sauce; a winter street favourite. Step 6: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: chicken, carrot, cabbage, green peas, garlic, ginger, black pepper, cornflour, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the chicken with garlic, ginger and salt in 6 cups of water for 30 minutes; shred the chicken and keep the stock. Step 3: Chop the carrot and cabbage finely. Step 4: Add the vegetables and peas to the stock and cook 8 minutes. Step 5: Add the shredded chicken and thicken lightly with cornflour slurry. Step 6: Season with black pepper and serve hot. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: chicken bones, onion, garlic, ginger, black pepper, whole spices, salt, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the chicken bones well. Step 3: Put them in a pot with an onion, garlic, ginger, whole spices, salt and 8 cups of water. Step 4: Bring to a boil, remove the foam, and simmer on low heat for 60 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Strain the yakhni through a fine sieve. Step 6: Season with black pepper and lemon and serve hot in mugs, especially in winter or when someone is unwell. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: boneless fish, garlic, ginger, tomato, black pepper, lemon juice, cornflour, fresh coriander, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the fish gently, pat it dry with kitchen paper and keep it cold; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the fish bones with garlic and ginger for 20 minutes and strain. Step 3: Add fish cubes and chopped tomato and simmer 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Thicken lightly with cornflour slurry. Step 5: Season with black pepper, salt and lemon. Step 6: Garnish with coriander. Step 7: Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of lemon and a little black pepper. Step 8: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: chicken, cabbage, carrot, capsicum, eggs, cornflour, soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, white pepper, chicken stock, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the chicken pieces and drain them well. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil chicken in stock 20 minutes and shred. Step 3: Add thin vegetables and cook 3 minutes. Step 4: Add soy, vinegar, chili sauce and pepper and thicken with cornflour. Step 5: Swirl in beaten egg and serve hot. Step 6: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: dried apricots, wheat flour, apricot oil, salt, water
Instructions: Step 1: Soak dried apricots overnight; remove the stones. Step 2: Boil the apricots in their soaking water with more water for 20 minutes until soft and mash. Step 3: Mix a spoon of wheat flour with water and stir it in; cook 5 minutes until slightly thick. Step 4: Add salt and a few drops of apricot oil and serve warm. Step 5: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: wheat noodles, chicken stock, potato, carrot, spinach, egg, salt, black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the leafy greens in plenty of water to remove all grit. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut potato, carrot and spinach. Step 3: Boil the potato and carrot in chicken stock for 15 minutes. Step 4: Add hand-cut wheat noodles and spinach and cook 8 minutes. Step 5: Swirl in a beaten egg and stir gently. Step 6: Season with salt and black pepper and serve hot. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: chicken, coconut milk, gram flour, egg noodles, onion, ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder, lemon, fried garlic, fried onion, fresh coriander, green chili, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; wash and chop the fresh coriander; wash the chicken pieces and drain them well; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cook chicken in oil with onion and ginger garlic for 10 minutes. Step 3: Add turmeric, chili, cumin and water and simmer 20 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Whisk gram flour into coconut milk, add and simmer 15 minutes into a smooth curry. Step 5: Boil noodles 5 minutes and serve curry over them with fried garlic, onion, lemon and coriander. Step 6: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: mutton, onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, black pepper, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the mutton pieces and drain them in a colander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Heat oil and fry a sliced onion for 6 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 3: Add the mutton, crushed garlic and ginger and fry 10 minutes. Step 4: Add chopped tomato, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder and salt and cook 5 minutes. Step 5: Add 8 cups of water and simmer covered for 60 minutes into a thin, spicy shorba. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Add black pepper, garnish with coriander and serve hot with naan. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: mutton bones, onion, garlic, ginger, whole spices, salt, black pepper, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and cut a lemon into wedges for serving. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the mutton bones well. Step 3: Put them in a large pot with an onion, garlic, ginger, whole spices, salt and 10 cups of water. Step 4: Bring to a boil and remove the foam that rises for the first 10 minutes. Step 5: Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until the stock is rich. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Strain, season with black pepper and lemon and drink hot in winter or when unwell. Step 7: Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of lemon and a little black pepper. Step 8: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: noodles, kidney beans, chickpeas, beef mince, tomato, onion, yogurt, dried mint, garlic, red chili flakes, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic; keep the mince in a colander to drain any water; and whisk the yogurt until smooth so it does not split in the heat. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil soaked beans and chickpeas for 50 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Cook mince with onion and tomato for 15 minutes. Step 4: Add noodles to the beans with water and boil 8 minutes. Step 5: Serve topped with garlic yogurt, the mince and dried mint. Step 6: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: goat trotters, onion, garlic, ginger, black pepper, salt, lemon
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; peel and crush the garlic; and peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Clean the trotters well, singe off any hair, and blanch in boiling water for 10 minutes; discard the water. Step 3: Put them in a pot with onion, garlic, ginger, salt and 10 cups of water. Step 4: Simmer on very low heat for 4 hours until the broth is sticky and rich. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Season with black pepper. Step 6: Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: mutton mince, flour, onion, garlic, black pepper, mutton stock, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Knead flour with water into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 2: Mix the mutton mince with chopped onion, garlic, black pepper and salt. Step 3: Roll the dough thin, cut small squares, fill with the mince and pinch closed into small dumplings. Step 4: Bring the mutton stock to a boil with onion, garlic and pepper. Step 5: Drop in the dumplings and simmer 15 minutes until cooked. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Serve hot in bowls. Step 7: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Instructions: Step 1: Chop the carrot and cabbage finely. Step 2: Boil the corn and vegetables in stock for 10 minutes. Step 3: Thicken with cornflour slurry and season with pepper and salt. Step 4: Drizzle beaten egg while stirring slowly to make ribbons. Step 5: Serve with soy sauce, vinegar and chili sauce on the side. Step 6: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

Ingredient Names: tomato, onion, garlic, black pepper, cumin seeds, butter, cream, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Roughly chop the tomatoes, onion and garlic. Step 2: Cook them in butter for 10 minutes until soft. Step 3: Blend until smooth and strain for a silky soup. Step 4: Return to the pot with 2 cups water, black pepper, roasted cumin and salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Swirl in cream and serve hot. Ingredient Names: salt, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, onion - roughly, diced potatoes, ginger garlic paste, tomato, chopped cilantro, diced green chilies, a squeeze of lemon juice
Instructions: Step 1: Combine all the ingredients in a small bowl and set aside. Step 2: Heat 1/4 cup of oil in a saucepan with a lid. Step 5: Now add in the achari masala ingredients and saute till aromatic. Step 6: Mix in the chopped potatoes and tomato, make sure you mix well. Step 7: Cover and cook on low flame for 20 minutes, add a splash of water if the mix starts to stick. Step 8: After 20 minutes check for doneness, if the potatoes are tender you can adjust consistency by adding water or drying it up (your preference). Step 9: Add a squeeze of lemon juice then taste and adjust seasoning. Step 10: Serve topped with cilantro and chilies.

Ingredient Names: eggplant, mustard oil, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, onion, tomato, yogurt, red chili powder, turmeric, salt, lemon juice, green chili
Instructions: Step 1: Cut the eggplant into cubes and keep in salted water so it does not darken. Step 3: Add chopped onion and fry 5 minutes, then tomato, red chili, turmeric and salt and bhuno 5 minutes. Step 5: Stir in whisked yogurt and lemon juice and cook 3 minutes until the masala is tangy and dry. Step 6: Add slit green chilies and serve with paratha. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: coriander seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chili peppers, raw peanuts, desiccated coconut/unsweetened shredded coconut, sesame seeds, white poppy seeds – or sub, tomato sauce can or purée, baby eggplant, yellow onion, garlic cloves, crushed ginger, neutral oil, or, mild kashmiri red chili, turmeric powder, kosher salt, serrano peppers, tamarind concentrate paste, sugar, finely chopped cilantro
Instructions: Step 1: Heat a small, preferably nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the whole spices (coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dried whole chilis). Toast, stirring and shaking the skillet often, for 1 minute and 20 seconds, just until aromatic and slightly darkened. You don’t want them to darken too much, which can make them bitter. Transfer to a plate and let cool. Step 2: In the same pan, add peanuts and toast until lightly golden, about 2 minutes. Add in the desiccated coconut, sesame seeds, and poppy seeds (or cashews), and continue to toast for another 2 minutes, until the poppy seeds crackle, and the coconut goes from white to golden brown and smells aromatic. Again, you don’t want it too dark, it may get bitter. Remove from heat. Step 3: Prep the eggplant: Slit each eggplant lengthwise in crisscross manner almost up to the stem, so the eggplant can remain intact once it's cooked. Step 4: Make the Onion Paste: Place the onion, garlic, and ginger in a nutribullet or small blender. Pour in 1 tbsp water, just enough to help it blend to a smooth paste. If you need more water, add up to 2 tbsp more water. Remove from the blender and set aside. Step 5: Make the Masala Paste: In the same blender, add the toasted spices, nut/seed mixture, tomato sauce, and 1/4 water. Blend for 1-2 minutes to make a smooth, uniform paste. (If you have trouble blending, add 1/4 cup more water.) It should be as smooth and non-grainy as possible. Step 6: Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and curry leaves (careful! - they sizzle and sputter) and allow them to sputter for 5-10 seconds. Do not allow curry leaves to darken. Step 7: Add the onion paste and fry, stirring frequently, for 3 minutes, until translucent and beginning to turn lightly golden. Add eggplants and increase heat to medium-high. Fry, stirring frequently, for 6-7 minutes, until the skin of the eggplant changes color, going from bright purple to brown. During this time, the onions will also deepen in color, eventually turning golden brown. Step 8: Add the blended tomato masala paste, along with the ground spices (Kashmiri chili, red chili powder, and turmeric) and salt. Fry, stirring gently, for 3-4 minutes to cook down the masala and bloom the spices. Pour with 1 cup water (I like to blend the water with any remains of blended paste in my blender). Step 9: Allow to come to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook the eggplant, covered, for 26-30 minutes, stirring gently halfway through. (Size of the eggplant will determine cook time). The eggplant should be very tender, but still intact. (You don’t want them completely mushed, but you want them to absorb the flavor as much as possible). The oil should have risen to the top. Step 10: Add the serrano pepper(s), tamarind, and sugar and mix gently. Step 11: Taste and adjust, adding more tamarind for tanginess or sugar for sweetness. If you’d like it more saucy, add 1/4-1/2 cup more (preferably boiling) water. Step 12: Cover and cook and simmer for 2-3 minutes until the oil rises to the top once again. Turn off heat and garnish with cilantro. Serve with roti, paratha, or naan.

Toss to coat the okra in the oil. Add the coriander powder, fennel seeds, and salt. Step 4: Continue cooking, stirring often, for 12 minutes, until there’s no more slime left. The okra should be shriveled, deep green, and well-charred. Step 5: Reduce the heat to low, add the dry mango powder, and mix gently for another minute. Turn off the heat. Serve hot with roti, paratha, or other bread. See post for more serving ideas!

Ingredient Names: yogurt, gram flour, okra, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin seeds, mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried red chilies, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Whisk yogurt with gram flour, turmeric, red chili powder and salt until smooth, then add 4 cups of water. Step 2: Bring to a boil, stirring continuously so it does not split, and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Meanwhile fry the cut okra in oil for 8 minutes until crisp. Step 4: Add the okra to the kadhi and cook 5 minutes. Step 5: Heat oil, add cumin, mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried red chilies, and pour the sizzling tarka over. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 6: Serve with plain rice. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: okra, onion, tomato, garlic, green chili, cumin seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, oil, salt, fresh coriander, amchoor
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and fully dry the okra, then cut into pieces and fry in a little oil for 8 minutes so it is not slimy. Step 2: Heat oil, add cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then sliced onion and chopped garlic and fry for 5 minutes until light golden. Step 3: Add tomato, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 4-5 minutes until oil separates. Step 4: Add the okra, mix well, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then; add a splash of water only if it sticks. Step 5: Uncover and cook on medium heat for 3 more minutes to dry the masala. Step 6: Sprinkle amchoor for a light sour taste. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with roti or paratha.

Ingredient Names: chana dal, onion, green chili, ginger, garam masala, fresh coriander, eggs, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak chana dal 1 hour. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Boil it with ginger, garam masala and salt until all water dries, then grind. Step 4: Mix with chopped onion, green chili and coriander and shape kebabs. Step 5: Dip in beaten egg and shallow fry 3 minutes per side. Step 6: Taste and adjust salt, garnish with fresh coriander and serve with chapati or paratha. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: white chickpeas, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin seeds, garam masala, anardana powder, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Soak the chickpeas overnight and boil for 45 minutes until soft. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 3: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds and fry chopped onion for 8 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add ginger garlic paste, tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook 12 minutes. Cook the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, just until its raw smell disappears. Step 5: Add the chickpeas with some of their water and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few to thicken. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Finish with garam masala and anardana powder for a tangy taste. Step 7: Serve with naan, puri or rice. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: cumin seeds, minced onions, garlic, grated ginger, salt, chili powder, turmeric, cumin powder, bouillon/ stock cube, canned chickpeas, chopped washed spinach, freshly cracked black pepper
Instructions: Step 1: Heat a lug of oil in a saucepan and when it starts to shimmer add the cumin seeds, they will crackle and smell delicious. Step 2: Add the minced onion and cook just until the edges are golden brown. Step 3: Now stir in the ginger and garlic and saute for a minute. Step 4: Add in the remaining spices and saute for another minute. Step 5: Now drain the can of chickpeas and add to the pot along with about 1.5 cup of hot water and your half a stock cube. Step 6: Bring to a boil and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the chickpeas reach desired tenderness. Step 7: Take off the stovetop and stir in the spinach, it will wilt instantly. Step 8: Top with your cilantro. Step 9: For greater heat remove kid sized portions and add some minced green chillies to the chickpeas or simply top with the chillies after plating. Step 10: Goes well with rice and flatbreads.

Ingredient Names: black chickpeas, tamarind, onion, tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, amchoor, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Soak black chickpeas overnight and boil 45 minutes. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 2: Soak tamarind and strain the pulp. Step 3: Fry chopped onion, add tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook 8 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add the chickpeas, tamarind water and 1 cup water and simmer 15 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 5: Finish with amchoor and serve with rice. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: amaranth leaves, spinach, maize flour, green chili, garlic, ginger, onion, ghee, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: slice the onions thinly; slit the green chilies; peel and crush the garlic; peel the ginger and chop or grate it finely; and wash the leafy greens in plenty of water to remove all grit. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the chaulai leaves and chop with the tender stems. Step 3: Boil the amaranth leaves (chaulai) with a little spinach, green chili, ginger and salt for 22 minutes. Step 4: Mash or blend coarsely and cook with 2 tablespoons maize flour for 10 minutes, stirring. Step 5: Temper with garlic and onion fried in ghee and serve with makki ki roti. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: beetroot, onion, tomato, garlic, green chili, cumin seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Peel the beetroot and cut into small cubes. Step 3: Heat oil, add cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then sliced onion and chopped garlic and fry for 5 minutes until light golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add tomato, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 4-5 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Add the beetroot, mix well, cover and cook on low heat for 25 minutes, stirring now and then; add a splash of water only if it sticks. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 6: Uncover and cook on medium heat for 3 more minutes to dry the masala. Step 7: Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with roti or paratha. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: chana dal, potato, onion, green chili, ginger, fresh coriander, mint leaves, garam masala, salt, oil
Instructions: Step 1: Put the chana dal, soaked chana dal, onion, ginger, garlic, dried red chilies, whole spices and salt in a pot with 3 cups water. Soaking makes it cook faster and more evenly, so do not skip it. Step 2: Cook covered for 45-60 minutes until the meat and dal are completely soft, then dry off any water on high heat for 5 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 3: Cool and grind into a smooth dough. Step 4: Mix in chopped mint, green chili, coriander and an egg (or potato for the vegetable version). Step 5: Shape into round flat kebabs, dip in beaten egg and shallow fry for 2-3 minutes each side. Step 6: Serve with green chutney or in a bun kebab; they freeze well for Ramadan. Cover it so it does not absorb fridge smells. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: cumin seeds, coriander seeds, round dried red chilies
Instructions: Step 1: FOR KACCHA MASALA (RAW 3 SPICE MIX). Step 2: Simply put everything in a food processor to get a coarse spice mix. Save in an airtight jar. Step 3: You can use this spice mix for marination and curries etc. Step 4: FOR DAHI BARA MASALA (ROASTED 3 SPICE MIX). Step 5: In a pan, add all the ingredients and roast them at low heat. Stir the contents of the pans occasionally to make sure all the seeds get evenly heated for about 6 to 7 mins. Step 6: When the color of the coriander seeds change from mustard to a golden brown color, turn off the heat and allow the spices to cool down. Step 7: Once cooled, use a food processor to grind the spices into a coarse spice mix. Preserve in an airtight jar. Step 8: This is a roasted spice version so it can also be used for directly sprinkling on top of food and is most commonly used with dahi bareys.

Ingredient Names: baby potatoes, yogurt, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin seeds, garam masala, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Boil the baby potatoes for 10 minutes, peel and prick with a fork. Step 3: Fry them in oil for 5 minutes until golden. Step 4: In the same oil crackle cumin, fry chopped onion for 6 minutes, then add ginger garlic paste. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 5: Add tomato, whisked yogurt and spices and cook 10 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 6: Add the potatoes and half a cup of water, cover tightly and cook on dum for 15 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 7: Sprinkle garam masala and serve with puri or naan. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: okra, onion, tomato, yogurt, fennel seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, amchoor, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Wash and dry the okra completely; trim the ends and make a slit in each, keeping them whole. Step 2: Fry the okra in oil for 8 minutes until it is no longer slimy; remove. Step 3: In the same oil fry chopped onion for 6 minutes, add tomato and cook 4 minutes. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add whisked yogurt, crushed fennel, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook 8 minutes, stirring. Step 5: Add the okra and amchoor, cover tightly and cook on dum on the lowest heat for 10 minutes. Seal the lid tightly (put a cloth or foil under it) and place the pot on a tawa over the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn. Step 6: Serve with roti. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: grapeseed or other neutral oil, onions, garlic cloves, ginger, cumin seeds, tomato, salt, coriander powder, black pepper powder, red chili powder, green zucchini squash, green chili pepper, turmeric powder, chopped cilantro
Instructions: Step 1: Heat oil in a nonstick or heavy bottomed skillet over high heat. Add the onions, and sauté until they are lightly golden (~8-10 minutes). Step 2: Lower the heat to medium and add the garlic, ginger and cumin seeds. Sauté until the raw smell of the ginger and garlic disappears (~1 min). Add the tomato, salt, coriander powder, black pepper powder, and red chili powder. Sauté for a minute, then stir in the zucchini and 1/4 cup of water. Mix well, ensuring that the zucchini is well coated. Step 3: Cover and let cook on medium heat for 7-10 minutes, stirring once in between. Once most of the water has dried up, use a wooden spoon to break the zucchini into pieces. Add the sliced green chili pepper and turmeric and sauté for a few minutes. Step 4: Lower the heat to the lowest setting, cover and continue to cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring half-way. If you’re afraid it will stick to the pan, add a splash of water. Uncover and stir well. If needed, raise the heat to high to sauté any extra moisture for 3-5 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Step 5: When the water has completely dried up and the zucchini is very well cooked, turn off the heat and garnish with cilantro, if desired. It is typically eaten with roti or naan but you can serve it with any type of bread or rice.

Ingredient Names: cauliflower, onion, tomato, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin seeds, garam masala, green chili, oil, salt, fresh coriander
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: chop the tomatoes; slit the green chilies; and wash and chop the fresh coriander. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Cut the cauliflower into florets and soak in salted water for 10 minutes. Step 3: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds for 30 seconds and fry chopped onion for 7-8 minutes until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 4: Add ginger garlic paste, then tomato, red chili, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and bhuno for 6 minutes until oil separates. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom; add a tablespoon of water whenever the masala sticks. It is ready when the oil shines at the edges and the raw smell of the spices is gone. Step 5: Add the cauliflower and fry in the masala for 3 minutes. Step 6: Pour in 2 cups of water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until soft and the gravy thickens. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 7: Add green chili, garam masala and fresh coriander and serve with roti or boiled rice. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: green beans, coconut oil, neutral vegetable oil, mustard seeds, nigella seeds, crushed ginger, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, sliced green chilies
Instructions: Step 1: Heat the oils in a large pan/wok on medium high heat. Step 2: Add the seeds and let them sizzle. Step 3: Now add the crushed ginger, give it a quick stir and add the green beans. Step 4: Add in about a teaspoon of salt, your 1/2 tsp of chili powder and the 1/4 tsp of turmeric and stir to combine. Step 5: Let cook uncovered without stirring for 4-5 minutes, the beans will start to char. Step 6: Move them around cook for another 4-5 minutes and test for doneness and seasoning. Step 7: Add your sliced green chilies, mix, cook for a minute more and serve.

Ingredient Names: spring onion, potato, cumin seeds, green chili, red chili powder, turmeric, oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel the potatoes and keep them in water so they do not turn brown. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Chop the spring onions with their green tops. Step 3: Fry cumin and potato cubes 10 minutes until almost cooked. Step 4: Add spices and the spring onion and cook 6 minutes. Step 5: Serve with chapati. Step 6: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: mustard greens, maize flour, garlic, green chili, ghee, butter, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: peel and crush the garlic. Measure out the spices so you can add them quickly. Step 2: Wash the mustard greens well and chop. Step 3: Boil them with garlic, green chili and salt in a little water on low heat for 60 minutes. Check once or twice and stir gently so nothing catches at the bottom; add a little hot (not cold) water if it dries out before it is done. Step 4: Mash with a wooden masher into a coarse paste. Step 5: Sprinkle in 2 tablespoons maize flour and cook 15 minutes, stirring often. Step 6: Temper with garlic in ghee and pour over. Pour the hot tarka over immediately so it sizzles, and cover for a minute to trap the aroma. Step 7: Serve with makai ki roti and a large piece of white butter. Step 8: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Ingredient Names: spinach, potato, noodles, onion, garlic, apricot oil, salt
Instructions: Step 1: Before you start, get everything ready: wash the leafy greens in plenty of water to remove all grit. Step 2: Knead a stiff wheat dough, roll thin and cut into short noodles; cube the potatoes and chop the spinach. The dough should be soft but not sticky; cover it with a damp cloth while it rests so it does not dry out. Step 3: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, then add the noodles and spinach and cook 7 minutes more. Step 4: Drain most of the water and mash lightly. Step 5: Fry sliced onion and garlic until golden. Stir every minute so the onion colours evenly; golden brown gives sweetness, but burnt onion makes the whole dish bitter. Step 6: Mix the onion and garlic in, drizzle apricot oil and serve warm. Step 7: Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1-2 days.

Instructions: Step 1: Scrape and slice the karela, rub with salt and rest 30 minutes, then squeeze out the bitter water and fry for 8 minutes. Ingredient Names: paneer, milk, turmeric, fennel seeds, dried ginger, cardamom, mustard oil, salt

Ingredient Names: ker berries, sangri beans, yogurt, dried red chili, cumin seeds, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, amchoor, oil, salt

Ingredient Names: lasoora, onion, tomato, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, fennel seeds, oil, salt

Ingredient Names: bottle gourd, salt, chopped garlic, turmeric powder, red chili powder, crushed red chili, onion, tomatoes, oil, cumin seeds, to, chopped coriander for garnish
Instructions: Step 1: Preparing the bottle gourd. Step 2: Peel the skin of your bottle gourd with a peeler. Cut the long bottle gourd into 4 smaller segments. Step 3: Keep a bowl of water on the side and put the segments in the water. Step 4: Take out one segment of the bottle gourd and cut it into 4 wedges (length wise). Now the fleshy center of the gourd will be visible to you. Step 5: Check for seeds of the gourd, if they are very big, slice the central part of the gourd with all the seeds. Small seeds can stay. Step 6: Now thinly slice the gourd wedges into triangular chips. You can do this manually with a knife. You can also use a mandoline or a food processor with the slicer attachment to do this step. Keep putting all the sliced chips in water to prevent them from turning brown. Step 7: Cooking the gourd. Step 8: Add oil in a wok or a pot along with sliced onions, chopped garlic and cumin seeds at medium flame. Step 9: Saute the onions till they turn translucent. Step 10: Add turmeric, crushed red chili and red chili powder. Saute for another 2 mins at low medium flame. Step 11: Add in chopped tomatoes and mix. Step 12: Drain water from the gourd and add it to the pot. Stir everything together so that all the sliced gourd gets coated with all the spices. Cover the pot and let it cook at medium flame. Step 13: Allow the gourd to cook for 20 to 25 mins or till the all the water from the vegetable evaporates. Step 14: Once you see oil separating on the side, reduce the flame to low. Add salt and mix well. Add green chilies and chopped coriander. Cover the pot again and let it simmer for another 4 mins at low flame. Step 15: Turn off the flame and serve with rice and lentils.

Ingredient Names: t salt, a scant, ghee, saffron threads, ground cardamom, warm milk to use
Instructions: Step 1: Combine all the ingredients except the milk in a large bowl with clean hands. The saffron you can snip into smaller pieces and scatter over. Step 2: Knead just until it all comes together to form a cohesive ball - the dough will not and should not be perfectly smooth, just hold together well and it will be on the harder side. If you cannot achieve this without the milk then add 1/2 tbsp of the milk and knead one more time. Do not add too much milk. Step 3: Set the dough aside and let it rest for at least two hours. Overnight is fine as well. In an hour or two you should see that the dough has taken off a little bit of a sheen. If it hasn't then add a half tbsp of ghee and knead it in. Step 4: When you are ready to cook heat ghee on a low flame in a wide pot (at least 8 inches). Heating ghee to the right temperature is key. A small ball of dough put into the ghee should sink to the bottom and instantly start slowly sizzling, gradually rising up and frying golden not brown. If it isn't rising the ghee is not hot enough, if it is darkening fast then add more ghee to bring down the temperature. Step 5: Roll out the dough for the tikiyaan on a lightly floured surface (flour more if the dough is too sticky to handle) and roll out to about 1/8 of an inch or sugar cookie thickness. The tikiyaan will puff up a little when cooked. Use your cutter of choice - I used the top of a babyfood jar but you can use any thing clean and round and cut out the tikiyaan. Step 6: Fry just one first to make sure it is frying correctly, cook till the center looks slightly golden and the edges a little more so - about 2.5 minutes on one side and 2 on the other. If you overcook them they will be ok the day off, but considerably crunchier the next day. The tiki will have a craggier surface on on side and that is totally fine. Step 7: If you are happy with the outcome then fry 5 at a time, adding ghee as needed to the pot. Be careful when you flip them, gentle is the way to go. Do remember that as the ghee level draws down the tikiyaan will brown faster, add ghee as needed. Step 8: Tikiyaan keep well for weeks in a tightly sealed container. Step 9: My 2-inch cutter yielded about 26-28 mini tikiyaan with this amount of dough.

Ingredient Names: cinnamon sticks, black pepper, cumin seeds, onions - roughly, garlic paste, ginger paste, salt, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder
Instructions: Step 1: Slice or dice your onions. Use a food processor or a mandolin if you have one handy. Step 2: Heat a generous amount of oil in your IP on saute mode. Step 3: When it is hot add the whole spices and saute for 30 seconds. Step 4: Add the onions, keep stirring and cook for about 10 minutes until the edges/tips of most of the onions are slightly golden. For a darker curry base keep cooking (and stirring) for 15-20 minutes - usually it is safer to go for a light golden. Step 5: Now add your ginger and garlic pastes and saute for 2 minutes. Step 6: Once they pastes are incorporated add the remaining dry masala and salt and saute until the mix starts to come together and form a cohesive paste. If it starts to burn add a small splash of water. When it is done the oil will rise to the top. Step 7: Pour 2.5 cups of hot water into the Instant Pot, give it a stir and put it on manual (pressure) for 20 minutes. Step 8: Let it naturally release and saute to reduce the liquid for a more concentrated base. If you want you can use an immersion blender to puree it at this point. Step 9: When it is cool enough to handle then drain the extra oil out of the masala. Step 10: This mix will keep in the coldest part of your fridge for 10 days or you can freeze it into roughly one cup servings for 3 months.
